tasks.title: Playback clock: play/pause/speed/loop; scrub bar with event ticks
tasks.validation: scrub to apex tick lands at v_y=0 state
tasks.notes: The blocking gap was that integrate() only ever root-localized *terminal* event crossings (ground-impact) -- non-terminal ones (apex) were detected but explicitly never localized/collected, per its own doc comments deferring that to 'a future EventCollector sink'. Implemented that sink: added Sink.event(root: EventRoot) to solverkit's types.ts, extended integrate()'s event-handling block to root-localize every candidate (not just terminal ones) and dispatch non-terminal roots to sinks -- but only those localized at-or-before the step's own earliest terminal crossing (a non-terminal crossing localized *after* a same-step terminal one never actually occurs). Added EventCollector (event-collector.ts, freeze-on-finish like TrajectoryRecorder). Wired into runtime: ResultStoreState.events is now EventRoot[] (was always [] via EventCandidate placeholder); SimulationSession.commitScenario attaches an EventCollector and publishes its events. Added the playback clock itself to SimulationSession (playback-store.ts's state existed since P3.02 but nothing advanced it): play()/pause()/scrubTo(t)/scrubToEvent(root), an injectable AnimationFrameScheduler-driven per-frame tick advancing playbackTime by dt*speed, looping (wraps modulo duration) or stopping+pausing at the trajectory's end, and play() restarting from 0 if already at the end and not looping. Added packages/viz/src/scrub-bar.ts: pure timeToFraction/fractionToTime, computeEventTicks (events -> sorted normalized tick positions), and snapToNearestEventTick for freehand drag/click to resolve onto a tick's exact time. Validation criterion is met by construction, not tolerance: scrubToEvent(apexRoot) sets playbackTime = apexRoot.t exactly, and apexRoot.y is the same root-localized state where v_y is ~0 by definition of the apex event (g(t,y)=v_y) -- verified in simulation-session.test.ts and integrate-events.test.ts (|v_y| < 1e-6 / 1e-9). No visual scrub-bar widget wired into app.tsx yet -- consistent with every other Phase-3 rendering task so far (P3.05-P3.12: camera, axes, trajectory layer, decimation, caching, projectile marker), which are all built and unit-tested as isolated modules with app-level wiring deferred; scrub-bar.ts is ready for that pass. pnpm typecheck/lint/lint:deps/test (534 tests)/build/bundle-size all green.

tasks.title: Force glyphs (F_g, F_d, F_M, resultant) log-scaled with legend
tasks.validation: glyph directions verified against rhs on 3 presets
tasks.notes: Model never exposes the individual ForceModels closed over its rhs (P1.17's registry is private), so per-force vectors can't be read off Model alone -- added `forces: readonly ForceModel[]` to runtime's ResolvedModel/resolveModel (scenario-resolver.ts), the live instances a caller already resolved from spec.model.forceIds, additive and non-breaking (also sets up P3.22's Forces panel magnitude badges to reuse it instead of re-deriving). Added packages/viz/src/force-glyphs.ts: computeForceGlyphs(model, forces, t, y, ctx, scratch) calls model.rhs once (refreshes ctx exactly as a real solve step would, and leaves ctx.forceAccum holding the exact resultant rhs itself divided by mass into out[VX]/out[VY]), then calls each ForceModel.accumulate against that same freshened ctx for its individual vector -- one source of truth between glyphs and physics, not a parallel reimplementation. logScaleGlyphLength/forceGlyphLegendTicks log-scale magnitude to an on-screen length (0 magnitude, e.g. no-spin Magnus, maps to 0 length -- nothing drawn -- vs. a floor length for a merely-tiny nonzero force). drawForceGlyphLayer + worldForceDirectionToScreen are the thin canvas-consumer half, following the AxesLayer split (pure compute + thin draw). Validation criterion met on 3 presets exercising all three force kinds (shot put: quadratic drag; golf drive: quadratic drag + Magnus; dust grain: linear drag): gravity is exactly (0, -mg); drag is antiparallel to v_rel (normalized cross ~0, dot ~-1); Magnus (golf drive) is perpendicular to v_rel (normalized dot ~0); the per-force sum equals the resultant, which divided by mass equals model.rhs's own acceleration output -- all to 1e-10, in force-glyphs.test.ts. No visual widget wired into app.tsx yet, consistent with every other Phase-3 rendering task so far (P3.05-P3.13), which stay isolated+unit-tested until a later app-wiring pass. pnpm typecheck/lint/lint:deps/test (547 tests)/build/bundle-size all green.

tasks.title: Share-URL: deflate+base64url spec in fragment; load on boot
tasks.validation: URL round-trip reproduces trajectory hash
tasks.notes: Added packages/runtime/src/scenario-share-url.ts (§6.3 point 7's "copy-URL (spec compressed into fragment via base64url of deflated JSON)" -- the separate concern from P3.31's save/load): encodeScenarioToShareFragment/decodeScenarioFromShareFragment do JSON.stringify -> CompressionStream("deflate") -> base64url (RFC 4648 §5, no +/=/ characters, safe unescaped in a fragment), and buildShareUrl/parseShareUrl wrap that into/out of a URL's #s=<encoded> fragment (parseShareUrl returns null rather than throwing on a missing/corrupt fragment, so §6.3's "load on boot" can fall back to a default scenario). Decode goes through migrateScenarioSpec (not a raw schema parse), so a link shared from an older schema version still loads, matching scenario-persistence.ts's precedent. packages/runtime/tsconfig.json's lib is ES2022-only (no DOM, per simulation-session.ts's existing defaultFrameScheduler/now() precedent for keeping L2 environment-agnostic) but CompressionStream/DecompressionStream/TextEncoder/TextDecoder/URL/URLSearchParams/btoa/atob are genuinely available in every environment this runs in (confirmed under Node 22; every evergreen browser) -- the gap is purely TypeScript's static types, which live only in the DOM lib bundle. Rather than add DOM to this package's lib (would pull in window/document) or an ambient global .d.ts (risks leaking into other packages' compilations via project references), used one local structural cast (`globalThis as unknown as WebCodecGlobals`) giving the rest of the module real types with zero cross-project risk -- verified by a full `pnpm typecheck` across every package, and a real `pnpm --filter @ballista/app build` (which does have DOM lib) exercising the actual browser CompressionStream types with no conflict. scenario-share-url.test.ts (10 tests) covers this task's literal validation criterion directly: a scenario built into a share URL and parsed back out resolves (via scenario-resolver.ts's resolveModel/resolveStepper/resolveSolverConfig) and integrates to a trajectory whose SHA-256 hash (mirroring solverkit/determinism.test.ts's own hashTrajectory convention) is bit-identical to the original's, for every preset scenario, not just one; plus fragment round-trip bit-equality, URL-safety, actual size reduction vs. raw JSON, corrupt-fragment/missing-fragment null-fallback, and future-schema-version rejection at the decode level. No app-level UI wiring yet (a share/copy-link button, or reading window.location.href on boot) -- consistent with every other Phase 3 module's precedent (P3.30's Plotly pane, P3.31's persistence) of shipping isolated-and-unit-tested first. pnpm typecheck/lint/lint:deps/test (782 tests, 125 files)/build/check-bundle-size all green.

tasks.title: prefers-reduced-motion: disable auto-play/animation
tasks.validation: media query honored (emulated test)
tasks.notes: The only continuous per-frame animation loop in the codebase is SimulationSession.play()'s requestAnimationFrame-driven playback tick (simulation-session.ts) -- surveyed viz's streamline/field/annotation layers and found no other wall-clock-driven animation (the streamline overlay is an explicitly 'display-only' static RK2 trace frozen at one instant, per its own module doc, not something that animates over time); no play/pause UI component is wired into the app yet (app.tsx's control dock is still a P3.02+ placeholder, same as every other panel task this phase), so runtime is the correct and only layer this task touches. Added a ReducedMotionQuery injectable option (mirrors the existing FrameScheduler/AnimationFrameScheduler injection pattern already used for deterministic testing) defaulting to a real `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` probe, guarded the same way the rAF probes already are since @ballista/runtime has no 'dom' lib dependency. play() now checks it first: when reduced motion is preferred, it jumps playback.playbackTime straight to the trajectory's end (mirroring how CSS transitions skip straight to their end state under the same preference) and never calls animationFrameScheduler, so the continuous tick loop never starts; playback.playing stays false throughout. Added 4 tests to simulation-session.test.ts: reduced-motion play() schedules zero animation frames and lands on the end time (this task's literal validation criterion, emulated via an injected query returning true); the non-reduced-motion default path is unchanged (existing behavior regression guard); a harmless no-trajectory no-op case; and a real-matchMedia integration test (temporarily stubs globalThis.matchMedia, asserts it's queried with the exact media-query string and that reduced motion is honored end-to-end through the default query path, not just the injected override). pnpm typecheck/lint/lint:deps/test (822 tests, 129 files, +4 from this task)/build/check-bundle-size all green (20.7 kB gz).

tasks.title: Colorblind-safe palette + viridis-only colormaps enforced
tasks.validation: palette contrast checks pass
tasks.notes: Found the two categorical (hue-coded, must-be-pairwise-distinguishable) palettes in the codebase: compare-store.ts's COMPARE_PALETTE (8-hue pinned-trajectory colors, P3.25) and force-glyphs.ts's DEFAULT_FORCE_GLYPH_COLORS (P3.14). Added packages/runtime/src/colorblind-safety.ts: simulates protanopia/deuteranopia/tritanopia via the Vienot-Brettel-Mollon (1999) linear-matrix approximation (as commonly implemented by web accessibility tooling, applied directly to gamma-encoded sRGB), converts to CIELAB (full sRGB->linear->XYZ->Lab per the standard D65 formulas), and measures CIE76 dE between every color pair under normal vision + all 3 CVD kinds; checkPaletteColorblindSafety(colors, minDeltaE=6) flags any pair below threshold. Placed in runtime (L2), not viz (L3) or analysis (L1, currently an empty stub reserved for statistical/UQ math per its own package intent), since viz already depends on runtime (allowed direction) and runtime itself needed it for COMPARE_PALETTE -- this lets both consumers reuse one implementation without a layering violation. Numerically verified the ORIGINAL ad hoc COMPARE_PALETTE was not colorblind-safe (overall min dE76 ~3.06 between its orange/red pair under simulated tritanopia, ~4.23 between aqua/violet under deuteranopia -- both far below any reasonable distinguishability threshold) -- this was a real, previously-unvalidated accessibility bug, not just a missing check. Replaced it with Okabe & Ito's (2008) peer-reviewed 'Color Universal Design' 8-color palette (min dE76 7.29, under simulated tritanopia between bluish-green/blue), the field-standard reference for exactly this problem, rather than hand-tuning arbitrary hex values; the minDeltaE=6 default threshold was chosen specifically to sit in the commonly-cited 'perceptible at a glance' dE76 band (~2-10) while remaining satisfiable by Okabe-Ito's worst-case pair. DEFAULT_FORCE_GLYPH_COLORS already passed with margin (min dE76 12.03) and was left unchanged (drag-linear/drag-quadratic intentionally share one color since a model only ever wires one drag law at a time and the two never render together -- deduped before checking so that legitimate self-pair isn't flagged as confusable). Added packages/runtime/src/colormap.ts: viridis(t), a 9-anchor linear-interpolated matplotlib-viridis LUT, documented as the platform's one permitted scalar-to-color mapping per SS6.1's hard 'viridis family only, no rainbow' style rule (no scalar-channel trajectory coloring feature exists yet to consume it -- this establishes the canonical implementation ahead of that future task rather than leaving 'enforced' as an unenforceable aspiration). 'Enforced' is a real automated check, not just a doc comment: colormap.test.ts (runtime) and colormap-enforcement.test.ts (viz) each fs-scan their own package's src/ for a second function/const whose name matches /colormap/i outside colormap.ts, failing if one appears (a future rainbow scale would need to either extend viridis.ts or get caught here) -- kept as two package-local scans rather than one cross-package scan since a runtime test reaching into viz's directory would itself blur the L2/L3 layering the check exists to protect. Added colorblind-safety.test.ts (runtime, validates COMPARE_PALETTE -- this task's literal 'palette contrast checks pass' criterion) and colorblind-safety.test.ts (viz, validates DEFAULT_FORCE_GLYPH_COLORS the same way, importing checkPaletteColorblindSafety from @ballista/runtime). Sanity-checked the simulator itself is discriminating using a color pair engineered onto the protanopia matrix's near-null direction (its 2x2 R/G submatrix has determinant ~0.008) rather than naive pure red/green, which turned out to be a poor sanity pair -- pure red and pure green differ so much in raw luminance that they stay clearly separated (dE76 ~35-48) even under this simplified CVD simulation; real dichromat confusion is a hue-axis effect at matched lightness, and only a lightness-matched pair actually demonstrates the simulator collapsing distinguishability under one specific CVD kind (correctly flagged under protanopia, correctly NOT flagged under deuteranopia -- a different confusion line -- or normal vision). pnpm typecheck/lint/lint:deps/test (837 tests, 133 files, +13 from this task)/build/check-bundle-size all green (20.7 kB gz; unchanged from before this task since nothing in app.tsx imports these modules yet -- consistent with every other panel/module this phase shipping isolated-and-unit-tested ahead of app wiring). Noted separately, not caused by this task: packages/viz/src/trajectory-decimation.test.ts's P3.10 performance assertion (<1ms for a 50k-point decimation) is flaky on this sandbox's CPU -- reproduced identically on a clean pre-P3.36 checkout, unrelated to any file this task touched.

tasks.title: Units display toggle (SI/imperial) at boundary only
tasks.validation: internal state unchanged (hash) when toggling
tasks.notes: uiStore.unitsDisplay (P3.36-era ui-store.ts) already held the SI/imperial preference; this task adds the actual boundary conversion so it does something. Added packages/ui/src/units-display-logic.ts: a pure SI-unit-string -> {displayUnit, toDisplay, toSI} lookup (m<->ft, m/s<->mph, kg<->lb -- the three physical quantities with schema fields in this app; every other unit -- deg, rad/s, kg/m^3, Pa, K -- has no imperial equivalent in scope and passes through unconverted in both modes) plus toDisplayValue/toSIValue/displayUnitFor wrapping it. Added kgToLb/lbToKg to engine/units.ts (m<->ft and m/s<->mph conversions already existed) with a round-trip test alongside the existing deg/rad and m/ft one. NumericControlRow takes an optional unitsDisplay prop (default 'SI'): it converts descriptor.value/min/max/step/unit to display units purely for rendering and for the clamp/nudge math (numeric-control-logic.ts's clampToRange/nudgeValue stay unit-agnostic, now just operating in 'display space'), then converts the committed value back to SI in commit() before calling onChange -- descriptor itself (the caller's SI source of truth) is only ever read. Every conversion is a pure scale factor (no Kelvin-style additive offset), which is what makes reusing toDisplayValue on a range's step (a delta, not a position) valid. Threaded the same optional prop through LaunchPanel/ProjectilePanel/EnvironmentPanel (the three panels with m/m/s/kg fields) down to their NumericControlRow calls; SolverPanel's only field (h, seconds) has no imperial equivalent so was left unchanged rather than adding a dead prop. This task's literal 'internal state unchanged (hash) when toggling' criterion is exercised directly in numeric-control-row.test.tsx: rendering the same descriptor at unitsDisplay SI -> imperial -> SI in sequence never calls onChange and never mutates the descriptor object (asserted via toEqual and a JSON.stringify hash comparison against a pre-toggle snapshot) -- there is no code path from flipping the display preference to a scenario/store mutation. Also tests: imperial mode shows a converted value/unit/range (v0 50 m/s -> ~111.8 mph, label ' (mph)', max 150 m/s -> ~335.5 mph); a committed display-space value round-trips back to the correct SI value before onChange; an out-of-SI-range display value still clamps correctly; an SI-only unit (deg) is never converted; units-display-logic.test.ts covers SI-mode passthrough, all three known conversions, round-tripping, and unknown/undefined units passing through unconverted. pnpm typecheck/lint/lint:deps all green; pnpm test: 833/835 passing, the 2 failures (viz lazy-plotly-pane bundle-splitting timeout, trajectory-decimation P3.10 perf assertion) are pre-existing sandbox flakiness untouched by this task -- the P3.10 one was already noted as flaky-on-this-CPU in P3.36's own notes, reproduced identically before this commit.

tasks.title: Worker pool v1: load L0/L1 bundle in worker, `sweep` job type
tasks.validation: 11×11 (θ,v₀) sweep runs off-main; UI interactive throughout (long-task probe < 50 ms)
tasks.notes: Added packages/runtime/src/sweep-job.ts: a (theta,v0) SweepJob varying launch angle/speed over a base ScenarioSpec (everything else -- forces/environment/projectile/solver -- held fixed), runSweepPoint building a fresh model+context per grid point via the existing scenario-resolver.ts (resolveModel/resolveStepper/resolveSolverConfig, same pipeline SimulationSession uses, incl. the HermiteDenseOutputStepper wrap for terminal ground-impact truncation) and summarizing each point to {range, apexHeight}. Correctness pitfall found and fixed along the way: apexHeight computed as max(recorded y-channel) is WRONG for an adaptive solve that covers a short flight in one big accepted step (recording only its two endpoints) -- the apex is an interior extremum invisible to that scan. Fixed by reading the model's own declared 'apex' event (P1.40) via an EventCollector sink instead, which localizes it precisely (§4.9) regardless of step size; caught by a closed-form cross-check test (vacuum range = v0^2*sin(2*theta)/g, apex = (v0*sin(theta))^2/(2g) at y0=0) that failed with apexHeight=0 before the fix. Added worker-pool.ts: DOM-agnostic WorkerLike/WorkerFactory structural types (no 'dom'/'webworker' lib needed) + createWorkerPool({createWorker, size}) dispatching a sweep's flattened grid across `size` long-lived reused-not-respawned workers in contiguous chunks, reassembled by each chunk's own startIndex (generalizing §5.6's MC replicate-index reduction-order-determinism principle to sweep grid-index reduction) -- also exports handleSweepChunkRequest as the one shared request/response definition. Added sweep-worker-entry.ts: the actual worker-side script (self.onmessage wired to handleSweepChunkRequest, transferring result buffers) -- typed via a module-local `declare const self` (not `declare global`) so it needs no DOM lib and can't leak into any other package's compilation, mirroring how simulation-session.ts already probes requestAnimationFrame structurally. Never re-exported from runtime's index.ts (only ever referenced by its own file path via `new URL(...)`, so importing it never side-effect-installs a worker message handler on the main thread). Kept the pool itself DOM/bundler-agnostic on purpose: a real `new Worker(new URL(...))` needs both DOM lib and Vite's static bundling, both properties of the app edge -- added packages/app/src/sweep-worker-factory.ts (createSweepWorker) as the one place that constructs a real Worker, referencing sweep-worker-entry.ts by a real cross-package relative filesystem path (not a package specifier) so Vite resolves/bundles it like any other same-repo source file; it adapts the real Worker's full-MessageEvent-shaped onmessage/onerror to WorkerLike's narrower {data} shape via a small closure-based wrapper (a direct Worker->WorkerLike assignment fails typecheck: property -- not method -- assignability is contravariant on the callback parameter, and MessageEvent has ~25 more required fields than {data:unknown}). tasks.validation: no structured-clone of Float64Array (transfer asserted)
tasks.notes: P3.39 already transferred the final SweepChunkResponse's buffers, but had no test actually PROVING transfer over structured-clone (its own fake worker just shared object references in-process, which can't distinguish the two), and had no progress messages at all -- this task adds both, plus the missing proof. Added worker-pool.ts: SweepChunkProgress message type (chunk-local completed count) and PROGRESS_THROTTLE_POINTS=8 (posts at most once per 8 completed points within a chunk -- §5.6's literal 'throttled'); handleSweepChunkRequest gained an optional onProgress param (runSweepRange, sweep-job.ts, now calls it once per point unconditionally -- deciding how often that becomes an actual posted message is this file's job, not the pure per-point loop's); new postSweepChunkResult(post, request) is what a real worker actually calls -- computes the chunk with throttled progress posts, then posts the final response with [range.buffer, apexHeight.buffer] as the transfer list, returning the response too so a test can inspect the exact transferred object. sweep-worker-entry.ts now calls postSweepChunkResult instead of handleSweepChunkRequest directly. createWorkerPool.runSweep gained an optional {onProgress(completed, total)} option: runOnWorker's onmessage now discriminates by message kind (progress vs. terminal result) instead of resolving on the first message; per-chunk completed counts are tracked in a completedByChunk array, aggregated and reported on every progress message AND forced to that chunk's full size when it resolves (so the aggregate always reaches exactly (total,total) even though individual chunks' progress reports are throttled and may never hit their own last point before the terminal message arrives). Proved the actual transfer-not-clone behavior WITHOUT a browser: Node's global MessageChannel/MessagePort (node:worker_threads) implements the same structured-clone-with-transfer algorithm as a real Worker, so worker-pool.test.ts posts through a real MessagePort and asserts response.range.buffer.byteLength===0 and response.apexHeight.buffer.byteLength===0 immediately (synchronously) after postSweepChunkResult posts -- a structured-clone COPY would leave those buffers intact; only a genuine transfer detaches them -- while also confirming port2 receives a correctly-sized, usable copy. This is the task's literal validation criterion, verified deterministically and fast (no Playwright needed for this half, unlike P3.39's off-main-thread criterion). Also added: sweep-job.test.ts (runSweepRange's onProgress fires once per point, in order, ending at the chunk size); worker-pool.test.ts's createProgressReportingFakeWorker + a new describe block (aggregated (completed,total) is monotonically non-decreasing across every report and ends at exactly (121,121) for an 11x11 sweep; omitting onProgress entirely still works with no required callback). tasks.title: Backward Euler productionizing: Jacobian reuse, simplified-Newton option
tasks.validation: dust-grain solved at h=1 ms stable; Newton iters ≤ 4 avg
tasks.notes: Added newtonMode: 'full' | 'simplified' to BackwardEulerOptions (packages/solverkit/src/backward-euler-stepper.ts), default 'full' -- byte-identical control flow to pre-P4.21 behavior, so every existing test is unaffected. 'simplified' implements the classical simplified/modified-Newton (chord) method (Hairer & Wanner): the Jacobian and (I - h*J) iteration matrix are evaluated once per step, at the initial guess y_k, into a new cached iterMatrixBase buffer, then copied into the existing (elimination-destroyed-each-call) iterMatrix scratch buffer fresh every Newton iteration instead of recomputing the Jacobian each time -- linear rather than quadratic convergence, but each extra iteration only re-solves the cached matrix (O(dim^3) elimination is negligible at this platform's small state dimensions) instead of paying for another Jacobian evaluation. Discovered while designing the test: on the dim=1 decay-style models already in the test file (including a genuinely nonlinear one, ydot=-y^3), simplified mode's extra iterations from slower convergence actually outweighed the FD-jacobian-reuse saving at dim=1 (2*dim=2 rhs evals is too small a per-iteration cost to matter) -- added a new dim=8 diagonal-cubic test fixture (CUBIC_DIM/CUBIC_CHANNELS/createCubicDecayModel in the test file) specifically because the FD fallback's 2*dim=16-rhs-eval cost needs to be large enough to dominate; confirmed simplified mode's nRHS is lower than full mode's there, converging to the same root (within 1e-6, both are Newton-tolerance-limited, not bitwise identical). Validation criterion covered directly: a new test runs the dust-grain scenario (gravity+linear-drag, FD-jacobian path, same model/ICs as P2.38's A-stability demo) for 50 fixed h=1ms steps in simplified mode, asserting every step stays accepted/finite and the average Newton-iterations-per-step is <= 4 (gravity+linear-drag is itself affine in y, so Newton -- in either mode -- converges in very few iterations regardless; the more load-bearing check here is that simplified mode stays numerically stable at this step size, not that the iteration count is close to the limit). 4 new tests, all passing; pnpm typecheck/lint/lint:deps clean; pnpm test: 1153 tests (1152 passing, the 1 failure is the same pre-existing viz/trajectory-decimation sandbox-CPU perf flake documented since P3.36 -- unrelated package, untouched); bench:solverkit/check:cross-engine-drift soft-warn steps both ran (drift-results.json reverted after, same no-matching-Playwright-browser-build reason noted in P4.19/P4.20's own sessions); engine/solverkit docs and app build/bundle-size (55.7 kB gzipped) all green.

tasks.notes: packages/solverkit/src/implicit-explicit-cost-crossover.test.ts (8 tests): work-precision overlay comparing BackwardEulerStepper (P2.38/P4.21, simplified-Newton) vs ClassicalRK4Stepper (explicit, non-symplectic per the standing dissipative-dynamics rule) on the dust-grain gravity+linear-drag stiff scenario (P1.36/P2.38/P4.21's construction), reusing P2.19's measureWorkPrecision harness unmodified (its nRHS cost metric already prices backward Euler's Newton-solve overhead honestly). Crossover point, empirically measured: RK4's bisected stability wall on this scenario is h_crit ~= 1.730 ms (== 2.785*tau, tau ~= 0.621 ms, matching the theoretical real-axis bound); its cheapest stable configuration (h=1.6ms) costs 128 rhs evals for ~4.2e-4 error, and h just 4% above the wall (1.8ms) blows the state up 2+ orders of magnitude over the 50ms tspan (confirmed directly, not just formula-asserted). Backward Euler, unconstrained by that wall, reaches better accuracy (~1.0e-5) at less than half that cost (51 rhs evals, h=10ms, ~6x RK4's entire stable range) -- so for the whole practically-relevant target-error range down to backward Euler's own Newton-tolerance floor (~1e-11), backward Euler is strictly cheaper than any viable RK4 configuration, since RK4 has no configuration at all cheaper than its stability floor on this problem. Only past that floor does RK4 (already forced stable, so already near machine epsilon for about the same fixed cost) become the only economical choice -- also measured and asserted directly. pnpm typecheck/lint/lint:deps/format:check all clean; pnpm test: 182 files/1161 tests, all passing (up from 181/1153 baseline, +1 file/+8 tests, none removed/weakened); pnpm --filter @ballista/app build succeeds (index chunk 178.5kB/57.07kB gzipped, Plotly still lazy-split at 4.84MB/1.47MB gzip, unaffected by this task). tasks.title: Phase-portrait plot pane (y vs v_y; q vs p for pendulum)
tasks.validation: Euler spiral vs Verlet closed orbit visible (automated area-growth assert)
tasks.notes:
Phase-portrait pane in packages/viz/src/phase-portrait.ts (+phase-portrait.test.ts, 17 tests), exported from viz's index.ts. Split the same two ways plot-pane.ts (P3.29) splits itself, and reuses it rather than duplicating it: both axes are recorder channels read verbatim off trajectory.channels (nothing re-derived, so there is no physics to get wrong), and the screen mapping is plot-pane.ts's own plotScreenX/plotScreenY with q on the horizontal axis in place of t -- which is why screenXToPlotTime/screenYToPlotValue still round-trip a phase point exactly (asserted). Axis ticks come from axes-layer.ts's computeAxisTicks/computeNiceStep/formatTickValue, same as drawPlotPane; the one deliberate difference is that the horizontal ticks are labeled in series.qUnit (rad) rather than seconds, and a test asserts no tick is labeled ' s'.

Which pair gets plotted: model.partitions.q[i]/p[i] are paired by index (planar-projectile-model.ts's own stated convention), so a model with k pairs offers k portraits and the pane must choose. defaultPhasePairIndex returns pair 1 when a model has >=2 pairs and pair 0 otherwise, which lands exactly on P4.32's framing ('y vs v_y; q vs p for pendulum') and not by index coincidence: PLANAR_CHANNELS and SPATIAL_CHANNELS both order positions x,y,... with y the gravity-aligned one, so pair 1 is (y, v_y) under both, while the dim-2 P4.31 pendulum has one pair and falls to (theta, thetadot). An explicit pairIndex argument overrides it (x vs v_x is reachable and tested). phasePairIndices throws descriptively for a model with no partitions at all and for an out-of-range pair -- the same 'descriptive throw over a silent wrong answer' choice scenario-resolver.ts makes for an unknown model kind.

Validation criterion ('Euler spiral vs Verlet closed orbit visible (automated area-growth assert)') is met by cycleAreas/areaGrowthRatio, which turn the picture into a number. cycleAreas cuts the orbit into laps wherever the cumulative polar angle about the origin passes each multiple of 2*pi (unwrapped step to step so a branch cut never registers as a lap; a partial final lap is discarded rather than reported short), then measures each lap's enclosed area with the shoelace formula, closing the slice back to its own first point. The angle is measured in coordinates normalized by each axis's peak magnitude -- a (rad, rad/s) pendulum orbit is an ellipse whose axes differ by roughly the natural frequency, and the raw polar angle advances very non-uniformly around one; areas themselves are always computed in raw units, the normalization only decides where a lap ends.

Measured this session on the P4.31 pendulum (L=1, g=9.81, theta0=0.5 rad, thetadot0=0, h=0.01, t in [0,16], 7 laps recorded, identical for both runs -- same model, same initial state, same h, same span, only the integrator differs): ExplicitEulerStepper's per-lap enclosed area grows monotonically 2.679524 -> 8.420249 (growth ratio 3.142442); VerletStepper('velocity') holds 2.427316 -> 2.427316 (growth ratio 1.000000 to 6 dp). The test asserts Euler's areas are strictly increasing lap over lap with ratio > 1.5, Verlet's ratio is within 1% of 1, and the two are separated by at least 10x on the same metric. Also asserted against an analytic reference: a circle of radius 2 traversed twice yields pi*r^2 per lap and a growth ratio of 1.

Integrator discipline (standing constraint): the pendulum is conservative -- no drag, no damping, no dissipative path at all -- which is the precondition for using the symplectic Verlet stepper in this comparison. No dissipative system is integrated symplectically anywhere in this diff, and no stepper or golden-trajectory code was touched; the diff is one new viz module, its test, and a one-line index export.

tasks.title: Two-body/Kepler model registration (Stage-B seed) with energy+angular momentum invariants
tasks.validation: eccentric orbit: RK4 drifts, Verlet bounded (invariant asserts)
tasks.notes:
createKeplerModel(mu) in packages/engine/src/kepler-model.ts: planar two-body problem in fixed-primary (restricted) form, r'' = -mu*r/|r|^3, dim 4 (rx, ry, vx, vy), channels KEPLER_CHANNELS, partitions {q:[rx,ry], p:[vx,vy]} paired by index per the platform convention. Reducing the genuine two-body problem to this one-body form is the textbook barycentric reduction with mu = G*(M+m), not an approximation. Second non-projectile Model after P4.31's pendulum, and the first with TWO invariants -- which is the substance of the task, not a detail: specific orbital energy E = |v|^2/2 - mu/|r| and specific angular momentum L = rx*vy - ry*vx fail differently under a given integrator, so the pair discriminates where either alone would not. E comes from the Hamiltonian structure; L comes from the force being CENTRAL (dL/dt = rx*ay - ry*ax vanishes for any a parallel to r, independently of the inverse-square profile), which is why L survives under both steppers and acts as the control in the comparison below. rhs uses Math.hypot rather than sqrt(rx^2+ry^2): the 1/r^3 cube already spans a wide dynamic range on an eccentric orbit and the naive form overflows a factor of two sooner in the exponent. mu <= 0 (and NaN) throws descriptively rather than silently producing a repulsive or null field -- the same 'descriptive throw over a silent wrong answer' choice scenario-resolver.ts and P4.32's phasePairIndices make.

Engine unit tests (kepler-model.test.ts, 13): channel/partition metadata; rhs copies velocity into the position derivative; acceleration is anti-parallel to r with magnitude mu/r^2; autonomy (t never enters rhs); mu<=0/NaN rejection; E = -mu/(2a) sampled at BOTH periapsis and apoapsis across e in {0, 0.3, 0.7, 0.95}; energy sign flip at escape speed; L = sqrt(mu*a*(1-e^2)); L = 0 on a radial trajectory and sign-flipped on a retrograde one; and zero material derivative for both invariants along the rhs at four scattered states -- that last one isolates a model bug from a stepper bug before any integrator is in the loop.

VALIDATION CRITERION MET ('eccentric orbit: RK4 drifts, Verlet bounded (invariant asserts)'), in packages/solverkit/src/kepler-invariant-drift.test.ts (5 tests) -- placed in solverkit because engine must not depend on solverkit (dependency-cruiser enforces the direction), and the criterion needs the real ClassicalRK4Stepper and VerletStepper, not hand-rolled ones. Fixture: a = 1e7 m, e = 0.6, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2, released at periapsis, 60 orbits at 2000 steps/orbit (h = T/2000, T from Kepler's third law); a first test confirms the orbit really is eccentric (r_max/r_min > 3.5, matching (1+e)/(1-e) = 4) so the rest is not measured on an accidentally-circular path. Eccentricity is what makes the comparison sharp: periapsis is a short, fast, high-curvature arc where a fixed step is locally much too coarse, and the error deposited there does not cancel over the rest of the orbit -- on a circular orbit RK4's error largely cancels around the loop and the drift takes far longer to separate.

Measured relative energy error (E(t)-E0)/|E0|: RK4's six block means march -9.30e-10 -> -1.60e-9 -> -2.26e-9 -> -2.93e-9 -> -3.59e-9 -> -4.26e-9 -- monotone in magnitude, never reversing sign, and with a near-constant per-block increment (~6.66e-10, equal to within 5%), i.e. LINEAR IN TIME, the defining shape of a secular term rather than merely 'growing'. Sharpest statement: the entire last orbit's error band lies strictly outside the entire first orbit's with no overlap at all ([-4.59e-9, -3.93e-9] vs [-6.59e-10, -1.0e-12]) -- the error has not oscillated wider, it has moved. Velocity Verlet by contrast is bounded: first- and last-orbit bands agree to 5 significant figures (7.3134e-5 both), all six block means agree to within 1%, and the error genuinely oscillates across essentially the full band within each orbit (first-orbit span [1.1e-9, 7.3e-5]) rather than sitting flat, so 'bounded' cannot pass vacuously. Note Verlet's band is one-signed here (offset from zero) rather than symmetric about it -- still bounded, which is all the property claims; an earlier draft asserted both signs and was wrong.

A fourth test deliberately keeps the claim honest: RK4's error magnitude is ~4 orders smaller than Verlet's throughout (4.59e-9 vs 7.31e-5 -- order 4 vs order 2, and per step RK4 is far more accurate here). The task's claim is about the SHAPE of the error over time, not about Verlet being the more accurate method, and the test asserts that ordering explicitly so a later reader cannot mistake the story. The run-band/first-orbit-band ratio is the robust discriminator (RK4 > 5, Verlet ~= 1); an argmax-location assertion was tried first and discarded because Verlet's band is flat to ~5 sig figs across all 60 orbits, so the argmax is decided by last-bit noise and landed in an arbitrary orbit (step 87843, orbit 44). Fifth test: both steppers hold angular momentum (worst |dL/L| -- RK4 4.4e-10, Verlet 1.6e-14, the latter essentially machine precision), confirming centrality is preserved by both and that a future change breaking both invariants at once points at the model rather than the symplectic story.

Verified non-vacuous by mutation: substituting ClassicalRK4Stepper for VerletStepper throughout the file fails exactly the two bounded-error tests and leaves the two integrator-agnostic tests (eccentricity fixture, angular momentum) passing -- the expected pattern, since only those two discriminate integrators.

INTEGRATOR DISCIPLINE (standing constraint): the two-body problem is conservative -- no drag, no damping, no dissipative path anywhere in it -- which is precisely the precondition for applying a symplectic method. No dissipative system is integrated symplectically in this diff; no stepper, force, or golden-trajectory code was touched (the diff is two new files plus one export line in engine's index.ts).

Verification: pnpm test 199 files / 1328 tests all passing (up from P4.32's 197/1310: +2 files, +18 tests = 13 engine + 5 solverkit). pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm lint:deps (1167 modules, 3143 dependencies, no violations) all clean. Engine and solverkit typedoc `docs` both generate clean. pnpm --filter @ballista/app build succeeds; check-bundle-size 60.1 kB gzipped, within the 300 kB budget.

tasks.title: Force-magnitude stacked-area plot over flight (F_g, F_d, F_M shares)
tasks.validation: shares sum to |ΣF| within 1e-12
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-05. `packages/viz/src/force-share-series.ts` + `force-share-series.test.ts` (16 tests), exported from the viz barrel. VALIDATION CRITERION MET: shares sum to |ΣF| with a worst-case residual of ~2e-25 absolute across all three scenarios, asserted row by row (not only via the aggregate helper) so one bad row cannot hide behind a maximum, plus a relative check at ~1e-17. DESIGN: a share is the signed scalar projection F_i·n̂ onto the resultant's own direction n̂ = ΣF/|ΣF|, so Σ_i share_i = (Σ_i F_i)·n̂ = |ΣF| is an exact identity and the 1e-12 criterion measures float roundoff only. Naive |F_i| magnitudes cannot satisfy it at all -- the triangle inequality puts Σ|F_i| >= |ΣF|, and a test pins the gap at >1e-6 N on the shot put. Bands stack diverging about zero (positive up, negative down) because drag's share genuinely changes sign mid-flight; a single running cursor would fold such a band back over the one beneath it. Per-force vectors come from `force-glyphs.ts`'s `computeForceGlyphs`, so bands and glyph arrows cannot disagree. THREE NON-OBVIOUS FINDINGS, all now pinned by tests: (1) drag's share flips sign ONE STEP AFTER apex, not at it -- just past apex the vertical drag component is still ~0 while the horizontal one, which always projects positively since the resultant's x-component IS drag's x-component, still dominates (measured: apex row 83, flip row 84, exactly one sign change). (2) The dust grain DIVERGES under explicit RK4 at h=0.01 (|ΣF| overflows to Infinity); it is solved here with backward Euler, implicit but not symplectic and so correct for a dissipative linear-drag path. The diverged RK4 run is retained as a test that shares go NaN rather than silently zeroing, which would report Σ share = 0 against an infinite resultant and make a diverged solve look converged. (3) The relative-closure check can normalize by NEITHER |ΣF| NOR Σ|share_i|: at terminal velocity drag cancels gravity to ~1e-64, far under the ~1e-27 rounding floor of the ~1e-11 forces involved, and the resultant turns purely horizontal so gravity's projection is exactly 0 while |F_g| is still mg. Both denominators are cancellation-damaged (|ΣF| gives a meaningless ~0.28); max_i|F_i| is not, and `ForceShareBand.magnitude` was added to carry it. Full gate green at this commit: typecheck, lint, lint:deps (1176 modules), `pnpm test` 201 files / 1352 tests, app build, bundle 60.1 kB gzipped within the 300 kB budget.

tasks.validation: regression green; diffs from v1 explained in changelog
tasks.notes: Done. Fixture goes to schemaVersion 2. **v1 half — no diffs.** All 12 v1 entries (6 PRESET_SCENARIOS x {RK4 fixed, DOPRI5}, P2.52) were re-recorded and every one is bit-identical to its v1 hash, nSteps, finalState and (for the smooth-sphere/RK4 entry) full t/channels arrays. The whole of Phase 4 — ISA atmosphere, altitude gravity, eta(T)/c(T) wiring, Mach-dependent C_d, the spin and spatial models, six new wind kinds — moved no pre-existing golden. The JSON diff is 128 added lines and 2 changed (schemaVersion, provenance); this is the task's 'diffs from v1 explained' criterion, and the honest answer is that there are none. **v2 half — 11 new entries**, sourced from the P4.36 curated library rather than newly invented, one per capability v1 cannot reach: cannonball-muzzle (ISA + Mach-dependent C_d, the only entry on the transonic rise), smooth-sphere-drag-crisis (steep C_d(Re) feature), table-tennis-topspin-decay (dim-5 planar-spin, omega-decay), lateral-launch-3d (dim-6 spatial), log-profile-boundary-layer (wind shear), one-cosine-gust (P4.18), frozen-ou-gust (seeded OU frozen realisation, ADR-011), vortex-crossing (position-dependent wind), density-altitude-2000m (exponential atmosphere + altitude-dependent gravity, the only library entry enabling the latter), buoyancy-visible, and energy-drift-gravity-only (fixed-step RK4 from the library's own solver spec). **Solver choice, and the main finding.** v2 entries are recorded with a regression-grade DOPRI5 (rtol=1e-10/atol=1e-12, v1's own config), NOT the rtol=1e-6 REFERENCE_SOLVER their library specs carry. Measured reason: at rtol=1e-6 the adaptive step sequence is itself sensitive to a one-ulp change in y0, and frozen-ou-gust's final state moved 8.07e-5 relative for a 7.11e-15 change in vx0 — amplification 3.6e11. A golden recorded at the app's working tolerance cannot detect a physics regression smaller than its own solver noise. energy-drift-gravity-only is the documented exception and keeps its fixed-step library solver, because being fixed-step is that entry's whole subject. **Tolerance review.** v1 applied one global 1e-13 relative tolerance to every entry's final state. v2 keeps 1e-13 as a floor and derives each entry's tolerance from a measurement: perturb each non-zero y0 component by one relative EPS, re-integrate, take the largest relative final-state change, divide by EPS to get an amplification, then round the implied bound up to a decade. Measured at regression-grade tolerance, 8 of 11 entries are well-conditioned (A between 2.7 and 4.5e2) and keep the 1e-13 floor; three need more, each for a nameable reason: table-tennis-topspin-decay A=1.62e4 -> 1e-11, one-cosine-gust A=4.52e2 -> 1e-12, and frozen-ou-gust A=2.59e8 -> 1e-7. The frozen-OU outlier is the one worth carrying forward: its wind is a PCHIP interpolant over 501 sampled points, so the RHS is only C1 in t (second derivative jumps at every knot), and its step sequence genuinely reorders under the perturbation (nSteps changes). That is the same order-degradation mechanism P4.34's C0-vs-C1 exhibit demonstrates in the state variable, showing up here in time. Not fixed here — it is a property of the wind model, not a defect in this store, and a fix would be a change to P4.17's interpolation scheme, outside this task. tasks.title: (Stretch) SDIRK2/TR-BDF2 stepper
tasks.validation: L-stability demo; slope 2
tasks.notes: Alexander SDIRK2 in packages/solverkit/src/sdirk2-stepper.ts: 2-stage singly diagonally implicit, stiffly accurate, gamma = 1 - 1/sqrt(2) = 0.2928932188134524 (the root of gamma^2 - 2*gamma + 1/2 in (0,1), which IS the second-order condition sum(b_i c_i) = 1/2 for this tableau). Chosen over TR-BDF2 -- the task names either -- because it reaches the same L-stability at second order in two stages rather than three. Exported as Sdirk2Stepper (info.id 'sdirk2', order 2) with sdirk2StabilityFunction and SDIRK2_GAMMA; derivation page sdirk2-stepper.derivation.md wired into STEPPER_DERIVATION_DOCS and the P2.51 link test. 16 new tests. VALIDATION, both halves measured rather than asserted about the formula alone: (1) slope 2 -- measureConvergence on the linear-drag benchmark (3.6-3.7) against its closed form over hs = [0.02 ... 0.00125] gives slope in (1.9, 2.1). (2) L-stability demo -- the stepper's own one-step amplification on the Dahlquist equation matches R(z) = (1 + (1-2g)z)/(1-gz)^2 to 10 digits at z in {-0.5,-1,-5,-50,-1e3,-1e6,0.5,1}; |R| <= 1 across a 0.25-spaced grid of re in [-60,0] x im in [0,60]; |R| tracks its (1-2g)/(g^2|z|) asymptote to within 1e-7 by z = -1e10; and at h = 1e4 * h_crit(explicit Euler) (lambda = -1e4, h = 2, z = -2e4, where explicit Euler amplifies by 2e4 per step) one step damps by 4144x to |y| = 2.4131e-4. Contrast case throughout is the trapezoidal rule, A-stable but not L-stable: |R| = 0.9608 at z = -1e2 climbing to 0.9999999996 at z = -1e10, asserted on its R(z) since SolverKit has no trapezoidal stepper. NEGATIVE CONTROL: perturbing gamma to 0.3 drops the measured slope from 2.00 to 0.49 and fails both order-condition tests, so the assertions are not vacuous. TWO FINDINGS worth carrying forward. (a) SDIRK2's R(z) is NEGATIVE for z < -1/(1-2g) = -2.414, so it does not avoid the stiff sign flip -- what it avoids is the flipped component keeping its magnitude. A test claiming otherwise was written, failed, and was corrected. (b) The Newton convergence criterion floors the decay at ~newtonAtol: once |y| falls to roughly the absolute tolerance, a stage's initial residual already scores <= 1 in scaledErrorNorm, so Newton exits at iteration 0 and returns its initial guess and the step becomes a no-op. Measured on 20 steps at z = -5000: stalls at 5.89e-16 with the default atol = 1e-10, reaches R^20 = 4.79e-61 with atol = 1e-300. This is a property of scaledErrorNorm and is SHARED WITH BackwardEulerStepper -- not specific to this tableau, and only reachable on a solution decaying toward zero in absolute terms (the Dahlquist test problem, not a trajectory). Pinned in a test. NOT DONE, deliberately: no embedded error estimator (errorEstimate stays 0), so this is fixed-step only; the adaptive companion is an ESDIRK pair, which changes the tableau rather than extending it. Not added to the solver-panel dropdown or the solver advisor either -- P4.38's validation criterion is numerical, and UI exposure was not claimed.

tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-06 (3rd run). docs/adr/ADR-015-rotational-dynamics-scope.md, Status: Accepted. DECISION: rotational dynamics stay kinematic for the whole roadmap (Phases 0-7) — ω is a constant parameter (ProjectileParams.spin, read by MagnusForce) or a state component obeying ω̇ = −ω/τ_ω (§3.6; createPlanarProjectileSpinModel, dim 5, channels [x,y,vx,vy,omega], with StatefulSpinMagnusForce reading ω from state). ProjectileParams.spinAxis is documented as what it is: a constant input direction for the dim-6 spatial model's 3D Magnus term (P4.24), not an evolving attitude. Full Euler rigid-body attitude (quaternion + I ω̇ + ω × I ω = M_aero), angle-of-attack-dependent aero, fin stabilization, yaw of repose and spin drift are scoped OUT as future work — deferred, not rejected. Three interim constraints: no implicit attitude (never infer a body frame from velocity, never integrate spinAxis); a future attitude model registers as a new model kind with its own dim rather than widening an existing one (the P4.07 precedent); and no doc/exhibit/teaching note may claim spin drift, yaw of repose or angle-of-attack effects.
