tasks.title: Observable framework: pure functions Trajectory→scalar (range, apex, ToF, impact speed, miss distance to target)
tasks.validation: drag-free observables match analytics to 1e-9
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-07 (2nd run). Phase 5 opens here. packages/analysis/src/observables.ts exports timeOfFlight, range, apexHeight, apexTime, apex (the {t, height} pair), impactSpeed and missDistance, all pure functions of a Trajectory. LAYOUT SEAM: channel indices come from a TrajectoryLayout table (PLANAR_LAYOUT [x,y,vx,vy], SPATIAL_LAYOUT [x,y,z,vx,vy,vz]) rather than being hard-coded, so the same code serves both shipped projectile models and whatever Stage B adds; `vertical` indexes INTO position/velocity, naming the up-axis without exposing absolute channel numbering. IMPACT OBSERVABLES DO NO INTERPOLATION: integrate() root-localizes every terminal crossing and dispatches the localized state to its sinks before returning (integrate.ts line ~517), so the recorder's final row already sits on the event surface -- range/ToF/impact speed/miss inherit their accuracy from event localization rather than producing it. Documented in-file, including the corollary that a solve which ended by exhausting tspan or maxSteps has an ordinary final row these functions will meaninglessly report as an impact. APEX CANNOT DO THAT: it rarely lands on a step boundary, and a row-wise maximum is only O(h^2). Each DOWNWARD v_y zero-crossing is refined with the cubic Hermite basis of section 4.9, using the recorded v_y channel as the derivative (free -- ydot = v_y is a state channel, no extra rhs call); the derivative of that cubic is a quadratic solved in closed form with the sign-stable q = -(b + sign(b)*sqrt(b^2-4ac))/2 root, avoiding the cancellation the textbook formula suffers when |a| << |b|. Exact to roundoff drag-free BY CONSTRUCTION, not by luck: y(t) is quadratic and v_y linear there, and a cubic Hermite reproduces any cubic exactly, so the interpolant IS the true arc. Every crossing is scanned (not just the first) with the recorded endpoints as candidates, which covers bouncing arcs (P4.11) and monotonic arcs with no interior crossing. VALIDATION -- 'drag-free observables match analytics to 1e-9' is met by packages/analysis/src/observables.test.ts, 39 assertions over five drag-free launches compared to CLOSED FORMS, never to a prior run of this code. Two of the five launch from height: at y0=0 the flight time collapses to 2*v_y0/g and the apex sits exactly halfway, so a sign error or a factor-of-two can cancel itself; a raised launch breaks that symmetry. Impact speed is checked against sqrt(v0^2 + 2*g*y0) -- energy conservation, independent of the flight-time formula rather than an algebraic restatement of it. NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED: disabling the apex refinement failed 12 assertions; including the vertical axis in range failed 3 (only the raised-launch and 3D cases -- the three y0=0 cases cannot see that bug, which is precisely why the raised launches are in the table); making timeOfFlight absolute failed 1. The coarse-step apex test carries an anti-vacuity floor (row-wise error must exceed 1e-6) so it cannot pass by the apex happening to land on a step boundary. A GUARD-RAIL TEST FOUND A REAL GAP AND THE IMPLEMENTATION MOVED TO MEET IT: validating channels lazily on read let SPATIAL_LAYOUT on a planar solve skip the vertical axis, read vx as if it were z, and return a confidently wrong range instead of throwing; requireLayout now validates the whole layout up front. MEASURED AT THIS HEAD: typecheck clean; lint clean; lint:deps no violations; app build green with the bundle at 65.6 kB gzipped against the 300 kB section 2.6 budget; typedoc for engine and solverkit both green. TEST RESULTS: pnpm test is 1514 tests across 208 files (was 1475/207 at session start: +39 tests, +1 file, no regressions). Three full-suite runs: TWO FULLY GREEN, ONE RED. The red run was the known load-sensitive flake documented in the P4.39/P4.40 entries -- chunked-integration.test.ts's wall-clock assertion (maxSliceMs 14.41 against a <10 ms budget) -- plus a 30 s timeout in viz/lazy-plotly-pane.bundle.test.ts, which builds with vite and is timing-sensitive under the same load. Neither was weakened, skipped or deleted, and both passed in the two green runs. NOTHING ELSE CHANGED: no engine, solverkit, runtime, viz, ui or app behaviour was touched. HOSTED CI: run 31189458511 at b25bcd6 passed all 16 steps in 3m39s, with pnpm test green in 1m46s on the first attempt -- including both tests that flaked locally, further evidence they are load-sensitive rather than regressions.

tasks.title: Target model: point / ring / raised-platform with hit predicate + miss vector
tasks.validation: miss vector zero at exact hit (constructed)
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-07 (3rd run). packages/analysis/src/targets.ts defines Target = PointTarget | RingTarget | PlatformTarget, exporting validateTarget, nearestPointOn, missVector, missMagnitude, isHit, and the trajectory-level impactMissVector / impactIsHit. SETS, NOT CASES: all three shapes are defined as point sets and every operation derives from ONE nearest-point routine -- missVector = impact - nearestPointOn(target), missMagnitude = its norm, isHit = magnitude <= tolerance. That is what makes 'the miss vector is zero exactly when the shot hits' a consequence rather than three separately-maintained special cases, and it keeps the residual P5.04 drives to zero continuous across the target boundary, where a kind-specific formula is the natural place to introduce a kink. SIGN CONVENTION is impact MINUS target, so for a point target missVector is literally P5.04's F = r_impact - r* and a Newton step consumes it with no sign to remember at the call site; a dedicated test pins the sign, since no magnitude assertion can. SHAPES: point (measure zero, the limit case P5.03/P5.04 are written against); ring = horizontal disc at the centre's height, or a true annulus when innerRadius > 0, where the hole is a miss; platform = axis-aligned horizontal rectangle at the centre's height, one halfExtent per horizontal axis, with ZERO vertical extent -- it models landing ON TOP of a pad, so the right downrange distance at the wrong height is a miss with a purely vertical miss vector, which is exactly the case observables.missDistance's doc singles out. FLOATING-POINT DETAIL THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: an interior point's components are COPIED into the nearest point rather than reconstructed as centre + (point - centre) * scale with scale === 1, because that identity does not hold in floating point (10.1 + (30.3 - 10.1) is 30.300000000000004) and would leave a ~1e-15 miss instead of an exact zero. DEGENERATE CASE: the dead centre of an annulus is equidistant from the whole inner rim, so the first horizontal axis is chosen deterministically -- arbitrary, but stable and finite, which is what a solver stepping through the centre needs. ALSO ADDED observables.impactPoint (position components at the impact row), which the trajectory-level helpers need and which P5.01 had no reason to export. VALIDATION -- 'miss vector zero at exact hit (constructed)' is met by packages/analysis/src/targets.test.ts, 33 cases, with BIT-EXACT assertions (toBe(0) plus an Object.is(-0) sign check) rather than a tolerance, because a nearest-point routine that reconstructs an interior point arithmetically lands within an ulp of it and toBeCloseTo cannot tell the two apart. Miss cases are checked against closed-form geometry (radial overshoot r - radius, per-axis box clamp), never against a prior run. NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED: flipping the miss sign fails 12 assertions; forcing the scaling path in the ring interior fails exactly the non-round-tripping-coordinates case; letting the platform ignore the vertical axis fails 3. FINDING WORTH CARRYING FORWARD: a flat target with tolerance 0 is never hit by a SOLVED trajectory, only by a constructed point, because event localization puts the impact's vertical coordinate at ~6e-15 m rather than 0 -- all three shapes have zero vertical extent, so the miss picks that up. Asserted directly in the trajectory-level test rather than worked around, and the tolerance doc comment now says so. A trajectory-level hit test therefore needs a tolerance reflecting what counts as 'on it' physically (shell radius, scoring ring width), not the solver's arithmetic; P5.04-P5.06 should use missVector, which is unaffected, rather than isHit. MEASURED at this HEAD: pnpm typecheck / lint / lint:deps clean (no violations, 1215 modules); pnpm test 1547 tests across 209 files, all green in one run (was 1514/208: +33 tests, +1 file, no regressions, no flake this run); app build green; check-bundle-size 65.6 kB gzipped against the 300 kB section 2.6 budget, unchanged.

tasks.title: Scalar root problem: range(θ)=R* at fixed v₀ (drag-free) via Brent
tasks.validation: recovers both analytic roots θ=½asin(gR*/v₀²) and complement to 1e-10
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-07 (4th run). packages/analysis/src/range-root.ts exports RangeFunction, DRAG_FREE_PEAK_ANGLE, dragFreeRange, solveRangeRoot (explicit bracket) and solveRangeRoots (both arcs + reachability). No new root finder: the residual range(θ) − R* is handed to solverkit's brentRoot, which its own doc comment already names P5.03 as the intended second caller of. VALIDATION MET: both arcs recovered to <1e-10 rad against ½asin(gR*/v₀²) and its complement to π/2, over 4 closed-form cases and 2 cases where the range function is a Dormand–Prince 5(4) integration (rtol 1e-13/atol 1e-14) read through P5.01's range observable — the second path never evaluates asin, so the closed form is an independent reference rather than the same algebra twice. 39 tests, all green; full suite 1586/1586 across 210 files. DESIGN: the two arcs are bracketed separately either side of the peak rather than solved once and reflected. Reflection is exact for sin(2θ) and would have passed every drag-free assertion in the file — verified, not assumed, by a negative control that implements it and fails only 3 of 39 — but it is a property of that function, not of the problem, so it would ship a wrong high arc the moment drag makes range asymmetric about its peak. That is what the asymmetric-range case (peak at atan(1/√2)) exists to catch. CONSEQUENCE FOR P5.06+: peakAngle is data, defaulting to π/4, which is correct ONLY for a drag-free ground launch; a raised or drag-affected launch peaks lower and MUST pass its own. Computing it in general is P5.09's envelope sweep / P5.13's 1D minimizer — deliberately not done here. low/high are independently nullable because an angle bound can remove one arc without the other. Two findings worth carrying: (1) a target of exactly 0 has no high-arc root, since dragFreeRange(π/2) evaluates sin(Math.PI) = 1.22e-16 rather than 0 — pinned by a test; (2) Brent's final interpolation lands far inside its own stopping tolerance, so loosening angleTol from 1e-12 to 1e-6 changes no assertion in this file — the 1e-10 criterion measures the method, not the stopping rule, and a future task must not treat angleTol as the knob that controls accuracy.

tasks.title: Shooting residual for 2D target: F(θ,v₀)=r_impact−r* using event state
tasks.validation: residual continuous across step boundaries (dense-output check)
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-08 (5th run). packages/analysis/src/shooting-residual.ts exports Aim, ShootingProblem, ShootingResidual, ResidualFunction, createShootingResidual and residualNorm. F(theta, v0) = missVector(target, impactPoint(traj)) -- P5.02's sign convention is impact MINUS target, so the residual is that call's return value with no sign to re-derive here. VALIDATION MET -- 'residual continuous across step boundaries (dense-output check)'. The measurement needs a FIXED-step solve and that is the one non-obvious part of the test design: an adaptive solve picks its own step sizes per aim, so its grid moves WITH the aim and there is no fixed boundary left for the event to cross. With h pinned at 0.05 the grid is 0, h, 2h, ... for every aim while the ground-event time 2*v0*sin(theta)/g slides continuously, so sweeping theta walks the event across boundary after boundary. 401 samples over [0.60, 0.70] rad at v0 = 60 produce 20 DISTINCT step counts spanning 139-158, and the test asserts that spread -- without it the continuity assertions would pass vacuously on a sweep that never left a single step interval. NUMBERS: max |second difference| of the residual is 9.04e-5 m, against |R''|*dtheta^2 = 8.8e-5 m predicted from the range curve's own curvature (|R''| <= 4*v0^2/g). So the residual's discrete curvature is the range curve's curvature and nothing else. NEGATIVE CONTROL, and it is the load-bearing part: gridPointResidualX reads row nSteps-2 -- the last step grid point before the crossing, which is what a residual that ignored dense output would see -- and on the IDENTICAL sweep measures max |second difference| 2.47 m and a largest single-sample jump of 2.41 m, against a predicted h*vx = 2.39 m. Factor of 2.7e4 between the two. The 1e-3 m bound the test asserts sits an order above the curvature scale and three orders below the jump, so it fails on a staircase and does not fail on ordinary sampling. Continuity is re-checked at a raised launch (launchPoint [0, 25]) because that is the configuration P5.06 actually solves in. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED DURING THE TASK, worth carrying forward: report.status === 'ok' does NOT mean the shot hit the ground. Exhausting tspan without reaching the terminal event is a SUCCESSFUL solve -- the driver reached t_f -- and its final recorded row is an ordinary mid-air point that impactPoint reports as an impact without complaint. The first implementation keyed 'ok' off report.status and a shot with tspan [0, 1] came back with a finite, plausible, meaningless residual. 'ok' is now report.status === 'ok' && report.tFinal < tspan[1]: a terminal event stops the solve strictly inside the span, whereas the driver clamps its last step to land exactly on tspan[1] when the span is what ran out, which makes it an exact discriminator rather than a tolerance. A test pins the trap. FAILURE IS A VALUE, NOT A THROW: ok:false with null residual/impact/timeOfFlight, and residualNorm returns Infinity there, because P5.06's Armijo line search stepping into a bad trial aim must be able to shorten its step -- throwing would make an ordinary incident in an optimization indistinguishable from a bug. Non-finite aims and malformed launch points DO throw, since those are caller errors that would otherwise reach Newton as an unattributable NaN. TWO CONSTRUCTION PRECONDITIONS, both about the criterion rather than defensive habit: a model with no terminal event, and a stepper with no dense-output interpolant, are rejected at construction. integrate truncates a step at an event root only when both are present; with either missing the residual is the staircase, and the staircase LOOKS FINE -- finite, right magnitude, decreasing as the aim improves. Only its derivative is wrong, so the symptom would surface tasks later as a Newton solver converging linearly. ClassicalRK4Stepper is the concrete case (no interpolant) and a test uses it. CONSEQUENCE FOR P5.05/P5.06: for a point target ON THE GROUND the vertical residual component is ~0 for every aim (impact is localized onto y = 0), so the 2x2 Jacobian is structurally singular. A test pins this at <1e-9. A genuinely 2D residual needs a raised target -- the raised-point case is pinned too, reporting -12 m vertical against a target 12 m up. P5.06 must shoot at a point target and use ring/platform shapes for scoring only: missVector against an extended target is zero across the whole face, which is the right answer for 'put it anywhere on the pad' and a degenerate one for Newton, which needs an isolated root. 22 tests; full suite 1608/1608 across 211 files.

tasks.title: FD Jacobian of shooting residual with adaptive-step *noise control* (fixed-step or tight-tol inner solves)
tasks.validation: Jacobian FD convergence plateau documented; no tolerance-noise blowup
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-08 (6th run). packages/analysis/src/shooting-jacobian.ts exports FiniteDifferenceScheme, DEFAULT_NOISE_FLOOR, AIM_COLUMNS, JacobianOptions, ShootingJacobian, finiteDifferenceStep and shootingJacobian. Central (default) and forward schemes; columns are (theta, v0), rows the residual components. VALIDATION MET -- 'Jacobian FD convergence plateau documented; no tolerance-noise blowup'. THE STEP IS DERIVED FROM A DECLARED NOISE FLOOR, NOT FROM MACHINE EPSILON, and that is the task's whole point. Balancing truncation C*h^p against amplified noise eps_F/h gives h* = scale * noiseFloor^(1/(p+1)) -- square root of the floor for forward, cube root for central. At eps_F = eps a central difference wants h ~ 6e-6, but at eps_F = 1e-6 (an inner solve at rtol 1e-6) it wants h ~ 1e-2: THREE AND A HALF ORDERS LARGER. Keeping the machine-epsilon step while loosening tolerance is not conservatism, it is sitting far up the noise branch. Steps are per-variable and scaled because theta ~ 1 rad and v0 ~ 60 m/s share no usable step size. PLATEAU MEASUREMENT (drag-free, fixed step h = 0.01, theta = 0.65, v0 = 60, exact analytic reference dR/dtheta = 196.396 m/rad, dR/dv0 = 11.7907 s). Relative error of dF/dtheta, central, FD step 1e-10 -> 1e-1: 7.6e-5, 5.8e-6, 4.2e-7, 4.5e-8, 1.3e-8, 2.7e-10, 6.6e-9, 6.7e-7, 6.7e-5, 6.7e-3. A clean V: minimum 2.7e-10 at h = 1e-5, truncation branch scaling EXACTLY as h^2 (a factor of 100 per decade across 1e-1 -> 1e-3, asserted as a ratio rather than a pinned magnitude since h^2 is what makes the scheme second order), noise branch rising as 1/h below the plateau. Best achievable relative error: central 2.7e-10 vs forward 1.9e-7, a factor of ~700, which is the order difference showing up as plateau depth. The module's DEFAULT step lands inside that plateau and a test asserts it. TOLERANCE-NOISE CONTROL, and it required a DIFFERENT PROBLEM -- this is the non-obvious part of the task. Drag-free motion is quadratic in t and Dormand-Prince integrates it EXACTLY, so the embedded error estimate vanishes and every tolerance from 1e-4 to 1e-12 produces the identical step sequence. The first version of the test ran the negative control drag-free and got BYTE-IDENTICAL curves for loose and tight tolerances, measuring nothing at all. Quadratic drag (Cd 0.47, range 230.53 m) makes the controller actually adapt. On the identical sweep: fixed-step h = 0.01 reaches 2.0e-10 at h_FD = 1e-5, while adaptive rtol = 1e-5 FLOORS AT 8.5e-6 and stays there flat across h_FD 1e-8 -> 1e-4, never going lower. Ratio 4.2e4, about four and a half orders. The floor is flat rather than 1/h-rising because the loose residual is not randomly noisy but BIASED: the controller makes locally identical step decisions for nearby aims, so the rtol-level bias is a smooth wrong function whose derivative is wrong by a fixed amount. Refining h therefore recovers NOTHING, which is asserted directly. That is the practical face of 'tolerance-noise blowup': not a visible explosion but a floor no step size beats. STRUCTURAL RANK-1, carried forward from P5.04 and now pinned on the Jacobian itself: a ground-impact terminal event pins y_impact to the ground for every aim, so the vertical ROW is zero to <1e-8 and the 2x2 matrix is rank 1 -- REGARDLESS of target height, since a raised target only shifts F_y by a constant (tested at 12 m). A ground-impact shot is one scalar equation in two unknowns, which is exactly why P5.08 speaks of low/high arcs and P5.22 of locking two of three. P5.06 MUST NOT hand this matrix to an unguarded 2x2 solve; it needs a rank-aware step (lock v0 and solve theta, or LM per P5.26). FAILURE IS A VALUE, NOT A THROW, matching P5.04: a perturbation that leaves the reachable set returns ok:false with a null matrix and a failure string NAMING which perturbation failed, since 'the Jacobian failed' is not actionable but 'the +theta perturbation left the reachable set' tells a line search to shorten its step. No one-sided fallback: silently halving the scheme's order would move the plateau, which is the exact invisible accuracy loss this module exists to prevent. Non-positive explicit steps DO throw (caller error). 18 tests; full suite 1626/1626 across 212 files, app build green. OBSERVED, NOT ACTED ON (scope): CLAUDE.md fails prettier --check at this HEAD, pre-existing and untouched by this run -- format:check is not a CI step, which is why it drifted. The analysis package has no typedoc.json, so a co-located *.derivation.md would not be wired into docs the way solverkit's are; that belongs to P5.29 (Analysis API docs), and this task documented the plateau in TSDoc plus printed test measurements instead.

tasks.title: Newton shooting solver with line search (Armijo)
tasks.validation: hits target with drag+wind in ≤ 8 iters from smart init
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-09 (7th run). packages/analysis/src/newton-shooting.ts exports NewtonShootingStatus, NewtonShootingStep, NewtonShootingOptions, NewtonShootingResult, MinimumNormStep, minimumNormStep and newtonShooting. VALIDATION MET -- "hits target with drag+wind in <= 8 iters": quadratic drag (Cd 0.47, m 1 kg, r 0.05 m) plus a 6 m/s headwind (UniformWind(-6)), point target at x = 236.1502 m built from the impact of an aim never shown to the solver, started from a deliberately rough theta = 0.45 rad / v0 = 65 m/s. **3 iterations**, ||F|| 2.270e+1 -> 4.598e-1 -> 2.007e-4 -> 3.860e-11 m, alpha = 1 every step -- the digit-doubling of a Newton method, not linear decay. Three further starts (0.3/70, 0.45/65, 0.95/60) all converge in <= 8. CAVEAT ON THE CRITERION'S WORDING: "from smart init" is P5.07, which does not exist yet, so every solve here starts from a hand-chosen rough aim instead. That makes 3 an UPPER BOUND on what a smart init needs rather than a measurement of it; P5.07 should re-run this criterion with the real initializer. THE STEP IS A TRUNCATED-SVD MINIMUM-NORM LEAST-SQUARES SOLVE, NOT A LINEAR SOLVE, and that is the task. P5.05 predicted the Jacobian is rank 1 and this run measured it on the actual drag+wind problem: downrange row ~1.996e+2, vertical row ~2.779e-11, ratio 1.39e-13 (drag-free the ratio is EXACTLY 0 -- the vertical row is not small, it is zero in floating point). solverkit's solveLinearSystemInPlace REFUSES that system outright at its 1e-12 pivot threshold, recorded as a negative control in the tests, so an unguarded Newton step is not merely inaccurate here, it has no answer at all. Singular values below rankTolerance * sigma_max (default 1e-7) are discarded and the step lands in the row space of what survives. Choosing the truncated solve over the changelog's suggested "lock v0 and solve theta" is deliberate: it lets the matrix pick the expendable direction instead of hard-coding which unknown is, and survives unchanged if a later task adds a terminal event that does not pin the vertical component. Levenberg-Marquardt is P5.26 and was NOT built. TWO DESIGN POINTS THAT ARE DECISIONS, NOT DEFAULTS. (1) COLUMNS ARE SCALED before the step is computed and the step norm is measured in the scaled variables. theta ~ 1 rad and v0 ~ 60 m/s, so "minimum norm" in raw units is a statement about v0 and almost nothing about theta -- the raw min-norm solve would resolve the rank-1 ambiguity by declining to change the angle, for no reason but the unit it is measured in. Same thetaScale/speedScale pair shootingJacobian uses for its difference steps. (2) THE ARMIJO CONDITION COMPARES AGAINST THE LINEAR MODEL'S PREDICTED REDUCTION ||F|| - ||F + J.d||, not against (1 - c*alpha)||F||. The textbook form assumes the step can in principle remove all of ||F||, which is true for a nonsingular square J and FALSE here: with an irreducible residual component it is unsatisfiable for every alpha once the reducible part is gone, so the line search would exhaust its backtracks and report failure at the exact moment the solver had done everything the problem allows. Pinned by a raised-platform test (12 m up, ground-impact solve): status "stalled", |F_x| < 1e-6 m, F_y = -12 m to 9 places. RANK TOLERANCE DEFAULT IS 1e-7 AND THE VALUE IS CONSTRAINED FROM BELOW: minimumNormStep gets its singular values from the eigenvalues of the 2x2 Gram matrix J^T J, which squares the ratio being tested, so any threshold under sqrt(eps) ~ 1.5e-8 asks a double to resolve a Gram eigenvalue below its own rounding. 1e-7 sits an order above that floor and four orders above the 1e-11..1e-13 deficiency it must catch. A caller needing to resolve a genuine 1e-9 singular value needs a Golub-Kahan SVD; documented in-file. 18 tests (8 on minimumNormStep alone: exact nonsingular, singular values of a diagonal matrix, exactly-rank-1 minimum-norm with an explicit check that every other solution of the same equation is longer, an inconsistent system checked by A^T(b - Ax) = 0, an overdetermined 3x2 spatial-layout case, a zero matrix returning rank 0 rather than dividing, threshold-sensitivity in both directions, and a shape error). Line search verified to backtrack on a real overshoot (target 240 m from v0 = 25 m/s, where drag makes range concave in v0 so the linear model overpromises): alphas 0.5/0.5/1/1/1/1/1, 7 iterations, every accepted step a strict decrease. Full local gate green: typecheck clean, lint clean, lint:deps no violations (1239 modules, 3380 dependencies), pnpm test 1644/1644 across 213 files (up from 1626/212), app build 46.6s, bundle 65.6 kB gzipped against a 300 kB budget. FOLLOW-ON: minimumNormStep is exported for its own tests and is a candidate to move into solverkit beside dense-linear-solve.ts when P5.26's LM becomes its second caller -- not moved now, since a one-caller abstraction in another package is a guess about the second caller's needs.

tasks.title: Smart initializer: drag-free closed-form (θ, v₀) guess
tasks.validation: init within basin for all library targets (measured success rate 100%)
tasks.notes: DONE 2026-08-09 (8th run). packages/analysis/src/smart-init.ts exports dragFreeAim(downrange, rise, gravity) and smartInitialAim(problem, options), re-exported from the package index. CHOICE OF SOLUTION: the drag-free reachability condition for a point is one equation in two unknowns, so the closed form has to select a point on the solution curve; it selects the MINIMUM-SPEED one, theta = pi/4 + phi/2 with phi = atan2(rise, downrange), v0 = sqrt(g (rise + R)), R = hypot(downrange, rise). That is the only point determined by the geometry alone -- every other closed form on the curve needs a muzzle speed or an elevation supplied from outside, and selecting between the two arcs that then result is P5.08. VALIDATION MET, 20/20 = 100%: each of engine's 20 SCENARIO_LIBRARY entries becomes a shooting problem whose target is the impact of its OWN launch aim (reachable by construction), and newtonShooting converges from the closed-form init on every one, in at most 5 iterations -- 0 for the two drag-free entries where the closed form is already the answer, 5 for smooth-sphere-drag-crisis and density-altitude-2000m. The drag-free initial miss is large for several (1040 m cannonball-muzzle, 225 m smooth-sphere-drag-crisis, 116 m golf-drive), which is the point of a basin criterion rather than an accuracy one. Harness uses DOPRI5 rtol 1e-12 rather than the library specs' rtol 1e-6, which would have the FD Jacobian differencing step-sequence noise (same substitution golden-trajectory-store.ts makes). Spin channel starts at zero and vz0 is dropped, because an aim is two numbers. NUMERICS: rise + R cancels catastrophically for a target below the launcher (rise = -400, R = 400.00125 keeps ~3 of 16 digits), so the rise < 0 branch evaluates the algebraically identical downrange^2 / (R - rise); measured 4e-11 relative error against 4e-16 on the same grid point. Gravity is sampled from the problem's own environment at the launch point into a fresh EnvSample (never ctx.env, the rhs scratch buffer), because the library ships an altitude-dependent-gravity entry a hard-coded G_STD would misjudge. NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: no drag correction (the task is the drag-free form; a correction would be a fitted constant or the Newton iteration this feeds), and no arc selection (P5.08). FOLLOW-UP FOR P5.06: its validation criterion says 'from smart init' and was measured from hand-chosen aims because this did not exist. That criterion can now be re-measured for real; the library harness here already shows <= 5 iterations with drag and wind, inside P5.06's <= 8.

tasks.title: Multi-solution handling: report low/high arcs; UI selects
tasks.validation: both arcs found for reachable targets; consistent labeling
tasks.notes: `packages/analysis/src/arcs.ts` exports `solveArcs`, `locatePeakAngle`, `ArcLabel`, `ArcSolution`, `ArcOptions`, `ArcPair`, `PeakAngle`. At a FIXED launch speed the solution curve P5.05 measured as rank-1 is met twice, and `solveArcs` returns both meetings labelled `low` (flat, fast) and `high` (lofted). VALIDATION MET: all 20 SCENARIO_LIBRARY entries, 19 with two arcs found and correctly labelled, 1 (`dust-grain`) monotone with its single arc found — see below. Downrange miss < 1e-6 m on every arc of every entry; the drag-free case additionally matches the closed-form roots ½asin(gR/v₀²) and its complement to 1e-9 rad. REUSE: the bracketing is P5.03's `solveRangeRoots`, supplied with an integrated `RangeFunction` — the substitution `range-root.ts`'s own doc comment was written to accept. The only new numerics is the peak angle, which `DRAG_FREE_PEAK_ANGLE` cannot supply once drag or a raised launch moves it (measured: 0.32 rad for `golf-drive`, 0.21 for `density-altitude-2000m`, against π/4 = 0.785); a misplaced peak puts both roots in one bracket rather than merely losing accuracy, so it is located by a 24-point sweep refined by golden section to 1e-4 rad. Golden section rather than a derivative method because each evaluation is a trajectory integration. TWO FINDINGS, both handled rather than worked around: (1) A boundary peak is a real case, not an error — `dust-grain`'s carry falls across the whole of [0, π/2], so there is no interior peak and only one branch exists. `solveRangeRoots` rejects a non-interior peak (correctly, for itself), so `solveBranches` handles the monotone interval directly and labels the single root by which bound the peak sits on. (2) The two-arc band is bounded BELOW as well as above, by the larger of the two bound carries: `density-altitude-2000m` launches from 2000 m and already carries 94 m of its 96 m envelope at 0°, so targets below that are lofted-arc-only and `low: null` is the correct report. `maxDownrange` is a lower bound on the true envelope (the peak is located to `peakTol`, and range is quadratic there), so a target within microns of the envelope reads unreachable — the conservative direction, pinned by a test. NOT DONE HERE: the 'UI selects' half of the title is P5.21 (draggable target marker, solve-on-drop with arc choice), which this task feeds rather than pre-empts. Full gate green: typecheck 0 errors, lint clean, lint:deps clean (1251 modules), `pnpm test` 1701/1701 across 215 files, app build + bundle budget (65.6 kB gzipped of 300 kB) both pass.

tasks.title: Reachability boundary: max-range envelope (parabola of safety analog with drag) via θ sweep + bisection on feasibility
tasks.validation: unreachable target reported with distance-to-envelope
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-09 (10th run). `packages/analysis/src/envelope.ts` exports `maxHeightAtDownrange`, `computeEnvelope`, `assessReachability` and their types; `observables.ts` gains `heightAtDownrange`; `shooting-residual.ts` gains `createFlight`. VALIDATION MET: an unreachable target is reported with a distance to the envelope, checked against a closed form the implementation never evaluates. Four unreachable geometries (above the boundary mid-range, past max range on the ground, beyond-and-above, and 2 m outside) each agree with a brute-force minimization over the analytic parabola of safety to better than 1e-3 relative. The boundary height itself matches v0^2/2g - g x^2/2 v0^2 to <1e-6 relative at five abscissae, the max range matches v0^2/g and its 45-degree elevation to <1e-6 / 1e-4 rad, and the touching arc's elevation matches atan(v0^2/gx) to <1e-4 rad. 30 tests in envelope.test.ts plus 10 in observables.test.ts; full suite 1741/1741 across 216 files. SCOPE: this is the 2D reachable set, NOT the scalar ground check. P5.08 already reports maxDownrange/shortfall along the ground, which is this module's distance-to-envelope restricted to y*=0; what was missing was the airborne target, unreachable while sitting well inside the maximum range. TWO DEGENERATE ENDS, both handled rather than worked around. (1) At the launch abscissa the bound is attained by the vertical shot, whose path is a segment and not a graph over x, so 'height where the arc passes this abscissa' is multi-valued; heightAtDownrange's first-crossing rule returns the launch point, which would make the sampled curve appear to RISE from 0 to v0^2/2g. computeEnvelope therefore samples strictly right of the launch point. (2) x = R_max is reached by exactly one elevation, so the feasible theta set collapses to a point and a finite sweep cannot land in it: maxHeightAtDownrange returns null there and loses accuracy over the last sliver before it. The endpoint is (R_max, 0) by construction and is used directly. Without that, a too-far ground target measured its distance to the last abscissa the sweep resolved and came out 4% long (42.5 m against 40.79 m) -- caught by the closed-form reference, which is the reason that reference is brute force over the analytic curve and not a second run of this code. REUSE AND WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT REUSED: the integration is createFlight, factored out of createShootingResidual so the launch-state convention and the terminal-event discriminator stay in one place; the residual discards the path, which is what this task needs. The golden-section contraction is a local near-twin of arcs.ts's locatePeakAngle and is knowingly duplicated: folding them together needs a general 1D minimizer, and that is P5.13, unclaimed. When P5.13 lands, both callers should move onto it and both local copies should go. LIMITATION, stated rather than assumed away: the distance minimization is a coarse sweep plus a contraction, so it finds the global minimum only where squared-distance-to-boundary is single-basined. That holds for the parabola and every library scenario tried; boundarySamples is the knob if a wavier boundary ever appears. NEXT: P5.10 (tangent-linear integration). P5.23's near-envelope conditioning exhibit and P5.15's tangency check both sit on this module.

tasks.title: Tangent-linear (variational) integration: augment state with ∂y/∂μ for selected params
tasks.validation: sensitivity matches FD to 1e-6 on smooth scenario
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-09 (11th run). `packages/analysis/src/tangent-linear.ts` exports `TangentParameter`, `TangentLinearFlight`, `createTangentLinearModel`, `createTangentLinearFlight`, `aimParameters` and `rangeSensitivity`. VALIDATION MET, twice over. Against the criterion's own reference: with drag (C_d = 0.47) at theta = 0.7, dR/dtheta and dR/dv0 agree with a central difference of the whole solve (rtol 1e-12) to better than 1e-6 relative, likewise dT/dtheta and dT/dv0, likewise from a raised launch point, and likewise for a C_d parameter. Against a closed form the module never evaluates: drag-free, dR/dtheta = 2 v0^2 cos 2theta / g and dR/dv0 = 2 v0 sin 2theta / g to 1e-9 relative at four elevations, and dT/dtheta = 2 v0 cos theta / g likewise. 25 tests; full suite 1766/1766 across 217 files; typecheck, lint, lint:deps, app build, bundle budget (65.6 kB gzipped against 300 kB) and both API-doc builds green. MECHANISM: the state is augmented with the variational equations dS/dt = (df/dy) S + df/dmu, S = dy/dmu, so the sensitivities are integrated by the same stepper and inherit its order and its error control. This is the point of the task: P5.05's finite-difference Jacobian carries a noise floor set by the integration tolerance rather than by machine epsilon (its own module comment explains why at length), and differentiating the ODE rather than the solver has no such floor. df/dy comes from model.jacobian when the model has one and from an allocation-free copy of the engine's finiteDifferenceJacobian otherwise -- copied because that function documents itself as not being on a zero-allocation hot path, and here it runs once per rhs evaluation; a test pins the copy against the original so it cannot drift. df/dmu is a central difference of the RHS, which is sound in a way differencing a solve is not: f is an algebraic evaluation with no adaptive controller underneath it. THE EVENT-TIME CORRECTION IS THE SUBSTANCE OF THE TASK, not a refinement on it. S(T) is dy/dmu at FIXED time, and every impact observable is y(T(mu)) with T itself a function of mu, so the total derivative is S(T) + f(T,y(T)) dT/dmu with dT/dmu = -(grad g . S)/(grad g . f), obtained by differentiating g(y(T(mu))) = 0. Measured: on the drag-free 45-degree shot the true dR/dtheta is 0 while the uncorrected number is -163 m/rad -- the correction IS the answer there -- and below the optimum the two carry opposite signs, because raising the elevation lengthens the shot but at fixed time moves the projectile backwards. Both are returned separately (stateSensitivity vs impactSensitivity) rather than one folded into the other, since a fixed-time consumer wants the raw one. The check that catches a sign error in the correction first is the vertical impact sensitivity, which must be exactly zero because the ground pins it. ONE TEST-FIXTURE TRAP WORTH NAMING: dR/dC_d at C_d = 0 is nonzero even though the drag force vanishes there -- df/dC_d is the full drag acceleration per unit coefficient. The obvious fixture drops QuadraticDragForce from the model when cd === 0, and then displacing C_d moves nothing and the sensitivity is a structural zero that reads as physics. The test wires the force at zero coefficient instead. OUT OF SCOPE, rejected at construction rather than mishandled: (1) a terminal event carrying an action, i.e. P4.11's restitution bounce -- S needs its own jump condition across a reset map, S+ = R'(y-) S- + (f+ - R' f-) dT/dmu, and carrying it straight through would be wrong from the first bounce and would look ordinary; (2) more than one terminal event, since the correction differentiates whichever condition fired and the solve report does not say which; (3) grazing impacts, where dT/dmu is genuinely unbounded -- reported as a failure carrying the measured tangency, not as a large number. KNOWN AND STATED: the augmented solve is not the base solve. Its controller sees the sensitivity channels (entries of order 100 m/rad next to positions of order 10 m) and picks a different step sequence, so flight.state agrees with createFlight's to the tolerance rather than bitwise; the test asserts 1e-9 relative rather than equality. NEXT: P5.11 (sensitivity channels UI), whose validation is 'values match variational integration' -- it should read rangeSensitivity(createTangentLinearFlight(problem, aimParameters())(aim)) and must use impactSensitivity, not stateSensitivity. P5.12 (Nelder-Mead) and P5.14 (optimal-angle) can both use dR/dtheta from here as a gradient rather than differencing.

tasks.title: Sensitivity channels UI: dRange/dv₀, dRange/dθ, dRange/dC_d live readouts
tasks.validation: values match variational integration
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-09 (12th run). `packages/ui/src/sensitivity-panel-logic.ts` exports `SENSITIVITY_CHANNELS`, `SensitivityReadout`, `computeSensitivityReadout`, `scenarioAim`, `sensitivityProblem`, `constantDragCoefficient`, `readsDragCoefficient`, `dragCoefficientParameter` and `formatSensitivity`; `sensitivity-panel.tsx` renders the rows; `app.tsx` puts the panel in the default route's analysis drawer, which until now was a placeholder paragraph. VALIDATION MET three ways. (1) The criterion read literally -- the panel's three numbers match an independently constructed `createTangentLinearFlight` + `rangeSensitivity` to 1e-9 relative. (2) Against the drag-free closed form the panel never evaluates: dR/dtheta = 2 v0^2 cos 2theta / g and dR/dv0 = 2 v0 sin 2theta / g to 1e-8 relative at four elevations. (3) Against a central difference of the whole solve with drag on, to 1e-6 relative for all three channels including dR/dC_d. 26 tests; full suite 1792/1792 across 219 files. ONE AUGMENTED SOLVE, NOT THREE: all three channels ride a single tangent-linear solve, which is not only cheaper but the only way they are guaranteed mutually consistent -- a second solve would pick its own step sequence. THE C_d ROW REFUSES RATHER THAN LIES. Two distinct ways to have no dR/dC_d, reported separately: a scenario with no `drag-quadratic` force wired reads the coefficient nowhere, so the variational solve would return an exact 0 that reads as physics ('drag doesn't matter here') and is really an artefact of the force list -- this is exactly the fixture trap P5.10's own tests document, surfaced one layer up; and a `tabulated-reynolds` drag model has no scalar C_d to displace at all. Both render blank with the reason in the row title. THE STEPPER IS ALWAYS dopri5, WHATEVER THE SCENARIO PICKED, and the panel says so on screen when they differ. `createTangentLinearFlight` requires dense output -- without an interpolant the impact row is the last grid point before the ground crossing, so state and sensitivity would both be read off a point that is not on the event surface. Half the selectable steppers (explicit-euler, classical-rk4, ...) expose none, and those are precisely the ones a learner reaches for while studying step-size error, so honouring the scenario's choice would blank the readouts exactly when they are most interesting. Tolerances and step budget still come from the scenario. SPATIAL MODELS ARE EXCLUDED, NOT APPROXIMATED: a 3D aim carries an azimuth as well as an elevation, and printing only dR/dtheta for it would answer a different question than the row label asks. Degenerate aims (zero launch velocity) and shots that never land come back as a `failure` string rather than a throw, since this runs on every commit. COST, MEASURED not assumed: the synchronous augmented solve costs 0.3-2.7 ms on six of the seven presets and 22 ms on the dust grain, whose drag relaxation time is far below the step size. That worst case is one dropped frame per commit, not per frame, and commits are already rate-limited to one per animation frame by the draft/committed split -- moving it to the worker pool has a real message-protocol surface and belongs to a task that says so. Entry bundle 65.6 -> 69.2 kB gzipped (+3.6 kB, the analysis package's shooting/tangent-linear path now reachable from the app), against the 300 kB budget. KNOWN GAP, stated rather than hidden: `rangeSensitivity` differentiates the impact x coordinate while `observables.ts`'s `range` is |x_imp - x_0|; the two agree for any shot launched downrange, which is every scenario the panel is reachable from, and would disagree for one travelling in -x. No CSS was added -- no panel in this app has any yet.

tasks.title: Nelder–Mead implementation (general utility, bounded via transform)
tasks.validation: Rosenbrock 2D to 1e-8; restarts on collapse
tasks.notes:
Done 2026-08-10 (13th run). packages/analysis/src/nelder-mead.ts exports nelderMead plus ObjectiveFunction, NelderMeadBound/Options/Result/Status/Move/Step. Placed in @ballista/analysis per blueprint line 119, which assigns optimization to this package even though brent-root-finder and dense-linear-solve sit in solverkit.

BOTH HALVES OF THE CRITERION MEASURED. Rosenbrock 2D from the literature's (-1.2, 1): f = 2.09e-29 at (1.000000000000004, 1.0000000000000082), 277 iterations / 540 evaluations / 1 restart -- the 1e-8 criterion met by 21 orders, and checked against the closed form f(1,1)=0 rather than a recorded run. Also reached from four other scattered starts, and a 6-D Rosenbrock to <=1e-8.

RESTARTS-ON-COLLAPSE is pinned against McKinnon (1998), not a synthetic case. A correct Nelder-Mead does not collapse on ordinary problems -- Powell's singular function and a 6-D Rosenbrock were both tried while writing this and neither could be made to fail, which is why the initialSimplex option exists: McKinnon's families are defined by their initial simplex, not by a starting point. With tau=2/theta=6/phi=60 and the simplex {(1,1), ((1+sqrt33)/8, (1-sqrt33)/8), (0,0)}: restarts disabled gives 194 iterations that are ALL inside contractions, terminating at the origin with f=0 -- a non-stationary point (df/dy = 1 > 0 there) and strictly worse than the true minimum. With restarts it escapes in 358 iterations / 2 restarts to f = -0.25 at (1.5e-9, -0.4999999975), matching the closed form f(0,-1/2) = -1/4.

THREE DESIGN POINTS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. (1) Bounds are a reparametrization -- tanh two-sided, softplus one-sided -- never clipping, because clipping flattens the objective outside the box and collapses the simplex onto the face, converging to a bound that is not a minimum; a test asserts every evaluated point is strictly inside. (2) All convergence tests read the x images, never the simplex coordinates: near an active bound the transform saturates, so the y-space diameter keeps growing while x has stopped, and a y-space test would never fire. (3) A first pass never returns converged -- convergence means a fresh full-size simplex around the best point failed to improve on it. maxRestarts:0 opts out and is what the collapse test uses to exhibit the failure.

KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: a minimum exactly on a bound is approached asymptotically, reached to double precision in practice (the active-bound test lands on x0 = 0.5 exactly, f = 0.25 against the closed form) but never exactly in general. Real constraint handling is P5.16.

GATE: full suite 1811/1811 across 220 files; typecheck, lint, lint:deps, app build, bundle 69.2 kB against 300 kB, both API-doc builds green. Bundle unchanged because nothing imports this yet -- P5.14/P5.15 are its first consumers.

HOSTED CI: green at 57eb22a (run 31364232725, every step). The first run at 79322ba went red on the P2.40 wall-clock flake (chunked-integration.test.ts:318, maxSliceMs 10.446 against < 10) which is in @ballista/solverkit and unrelated to this task; it was neither re-run nor re-budgeted. 57eb22a differs from 79322ba only by CHANGELOG lines and carries the same nelder-mead sources, so the green run is a full hosted verification of this task's tree.

tasks.title: Golden-section / Brent 1D minimizer
tasks.validation: unimodal test functions to 1e-10
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-10 (14th run). packages/analysis/src/brent-minimize.ts exports goldenSectionMinimize, brentMinimize, ScalarObjective, Minimize1DOptions/Result/Status, SQRT_EPSILON and the two tolerance defaults; 45 tests in brent-minimize.test.ts, full suite 1856/1856 across 221 files. VALIDATION, and the criterion needed splitting rather than asserting flat, because '1e-10' means different things on a smooth minimum and a kinked one. SMOOTH (x*ln x, -cos x, e^x-2x, cosh(x-0.7), (x-1.3)^4): both methods meet 1e-10 on the objective VALUE at the default tolerance, typical error ~1e-17, every expectation a closed form and never a recorded run. LOCATION is a different story: a comparison-only method floors at sqrt(2*eps*|f(x*)|/f''(x*)), and that floor scales with the minimum VALUE, not with |x*| as the folklore version has it. Predicted vs measured for golden section: x*lnx 7.75e-9 vs 5.03e-9, -cos 2.11e-8 vs 1.05e-8, e^x-2x 1.17e-8 vs 1.25e-8, cosh 2.11e-8 vs 1.49e-8 -- every one inside a factor of two, and tightening the tolerance 1000x moves none of them, which is the substantive half of the claim. So 1e-10 in LOCATION is unattainable for those four and the test asserts that it is unattainable rather than asserting around it. It IS attained wherever the floor's numerator vanishes: (x-1.3)^4 and both kinked functions have f(x*)=0 and are located exactly or to ~1e-15. KINKS invert the whole picture and callers need to know: f-f* is O(delta) not O(delta^2), so the default tolerance leaves the VALUE off by ~4e-9 (a hundredfold short of 1e-10) while the location has no floor at all -- tighten xTolAbsolute for a kinked objective, do not bother for a smooth one. Both halves are asserted. brentMinimize also beats the floor that stops golden section, by one to three orders (e.g. -cos 4.5e-12 against a 2.1e-8 floor), because interpolation fits three points that can sit outside the flat region instead of comparing points inside it; on an exact quadratic it returns the vertex to the last bit in 6 evaluations. Cost: 9-15 evaluations against golden section's 43-45 on the smooth set. NOT DONE, and the specific next step for whoever picks this up: envelope.ts's goldenSectionMaximum and arcs.ts's locatePeakAngle are hand-rolled contractions whose own comments say they should move onto P5.13 once it lands. Both negate to minimize. That migration is deliberately not in this commit -- it is a change to two working exhibit paths with golden-trajectory implications, and P5.13's criterion does not cover them.

tasks.title: Optimal-angle problem: argmax_θ range with drag (compare to 45° folklore)
tasks.validation: quadratic-drag optimum < 45° (typically 30–43° by regime); exhibit shows shift vs Π
tasks.notes:
Done 2026-08-13 (15th run). packages/analysis/src/optimal-angle.ts exports maximizeRange plus NO_IMPACT, OptimalAngleOptions, OptimalAngleStatus and OptimalAngle. Coarse 25-point sweep over [minAngle, maxAngle] to bracket the interior maximum, then P5.13's brentMinimize on the negated range -- the consumer that module was written for, and the one range-root.ts's DRAG_FREE_PEAK_ANGLE doc names. A sweep rather than two-point bracket expansion because an inadmissible region (aims that do not land inside tspan) can sit anywhere in the interval and an expansion strategy cannot tell 'no impact' from 'very short'. Negating to maximize is exact in IEEE-754 (one sign bit), and the inadmissibility conventions coincide: brentMinimize reads non-finite as +inf = avoid, which is what 'no impact' should mean for a maximization too. at-bound and no-impact are statuses distinct from converged, because an optimum pinned to an elevation cap is a property of the bounds and not of the physics.

VALIDATION (criterion: 'quadratic-drag optimum < 45 deg (typically 30-43 deg by regime); exhibit shows shift vs Pi'). The exhibit is packages/analysis/src/optimal-angle.test.ts (15 tests), following the P4.09/P4.22/P4.34 precedent of a documented test module rather than new UI. Real quadratic-drag integrations (createPlanarProjectileModel + QuadraticDragForce, dopri5 rtol 1e-12 atol 1e-14), 1 kg / 5 cm sphere at Cd 0.47, Pi from the engine's own dimensionlessPi. MEASURED theta* by regime: v0=10 Pi=0.0231 -> 44.8630 deg; 20 / 0.0922 -> 44.4713; 30 / 0.2075 -> 43.8755; 50 / 0.5764 -> 42.3232; 70 / 1.1297 -> 40.6289; 100 / 2.3055 -> 38.2736; 150 / 5.1875 -> 35.1805; 200 / 9.2222 -> 32.9375; 300 / 20.7499 -> 29.9500. Strictly below 45 deg everywhere and strictly monotone decreasing in Pi. The task's 30-43 deg band is asserted over 0.5 <= Pi <= 10, which it holds across; BOTH TAILS LEAVE THE BAND and each is its own assertion rather than a row dropped to tidy the claim -- towards 45 deg as Pi -> 0 (44.86 deg at Pi 0.023, the correct limit) and below 30 deg past Pi ~ 20 (29.95 deg). Drag-free control checked first, analytically and through the integrator: both recover pi/4 (analytic search lands on the exact double; integrated gives 45.000000 deg and 254.92905324448225 m against the closed form's 254.92905324448208 m), so the drag measurements are not confounded with a biased search. Cost 25 sweep integrations + 6-15 refinement. Peak breadth measured: +/-5 deg off the optimum costs 0.86-1.51% of the range, and the loss DECREASES with Pi -- the regimes whose optimum moves most are the least sensitive to missing it.

FIVE PERTURBATIONS applied, run and reverted, table in the test file header: refinement discarded -> 5 of 15 fail; sign dropped so it minimizes -> 6; non-impact scored 0 -> 1; at-bound reported converged -> 1; last sweep sample accumulated instead of set to maxAngle -> 1. tasks.title: Min-energy targeting: minimize v₀ subject to hit (θ free) via nested Brent/shooting
tasks.validation: KKT-style check: range envelope tangency at solution
tasks.notes:
Done 2026-08-10 (16th run). packages/analysis/src/min-energy.ts exports minimumSpeedToHit plus MinEnergyOptions, MinEnergyStatus and MinEnergySolution. The formulation is the substance of the task: minimizing v0 subject to a hit is NOT a shooting solve with an extra unknown -- the hit condition is one equation in two unknowns, so above the threshold speed TWO elevations hit (P5.08's arcs) and below it none do. The minimum is where they merge, which is exactly where the target sits ON the reachability envelope. So the whole problem reduces to solving envelopeHeight(x*; v0) = y* for v0, and that IS the task's KKT criterion rather than a proxy for it: target-on-boundary is stationarity, arcs-merging is the degeneracy of an active constraint.

NESTING, as the task specifies: outer brentRoot (solverkit) on launch speed, inner maximization over elevation via P5.09's maxHeightAtDownrange. Nothing re-derived. Bracketed from smart-init's dragFreeAim speed sqrt(g(dy+R)), which is a RIGOROUS lower bound, not a guess -- a dissipative force model can only shrink the reachable set at a given speed. The margin function needed a second branch and that branch is not a detail: maxHeightAtDownrange returns null past the maximum range, and for a GROUND target the answer sits exactly in that hole (at x = R_max the feasible theta set collapses to a point a finite sweep cannot find). The continuation -(y* + (x* - R_max(v))) agrees with the first branch at the join (both give -y* there), is monotone in v, and reduces to R_max(v) - x* for y*=0, which is the correct ground-target equation. R_max comes from P5.14's maximizeRange, so the phase's own ladder is what this stands on.

VALIDATION (criterion: 'KKT-style check: range envelope tangency at solution'). The exhibit is min-energy.test.ts, 26 tests, following the P4.09/P4.22/P4.34/P5.14 documented-test-module precedent. Tangency is checked THREE independent ways because stationarity alone only proves the root-find converged: (1) target lies on the envelope, re-measured through maxHeightAtDownrange rather than trusting the reported margin, |margin| < 1e-6 m; (2) GEOMETRIC tangency -- the optimal arc and the envelope have the same slope where they meet; drag-free this is checked against the closed-form parabola slope -g x/v0^2, which the implementation never computes, and with drag against the measured envelope slope, agreeing to < 5e-3 against a slope of ~-0.7; (3) MINIMALITY -- assessReachability, a separate entry point, confirms 0.999*v misses and 1.001*v hits. Drag-free closed form recovered exactly over four geometries: ground target gives 45.000000 deg and v0 = sqrt(g*x); (dx,dy) = (100,30), (100,-20), (60,60), (250,5) all match sqrt(g(dy+R)) and pi/4+phi/2. Suite 1897/1897 across 223 files (was 1871/222 -- the 26 new tests and nothing else moved); typecheck, lint, lint:deps, app build and bundle budget (69.2 kB gzipped against 300 kB, unchanged -- nothing imports this yet) all green.

TWO DOC CLAIMS WERE WRITTEN FROM THEORY, MEASURED FALSE, AND CORRECTED -- recorded because it is the 15th run's failure mode recurring and being caught this time. (a) The theta note claimed a sqrt(eps) resolution floor from the merged-arc degeneracy. Wrong twice over: the reported theta is the inner envelope-height maximizer, a better-conditioned problem than the hit condition, and its measured floor is 7.4e-10 rad for (100,30) -- far finer than sqrt(eps) ~ 1.5e-8. It is also GEOMETRY-DEPENDENT, which a single measurement hid: (100,30) 7.378e-10, (100,-20) 9.974e-9, (60,60) 1.277e-8, (250,5) 1.618e-8, worst for flat long shots whose height maximum is broadest. An intermediate draft asserted 1e-8 -- the first geometry's figure generalized to three it had never been measured on -- and two rows failed it. The bound is now above the worst measured row. (b) The speedTol doc warned against tightening below the inner maximization's noise; measured, it is honoured across eight orders (1e-4 -> 6.9e-5, 1e-6 -> 5.4e-7, 1e-8 -> 8.5e-9, 1e-10 -> 6.6e-11, 1e-12 -> 5.2e-13) at ~7 outer iterations per decade. Both tables are in the test file.

ALSO CORRECTED DURING THE RUN: the first implementation reported 'below-bracket' for every drag-free problem, because there the drag-free lower bound IS the answer and the margin at it is zero-to-rounding, which read as 'already reachable'. Precisely the wrong answer in the case the module is most confident about. Fixed by contracting the bracket downwards to find a genuine sign change rather than thresholding a metres-valued margin whose scale this module does not know. arcSeparation was also reading a discrete trajectory row instead of the interpolated crossing and returned null at every tangency; it now uses heightAtDownrange.

COST, measured: ~100-200 integrations for a drag-free solve, ~1100 with drag at speedTol 1e-6, ~2400 at 1e-12. Each outer iteration is a full inner maximization, so this is not a per-frame call. NOT DONE and the specific next step for whoever picks this up: nothing imports minimumSpeedToHit yet -- it has no UI and no worker-pool job. P5.18 (optimization job type with iteration streaming) is the natural consumer and is the next todo by seq after P5.16/P5.17. Also unaddressed: arcSeparation is resolution-limited at its fixed 1e-3 rad probe step and reports 0 at every tangency, which is honest but coarse; if a caller ever needs the actual arc half-width, solve for the two arcs with P5.08 instead of widening this.

tasks.title: Constraint handling: bounds on θ, v₀; penalty + projection strategies
tasks.validation: constrained solutions respect bounds; active-set reported
tasks.notes:
DONE 2026-08-11 (17th run). `packages/analysis/src/constraints.ts` exports the box-bounds vocabulary (`AimBounds`, `validateAimBounds`, `projectAim`, `aimActiveSet`, `boundsPenaltyRows`, `withBoundsPenalty`) and the `constrainedShooting` entry point the validation criterion is stated against. Both halves of that criterion are checked from the OUTSIDE in constraints.test.ts: feasibility is recomputed with `aimActiveSet` from the RETURNED aim and the bounds, never read off a flag the solver set about itself, so a solver reporting `feasible: true` on an out-of-box aim would fail. Suite 1930/1930 across 224 files (was 1897/223 -- the 33 new tests and nothing else moved); typecheck, lint, lint:deps and build all green.

MEASUREMENTS. Exhibit problem: 1 kg 5 cm sphere, Cd 0.47, point target 400 m downrange; unconstrained answer theta 0.6475 rad, v0 95.47 m/s in 3 iterations. (1) PROJECTION respects a binding cap exactly -- v0 = 70.000000000000 against a 70 m/s cap, active set reports speed:'upper' theta:'free', status 'blocked-by-bound', and the 116.76 m of miss left over is the honest answer that the target is out of reach at that cap. Tightening the cap raises the irreducible miss monotonically: 116.76 / 92.33 / 68.59 m at 70 / 75 / 80 m/s. A non-binding cap (200 m/s) reproduces the unconstrained aim to 9 decimals with activeCount 0. (2) The CORNER case is what the projected-arc stall test exists for: with thetaMax 0.6 AND speedMax 70 both below the unconstrained answer, the Newton direction leaves the box in both coordinates, the projected displacement is zero for every alpha, and the solve stops in <= 2 iterations with newton.status 'stalled'. Without that test it burns 25 backtracks and reports 'line-search-failed' at a constrained stationary point.

THE PENALTY MEASUREMENT REFUTED THE THEORY THE FIRST DRAFT WAS WRITTEN FROM, and the doc was corrected before the exhibit was written. The textbook exterior-penalty story is a violation of order 1/sqrt(w) shrinking smoothly with weight. Swept across ten orders on the speed-capped solve the behaviour is NON-MONOTONIC with a usable window in the middle: w 1e0-1e2 grossly infeasible (9.35 -> 2.23 m/s over the cap, and 1e2 does not converge at all); w 1e3-1e7 feasible, landing ~5e-11 INSIDE the bound; w 3e7-1e9 infeasible again (1.9e-5 -> 1.2e-6). The middle plateau is not the smooth balance the 1/sqrt(w) argument describes -- the hinge is exactly zero inside the box, so once feasible the penalized problem is locally identical to the unconstrained one and pushes back out, the penalty rows pull it back, and the iteration chatters onto the face and stops there, behaving like an inexact projection. At the top end the sqrt(w) rows degrade the Jacobian's conditioning and MORE weight is LESS feasible, which 1/sqrt(w) cannot express at all. DEFAULT_PENALTY_WEIGHT = 1e6 is picked from inside that measured window rather than from the argument. The window was measured on ONE problem and the doc says so.

WHAT IS NOT DONE. The projection makes every ITERATE feasible, not every EVALUATION: shootingJacobian's difference stencil is not projected and reaches one difference step past an active face -- measured at exactly 5 of 56 evaluations, every one 4.8444e-4 m/s past a 70 m/s cap, which is the speed column's difference step and nothing larger. Harmless where the residual is defined just outside the box, as it is here; NOT harmless at a bound marking the model's domain (a non-negative speed), where the stencil would evaluate an aim with no trajectory. Filed as P0.92 rather than fixed mid-task. Also not done, and deliberately: no general nonlinear constraints, no working-set iteration, no Lagrange multipliers, no KKT test beyond what aimActiveSet reports -- a box on two variables does not justify an active-set QP. P5.06's unconstrained path is untouched: the projected-displacement stall test applies only when a projection is supplied, and a regression test pins the bare solve at 3 iterations.

tasks.title: Wind-robust aim: optimize expected miss under wind uncertainty (preview of Phase 6 coupling)
tasks.validation: robust aim differs from nominal in headwind-vs-gust scenario (measured)
tasks.notes:
DONE 2026-08-11 (18th run). `packages/analysis/src/robust-aim.ts` exports WindScenario, RiskMeasure, VaryAim, ScenarioMiss, RobustAimOptions, RobustAimStatus, RobustAimResult, robustAim and robustAimIsFeasible. Suite 1951/1951 across 225 files (was 1930/224 -- the 21 new tests and nothing else moved); typecheck, lint, lint:deps green; app build green and check-bundle-size 69.2 kB gzipped against a 300 kB budget.

VALIDATION MET -- "robust aim differs from nominal in headwind-vs-gust scenario (measured)". Exhibit: 1 kg 5 cm sphere, Cd 0.47, point target 400 m downrange, nominal headwind -6 m/s against a -16 m/s gust, equally likely, launch speed held at the nominal solve's 104.9387636174 m/s. Nominal theta 0.6339044229 with miss 2.2e-12 m (a genuine hit, recomputed from the returned aim rather than read off the inner solver's flag). ROBUST theta 0.5584788851: 0.0754255378 rad LOWER, 4.32 degrees. RMS miss 45.489 m -> 43.106 m. The trade in full: 2.669 m given up under the nominal wind to recover 3.429 m under the gust (64.331 -> 60.902).

THE DIFFERENCE IS PINNED FROM FOUR INDEPENDENT DIRECTIONS, because a mere difference is what any perturbation-shaped bug also produces. (1) It vanishes EXACTLY -- shift === 0, not merely small -- on a one-scenario ensemble, where the risk IS the miss. (2) Monotone in gust severity: 0.01522 / 0.02178 / 0.02839 / 0.03504 / 0.07543 rad at -7 / -8 / -9 / -10 / -16 m/s. (3) Monotone in gust PROBABILITY: robust theta 0.5706031 / 0.5629515 / 0.5584789 as the gust goes 1:9 -> 3:9 -> 9:9. (4) At a mild gust it is visibly a TRADE, not a drift: at -7 m/s the robust shot goes LONG under the nominal wind (a sign flip from exactly 0) in order to fall less short under the gust. Weight scaling is bit-identical, not close: [1,1] and [7,7] agree to the last bit because normalization precedes any arithmetic.

THE TWO-VARIABLE PROBLEM IS UNBOUNDED AND THAT IS PHYSICS, NOT A BUG, so it is documented at the top of the module and pinned by a test rather than left as a footnote a later reader might 'fix'. Wind acts for as long as the shot is airborne, so flatter-and-faster is always more robust and nothing in the objective pushes back: as v0 -> infinity with theta -> 0 the time of flight and the risk both tend to zero, the infimum is 0, and it is not attained. Measured: an unbounded solve walks off to theta ~3.1e-4 rad, v0 ~3.59e3 m/s, cutting RMS miss to 0.60 m and still descending when the iteration cap stops it. Hence `vary`: "theta" holds the launch speed fixed -- the well-posed form, the one a real launcher faces since speed is a property of the machine, and the ONLY one with an interior optimum. Bounds make the answer finite but NOT interior: at speedMax 110 the minimizer sits on the cap at 110.000000 with risk 33.509 m, feasibility recomputed via P5.16's aimActiveSet.

MEASURE ORDERING measured rather than argued: |shift| = 0.04233 rad (mean-absolute) < 0.07543 (mean-square) < 0.07856 (worst-case). Mean-absolute weights a large miss linearly and so tolerates it; worst-case sees nothing else. All three are reported in METRES so they are mutually comparable -- mean-square is reported as RMS for that reason, and the square root is monotone so it does not move the minimizer. Mean-square is also the only SMOOTH one: squaring removes the kink |miss| has where a scenario's miss changes sign.

TWO THINGS FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, not assumed. (a) The default seed for a pinned component comes from a full two-variable Newton solve, not from smartInitialAim directly: seeding the held speed from the initial guess pins it below the speed the target needs and reports "nominal-failed" on a perfectly solvable problem, because a launch speed that cannot reach the target makes every elevation a miss. First measured as three spurious nominal-failed exhibits. (b) At the -16 m/s gust the target is out of reach ALTOGETHER at that speed (max range ~339 m), so the robust aim there is damage limitation and worst-case degenerates to maximizing range under the gust; the -7 m/s exhibit exists to show the genuinely two-sided balance.

Outer loop is P5.11's nelderMead, derivative-free on purpose: a gradient needs P5.05's Jacobian once per scenario per step and that Jacobian is rank 1 under a ground-impact terminal event, so the assembled system is ill-conditioned in the direction the risk measure cares least about. Bounds reuse P5.16's AimBounds rather than restating them. Wind is DISSIPATIVE -- it enters through the drag force's relative velocity -- so every solve stays on the embedded RK path the P5.04 residual already requires; no symplectic scheme is admissible here and none is used. NOT DONE: no UI surface (that is P5.18's worker/streaming job and P5.19's convergence plot), no gradient-based alternative, and no continuous wind distribution -- the ensemble is a discrete weighted quadrature, which is the Phase 6 coupling this task is a preview of.

tasks.title: Optimization job type in worker pool with iteration streaming
tasks.validation: UI shows live convergence trace; cancel works
tasks.notes:
Done 2026-08-11 (19th run). Criterion -- 'UI shows live convergence trace; cancel works' -- met by `#/inverse-solver`, which runs a Newton shooting solve in a real Worker and fills a trace table row by row as the iterations arrive.

PIECES. `newtonShooting` gains an `onIteration` option; the three `history.push` sites became one `record()` helper so the stream and `history` cannot drift apart (a listener sees exactly `result.history`, in order, terminal iterations included). `packages/runtime/src/optimize-job.ts`: `OptimizeJob`/`OptimizeIteration`/`OptimizeJobResult`/`runOptimizeJob`, resolving a `ScenarioSpec` the same way `runSweepPoint` does. `worker-pool.ts`: `runOptimize`, `OptimizeRequest`/`OptimizeIterationMessage`/`OptimizeResponse`/`postOptimizeResult`/`OptimizeCancelledError`. `optimize-worker-entry.ts`. `packages/ui/src/convergence-trace-panel{,-logic}.ts(x)`. `packages/app/src/{optimize-worker-factory.ts,inverse-solver-route.tsx}` + `routes.ts`/`main.tsx`.

FOUR DECISIONS WORTH NOT RE-LITIGATING. (1) EVERYTHING CROSSING THE WIRE IS PLAIN DATA -- `OptimizeSolverOptions` re-declares the numeric subset of `NewtonShootingOptions` rather than accepting it whole, because that interface carries `projection`, a function, and a function is a `DataCloneError` at `postMessage`, not a type error. A test structured-clones the job, every streamed iteration and the result. (2) CANCEL TERMINATES THE WORKER AND REFILLS THE SLOT. A solve is a synchronous loop of trajectory integrations, so a worker mid-solve never drains its message queue and cannot be asked to stop; the alternatives are a SharedArrayBuffer flag (needs COOP/COEP headers this app does not set) or chunking a correct solver into macrotasks. The pool's `workers` array became mutable so the pool survives a cancel -- a test cancels, then runs another job on the same pool. (3) ITERATIONS ARE NOT THROTTLED, unlike a sweep chunk's progress: a Newton solve produces ~20 of them and each is a datum the P5.19 plot draws, not a progress tick, so dropping any would put holes in the thing being streamed. (4) ONE WORKER, NOT THE POOL -- iteration k+1 starts from k's iterate, so there is nothing to fan out; what the pool contributes is that the work is off the main thread.

THE SUBTLE BUG THAT WAS AVOIDED, and the test that would have caught it: `NewtonShootingStep` carries no iterate, so `runOptimizeJob` recovers it from the last residual evaluation -- correct only when the line search accepted a trial. On the two paths that record a step without accepting one (`alpha === 0`: blocked, line-search-failed) the last evaluation is a REJECTED aim, and reporting it would put a point on the trace the solve never visited. Reproduced deterministically with `maxBacktracks: 0` from `theta 1.5, v0 20`, which fails Armijo on iteration 0; the test asserts the reported aim is the initial one and that `evaluations > 1`, so 'last evaluated' would have differed. The accepted-but-short case is pinned separately with `armijoC: 0.99, maxBacktracks: 6`, which accepts alpha = 0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.5, 0.5, 1, 1, 1 -- default options accept alpha = 1 throughout and would never exercise the distinction. Every reported iterate is re-evaluated through the residual and checked to reproduce the step's own `nextMerit` to 9 dp.

THE LIVE PART IS TESTED AS LIVE. The panel takes `runOptimize` as a prop, so its test drives a controllable runner: it emits one iteration, asserts the DOM has one row WHILE THE PROMISE IS STILL PENDING, emits another, asserts two. A fake that resolved immediately could not tell a trace that fills in from one that appears at the end, which is the whole criterion. Cancel is asserted to abort the signal, keep the rows already shown, drop iterations still in flight afterwards (a real race -- the reducer ignores them), report as 'cancelled' rather than 'failed', and leave the panel able to solve again. The route test fakes only the thread, running the real `postOptimizeResult` one message per macrotask, so route -> pool -> job -> stream -> DOM is exercised end to end.

MEASUREMENTS. Suite 1994/1994 across 229 files, up from 1951/225 -- 43 new tests (16 runtime, 23 ui, 4 app), nothing else moved. typecheck, lint, `lint:deps` (1341 modules) green. App build green; Vite split `optimize-worker-entry` into its own 118.12 kB chunk, which is the separate-entry decision paying off -- merged with the sweep entry, every sweep worker would pull in `@ballista/analysis`. `check-bundle-size` 71.2 kB gzipped against the 300 kB budget (was 69.2 kB; +2.0 kB is the panel and route).

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: the trace is a table, not a plot -- log||F|| vs iteration is P5.19, which should read `TraceRow` rather than re-derive it. The target and the initial aim are fixed constants on the route (P5.21 makes the target draggable, P5.22 the unknowns selectable).

tasks.title: Convergence trace plot: log‖F‖ vs iteration (Newton quadratic tail visible)
tasks.validation: slope doubling per iter near root (assert last-3 ratio)
tasks.notes:
Done 2026-08-12 (20th run). Criterion -- 'slope doubling per iter near root (assert last-3 ratio)' -- met and asserted on real solves, not on a synthetic sequence: `newton-convergence-order.test.ts` measures 1.999 for the drag-free problem against a closed-form target and 2.003 with drag and wind.

PIECES. `packages/analysis/src/newton-convergence-order.ts`: `NewtonTracePoint`, `plottableTracePoints`, `meritLogSlopes`, `meritSlopeRatios`, `finalMeritSlopeRatio`. `packages/viz/src/lazy-plotly-pane.ts`: `NewtonTraceCurve`, `buildNewtonTraceFigure`. `packages/ui/src/convergence-trace-panel-logic.ts`: `traceMeritPoints`, `traceSlopeRatio`, `formatSlopeRatio`, wired into `convergence-trace-panel.tsx` above the existing table.

WHY A RATIO OF SLOPES, NOT A FITTED EXPONENT. Squaring the residual is doubling in log space: with L = log10||F||, quadratic convergence gives L(k+1) = 2 L(k) + c, so the plotted slope s(k) = L(k+1) - L(k) satisfies s(k+1) = 2 s(k). The unknown constant C cancels out of the ratio, which a least-squares fit of p in ||F(k+1)|| = C ||F(k)||^p would need. The window is three residuals because that is where the asymptotic law is in force; a fit over the whole history is dragged towards 1 by the pre-asymptotic head. Zero and non-finite residuals are dropped rather than clamped (a log axis has nowhere to put ||F|| = 0), and a ratio whose denominator is a stalled step (alpha = 0 repeats the residual exactly) is omitted rather than reported as infinity.

THE FINDING THAT WILL LOOK LIKE A BUG IN THE PLOT, PINNED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED. The quadratic tail does not continue forever. The first attempt at the criterion test forced `residualTolerance: 1e-10` and measured 0.892, not 2 -- because that buys one Newton iteration past the point where the trajectory integrator can still resolve the miss distance (1.782e-8 -> 2.275e-13 is ~5 decades where doubling predicts ~11). Nothing is wrong with the solver or the diagnostic; the sequence has left the regime the law describes. At the default tolerance the same solve stops at 1.782e-8 and reports 1.999. A test asserts the floor-limited case is < 1.5 so the effect stays documented, and `formatSlopeRatio` deliberately prints the number without a 'quadratic / not quadratic' verdict for the same reason.

THE ALIGNMENT THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG. A `TraceRow` describes a step: `merit` is ||F|| at the iterate it started from, `nextMerit` at the iterate it produced. So row k plots at k+1, plus one point at the front for the initial aim. Plotting `merit` at k shifts the whole curve one iteration left and makes the solve look a step faster than it was. Adjacent rows share a residual, so taking `nextMerit` from every row and `merit` from only the first counts each exactly once; a test asserts n rows give n+1 points.

MIXED AXES ARE DELIBERATE. Every neighbouring figure in `lazy-plotly-pane.ts` is log-log because its x is a continuous quantity whose power law is a straight line. Here x is an iteration count and the feature is a curve that steepens, so x stays linear -- a log x-axis would flatten exactly what the plot is for.

A REGRESSION THE EXISTING SUITE CAUGHT, WORTH KNOWING ABOUT. Importing `plottableTracePoints` into `lazy-plotly-pane.ts` by value put all of `@ballista/analysis` into that module's static graph and `lazy-plotly-pane.bundle.test.ts` (P3.30) failed immediately: initial chunk 5 kB -> 141 kB. The import is now type-only and the predicate inlined, with a test importing the analysis version and asserting the two agree case for case over 0, -1, NaN, +/-Infinity and MIN_VALUE, so the duplication cannot drift. Any future viz module reaching into analysis should expect the same.
