tasks.title: Basin-of-attraction visual: initial-guess grid colored by converged solution
tasks.validation: two-arc basins render; boundary fractal-ish structure noted
tasks.notes:
Done 2026-08-12 (21st run). Criterion -- 'two-arc basins render; boundary fractal-ish structure noted' -- met on the first half and MEASURED THE OTHER WAY on the second, which is the finding of this task.

TWO-ARC BASINS RENDER. `sweepBasins` walks a grid of initial guesses through `newtonShooting` and labels each cell by the arc it converged to. Drag-and-wind problem, target at 140 m, 17x17 grid over theta0 in [0.05, 1.5] rad and v0 in [40, 80] m/s: 136 low, 153 high, zero unconverged, zero failed. Within every row each 'low' cell starts from a shallower guess than every 'high' cell -- asserted against the elevation ordering rather than against the sign convention that produced the label, so a swap could not pass by agreeing with itself. `buildBasinFigure` draws it; `BasinPanel` mounts it with a legend and the boundary readout, and a jsdom test asserts the spec that reaches the pane is the real one.

THE BOUNDARY IS NOT FRACTAL FOR THE SOLVER WE SHIP, AND THE NUMBERS SAY SO. Boundary cells per row (n x boundaryFraction, the scale-free form -- an n x n grid has n^2 cells so a k-per-row boundary has fraction k/n):

  shipped solver      n=9 -> 2.000   n=17 -> 2.000   n=33 -> 2.000
  rankTolerance 1e-14 n=9 -> 1.823   n=17 -> 2.556   n=33 -> 3.432

Exactly two cells per row at every refinement is the pair straddling a single curve crossed once: a smooth boundary with nothing at the finer scales to find. Set `rankTolerance` below the ground-impact rank deficiency P5.05 measured at ~1e-11, so the near-null singular value is retained instead of truncated, and the same sweep speckles -- isolated cells of the opposite label well inside both basins -- and the count grows with refinement instead of holding. So the fractal-ish boundary the criterion expected is what an UNGUARDED Newton produces, and P5.06's truncated-SVD minimum-norm step is precisely what removes it. This is a scaling observation over three levels and is deliberately not reported as a box-counting dimension, which three levels do not support (blueprint 8.4).

THE CLASSIFICATION RULE. A converged aim is labelled by the SIGN OF dR/dtheta there, at fixed speed. The branch boundary is by definition the maximum-range elevation, the point where that derivative changes sign, so the sign is the definition of the label rather than an approximation of it. Cost is one central difference (2 residual evaluations) per cell against a full `solveArcs` sweep per cell -- on a 33x33 grid, ~2000 extra integrations rather than ~50000. The difference step is 1e-4 rad, sized against the adaptive integrator's own accuracy rather than against sqrt(eps): differencing at 1e-8 would measure the error tolerance instead of the physics. A slope that cannot be measured, or is exactly zero, yields 'unconverged' rather than a guessed label -- a cell sitting on the peak genuinely belongs to neither arc.

A CELL IS JUDGED ON DOWNRANGE MISS, NOT ON `result.converged`. The shooting Jacobian's vertical row is zero for every aim, so against a raised target the vertical component of F is irreducible and the solver's expected terminal state is 'stalled' with an honestly non-zero residual. Keying the map off `converged` would render a uniform sheet of failures and show nothing.

PIECES. `packages/analysis/src/basin-of-attraction.ts`: `sweepBasins`, `linearSamples`, `rangeSlopeAt`, `censusOf`, `hasTwoArcBasins`, `boundaryFraction`, `refineBoundaryFraction`. `packages/viz/src/lazy-plotly-pane.ts`: `PlotlyHeatmapTrace`, `BASIN_CLASS_INDEX`, `BASIN_COLOURS`, `buildBasinFigure`. `packages/ui/src/basin-panel-logic.ts` and `basin-panel.tsx`.

WHY THE HEATMAP SCALE IS BANDED. `z` holds class indices, not a measured quantity, so Plotly's default autoscaled continuous scale would interpolate across a boundary that is a step and paint cells either side of the seam an arc that is neither low nor high. Each class owns a closed band, zmin/zmax are pinned to the index range, and zsmooth is off. A 'failed' cell maps to null and renders as a hole rather than as a fourth colour: a starting guess with no trajectory at all is not an outcome, and colouring it would suggest the solver reached one. `BasinOutcome` is imported as a type only and `BASIN_CLASS_INDEX` is declared in viz rather than imported, for the reason `lazy-plotly-pane.bundle.test.ts` pins -- a value import from @ballista/analysis put 141 kB into the initial chunk.

WHAT IS NOT DONE. No app route mounts `BasinPanel`; `runSweep` is an injected prop and nothing supplies it outside the tests. Wiring it needs a sweep job in @ballista/runtime's worker protocol -- a sweep is n^2 Newton solves and must not run on the UI thread -- which is its own change. That is the first thing the next session should pick up if it wants the map in the app; P5.21 (draggable target marker) is the next roadmap task either way and touches the same solver surface.

tasks.validation: drag→solution < 200 ms typical (measured)
tasks.notes:

CRITERION MET. Measured in packages/analysis/src/arcs.test.ts, describe 'P5.21 validation: drag->solution latency': solveArcs timed over 15 distinct drops across the reachable band of a planar quadratic-drag shot at 60 m/s, TIGHT_TOL. Median 19.2 ms, slowest 50.9 ms, fastest 15.2 ms on the development container -- about an order of magnitude inside the 200 ms budget. The assertion is the criterion (median < 200 ms), not the measured number, so a slower machine still passes while a regression that ate the headroom would not; the slowest solve is backstopped ten times looser so a GC pause on a loaded runner cannot fail the suite.

Design: solve-on-drop, not solve-on-move. A pointer move fires tens of times a second and each solve is a pair of Brent root-finds over full integrations, so solving per move would queue work faster than it retires and the marker would lag the pointer by a growing margin. Dragging is pure state; exactly one solve per drop, asserted. A second drop aborts the solve still in flight, and a solve answering after the user resumed dragging is discarded rather than repainted onto a target they can see they have left. The drag is tracked in world metres, not pixels, so a resize mid-drag cannot silently move the target.

tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-12. packages/analysis/src/trajectory-designer.ts exports designTrajectory(problem, request, options), with the three locks as a discriminated union on the unknown so 'lock any two' is a type constraint rather than a runtime arity check. (v0, R) -> theta delegates wholly to P5.08's solveArcs, inheriting its two answers, measured peak and low/high labels. (theta, R) -> v0 is the only new numerics: range is monotone in speed at fixed elevation, so no peak and at most one root, found by brentRoot bracketed by geometric expansion from the drag-free inverse v0 = sqrt(gR/sin 2theta) — exact without drag, a strict under-estimate with it — following min-energy.ts's speed-bracketing precedent. R is downrange displacement from the launch point, not a world abscissa, so raised and displaced launchers stay consistent across all three locks. Infeasibility is a reported value (unreachable, degenerate-elevation, non-positive-range, max-iterations), never a throw; a malformed aim still throws, so a caller bug and an out-of-reach target cannot be confused. VALIDATION: criterion is 'all three lock combinations function' — 17 tests in trajectory-designer.test.ts. Each lock is checked against the drag-free closed form R = v0^2 sin2theta/g and its two analytic inverses (plus R/sqrt(2h/g) for the raised zero-elevation case, where no seed formula exists). Cross-lock round trips run with drag ON deliberately: without drag, three independent re-derivations of the same formula would agree while all being wrong. Arc labels checked against flight time, not elevation ordering, which is true by construction. tasks.title: Ill-conditioning exhibit: grazing target near envelope, Jacobian condition number readout
tasks.validation: cond(J) spikes near envelope (plotted); solver warns
tasks.notes:
Done 2026-08-15 (24th run). packages/analysis/src/ill-conditioning.ts (solveArcsWithConditioning, sweepEnvelopeConditioning, conditioningLevel, geometricMargins, logLogSlope), exported from @ballista/analysis, plus buildConditionNumberFigure in packages/viz/src/lazy-plotly-pane.ts.

WHICH JACOBIAN, because the obvious one is the wrong one. Not P5.05's 2x2 d(F)/d(theta, v0): the ground-impact event pins its vertical row (measured <1e-8 there), so it is rank 1 for EVERY aim, its condition number is about 1e11 everywhere, and plotting it against envelope proximity draws a flat line. That is a fact about the terminal event, not about the envelope. The fold the blueprint means ("the envelope is a fold: the two solution arcs merge and det J -> 0") lives in the fixed-speed problem P5.08 solves -- one unknown theta, one equation R(theta) = R_target -- where the Jacobian is the 1x1 dR/dtheta and det J genuinely vanishes, because the envelope IS the maximum of R(theta) and the derivative of a smooth function at its maximum is zero. Free v0 as well and there is no fold at all: a target past the envelope at one speed is simply reached at a higher one.

THE RATE IS THE CONTENT, AND IT IS A SQUARE ROOT. Near the quadratic maximum a target short by s is hit at theta_p +/- sqrt(2s/|R''|), so dR/dtheta at the root goes like s^(+1/2), the sensitivity |dtheta/dR| like s^(-1/2), and the arc separation like s^(+1/2). Measured log-log fits: sensitivity -0.4999 drag-free and -0.5009 with cd 0.47; separation +0.5000 and +0.4999. The drag runs are the ones that earn the word "exhibit" -- a law appearing only drag-free could be an artifact of the closed form rather than of the fold. Practical reading: kappa only doubles per factor of four in margin, so the blow-up is real but gentle, which is exactly why quantifying it beats hand-waving it.

THRESHOLDS KEY OFF THE DIMENSIONLESS RELATIVE CONDITION NUMBER, NOT THE rad/m SENSITIVITY. An absolute rate is scale-dependent -- the same well-posed shot reads 1.5e-3 rad/m at 60 m/s and something else entirely at 600 -- so no absolute threshold separates "ordinary" from "at the fold" across problems. Drag-free the relative number is exactly tan(2theta)/(2theta), which is 1 at zero elevation and diverges at the 45-degree peak, so kappa ~= 1 is what a well-posed shot IS here, and the 10 / 100 thresholds are real decades above a real baseline, read as significant digits lost. The first cut used absolute sensitivity with a 1e-3 threshold and flagged every ordinary shot as ill-conditioned; that was wrong and was replaced, not tuned.

VALIDATION: criterion is "cond(J) spikes near envelope (plotted); solver warns" -- 38 tests (31 in ill-conditioning.test.ts, 7 in lazy-plotly-pane.test.ts), read as three claims. SPIKES: the exponent fits above, plus monotone rise in kappa and monotone escalation of the level ladder. PLOTTED: buildConditionNumberFigure, log-log on both axes because the claim is a straight line of slope -1/2 and only log-log makes a rate visible -- on linear axes the same data sweeps up the left edge looking dramatic and saying nothing about the exponent. Arc separation shares the axes and draws the opposite slope, so the Jacobian degenerating and the two solutions merging appear as one fold rather than two coincidences. Rows at or beyond the envelope are dropped rather than clamped: past the fold there is no solution to be conditioned. WARNS: silent on ordinary shots (kappa in [0.5, 2] at 100-300 m), escalates through both thresholds, names the cost in digits, says "The aim is not wrong" so a caller does not discard a usable aim, and reports a target past the envelope as unreachable rather than throwing.

The measurement is checked against the drag-free closed forms for BOTH dR/dtheta = (2 v0^2/g) cos 2theta and kappa = tan(2theta)/(2theta) -- neither of which the implementation knows -- at every sampled target, to five significant figures. Five and not six for a reason that is this module's own subject: a central difference truncates at (h^2/6) R''', so its RELATIVE error is (h^2/6) R'''/R', and R' -> 0 at the fold while R''' does not. The measurement of the conditioning is itself conditioned by the thing it measures. A separate test pins that the agreement degrades towards the fold, which makes the tolerance a measurement rather than a concession. Shrinking h trades this for the integrator noise shooting-jacobian.ts documents and lands worse.

FOUND WHILE BUILDING THIS AND FILED AS P0.97, NOT FIXED: launching from exactly y=0 makes the impact event true at t=0, and any flight fitting inside the integrator's first step gets localized there -- solveArcs returns a low arc missing a 50 m target by 39 m, silently. tasks.title: Discrete-adjoint note + prototype for range gradient (optional, documents scaling to many params)
tasks.validation: adjoint gradient matches tangent-linear to 1e-8 on 3-param case
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-18 (36th run). packages/analysis/src/adjoint-range-gradient.ts exports AdjointRangeGradient, AdjointRangeGradientFunction, createAdjointRangeGradient and createBackwardAdjointModel; the note is docs/notes/adjoint-sensitivity.md. VALIDATION MET BY FOUR ORDERS. The criterion is 'adjoint gradient matches tangent-linear to 1e-8 on 3-param case'. On (theta, v0, C_d) with drag at rtol 1e-12 the worst RELATIVE disagreement against createTangentLinearFlight/rangeSensitivity is 4.265e-13 on the flat shot (adjoint 24.1873987362973 / 5.12531951694258 / -53.4687545700258 against tangent 24.1873987363076 / 5.12531951694283 / -53.4687545700752) and 1.808e-12 from a 12 m launch. Held across a sweep of six elevations 0.25..1.1 rad. THE IDENTITY. Folding the event-time correction into a terminal covector lambda(T) = e_R - (e_R.f / grad_g.f) grad_g and running lambda' = -A^T lambda backwards makes d/dt(lambda^T S_k) = lambda^T b_k, so dR/dmu_k = lambda(0)^T S_k(0) + int_0^T lambda^T b_k dt with S_k never formed. Those two terms are exactly TangentParameter's two entry points, and the tests assert the split rather than describing it: a launch-state parameter's quadrature is not merely small but never accumulated (toEqual([0,0])), and a dynamics parameter's gradient IS its quadrature (toBe, not toBeCloseTo). CONTINUOUS, NOT DISCRETE -- SAID PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT TO THE TITLE. This differentiates the ODE and then discretises. A true discrete adjoint transposes the RK scheme and needs stage values, a transposed tableau and checkpointing, which is the 'full adjoint infrastructure' blueprint 9.2 explicitly says this task must not commit the platform to. The cost is measured: agreement is set by integration tolerance (4e-13), where a discrete adjoint's would be at machine precision. docs/notes/adjoint-sensitivity.md section 5 carries the comparison table. THE ONE SHORTCUT IS INSTRUMENTED. A(t) is needed along the base trajectory and this replays it by integrating y backwards from impact rather than checkpointing -- anti-dissipative, and it does drift. The result reports stateRoundTripError; measured 1.105e-11 (flat) and 8.413e-12 (raised), and the field exists so a longer or stiffer problem fails visibly instead of returning a quietly wrong gradient. THE SCALING CLAIM IS CHECKED INCLUDING THE ROW WHERE IT LOSES. forwardDimension n(1+m) and backwardDimension 2n+m are reported and asserted at m = 1, 3, 30: 8 vs 9, 16 vs 11, 124 vs 38. The m=1 row, where the forward method is smaller, is asserted too. Measured solver cost on the flat 3-param case: forward base 83 steps / 541 RHS, backward 117 steps / 801 RHS. The note also records where this direction does NOT pay -- Phase 5's shooting solves want a 2x2 Jacobian, which is the shape adjoints lose on; Phase 6's sensitivity work (blueprint 9.4) is the shape they win. MUTATION-CHECKED, four perturbations applied, run and reverted: dropping the A^T transpose turns 8 tests red; seeding lambda(T) = e_R (no event-time correction) turns 6 red; forgetting the sign flip on dy/ds turns 6 red; contracting the quadrature against y instead of lambda turns 3 red. 19 tests in the new file. NOT DONE and deliberately out of scope, each rejected at construction with a message rather than mishandled: terminal events with an action (P4.11 bounce -- the adjoint needs its own backward jump condition), multiple terminal events, no terminal event, and grazing impacts where grad_g.f -> 0. Observables other than range are not attempted; the identity is unchanged but each needs its own terminal seed and validation.

Nine cases across four solver families in packages/validation/src/golden-optimization-store.ts, recorded to golden-optimizations.json and checked by golden-optimizations.test.ts (25 tests). The criterion -- 'CI compares within tolerances' -- is met, and the shape of the comparison is the part worth knowing: status, converged, iterations and evaluations are pinned EXACTLY (integers from deterministic arithmetic; a move in any of them is the signal, and golden-trajectories.test.ts pins nSteps the same way), while solutions and objectives use a per-case tolerance taken from the solver's own documented resolution. Both reverted. FOUR ASSERTIONS DO NOT CONSULT THE FIXTURE AT ALL, which is what stops the store being self-referential: drag-free max range at pi/4 with R = v0^2/g, the drag-induced shift below pi/4, minimum launch speed sqrt(g*R) at the tangency aim, and the claim that every converged Newton case really is inside the 1e-6 m residual test while every non-converged one is outside. TWO FINDINGS, both measured, both filed rather than fixed: P0.105 (a raised PlatformTarget is unreachable for any ground-terminating model, so the solver stalls at a 15 m miss -- pinned deliberately as the store's non-convergence entry) and, separately, the measured fact that Newton and Nelder-Mead converge to DIFFERENT aims on the same problem (0.549 rad / 46.25 m/s against 0.655 rad / 44.63 m/s, both with miss < 3e-14 m). That second one is not a bug: the ground event pins the impact height, leaving one constraint over two unknowns, so the hitting aims form a curve. It is P5.05's rank-1 Jacobian seen from the other side, and the store's nelder-mead entry documents it so a later session does not 'fix' the disagreement by changing a solver. tasks.title: Levenberg–Marquardt fallback for tough shooting cases
tasks.validation: converges on case where pure Newton fails (constructed near-envelope)
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-18 (37th run). VALIDATION MET. packages/analysis/src/levenberg-marquardt.ts (levenbergMarquardt + shootingWithFallback) and levenberg-marquardt.test.ts, 14 tests in ~1.0 s. THE CONSTRUCTION IS THE SUBSTANTIVE HALF, because a case where Newton fails is easy to produce by accident and proves nothing about why. An UNCONSTRAINED aim problem HAS NO FOLD -- the solution set of a ground-impact shot is a curve in (theta, v0), and a target past the envelope at one speed is simply reached at a higher one -- so the degeneracy the blueprint pairs LM with only exists once the launch speed is BOUNDED, which is what a real machine is. Constructed case: quadratic drag (Cd 0.47, 1 kg, r 0.05), speed capped at 60 m/s via the P5.16 projection, point target 1 cm inside the envelope that cap allows. Envelope located by golden section, not hard-coded, then pinned: peak theta 0.7238770840242084, Rmax 232.61580676320023 m. MEASURED NOT INFERRED: the two arcs close to under 2.3 degrees at that shortfall; the scaled Jacobian row favours speed over elevation by >3x at the start aim while its vertical row is zero to <1e-8 (P5.05's structural rank deficiency); dR/dtheta at the peak is >100x smaller than at theta = 0.5. HEADLINE: from (0.7 rad, 50 m/s), pure newtonShooting reaches 'max-iterations' at |F| = 3.6e-3 after 40 iterations WITHOUT DIVERGING -- it crawls, three orders better than it started and two short of the 1e-6 tolerance, with the cap active -- and levenbergMarquardt converges below 1e-6 in 14 iterations on the same tolerance and budget, every step accepted on a positive gain ratio with monotonically decreasing merit. MECHANISM: on a rank-1 Jacobian with surviving scaled row (a, b) the minimum-norm step is parallel to (a, b), so the correction is allocated in proportion to sensitivity and goes almost entirely into speed -- which the cap then clips away. Marquardt's diag(JtJ) damping (not Levenberg's I) is invariant to column scaling and collapses on a rank-1 system to a step along (b, a), the reciprocal direction: the least-sensitive variable gets the largest correction, which near the envelope is theta. Nielsen gain-ratio lambda update rather than a multiply-by-10 schedule, which is discontinuous in rho and oscillates exactly where the truth is in between. Gain ratio in |F|^2, since that is what the least-squares model predicts; newtonShooting's Armijo test is in |F| and the two are deliberately NOT shared. LM IS A FALLBACK, NOT A REPLACEMENT, and this is asserted rather than asserted-away: where both solvers work Newton takes 3-4 iterations and LM 14, which is what fixes shootingWithFallback's order (Newton first, LM only on non-convergence, warm started from Newton's best aim). HONEST LIMIT: neither solver reaches the target from a start on the far side of the peak. That is a BASIN problem and belongs to P5.27's multi-start, not here. Warm starting does not rescue it; what it buys there is measured instead -- |F| 8.6e-6 chained against 3.8e-1 cold, four to five orders, with both still reporting max-iterations. NOTE FOR P5.29 (method-selection docs): the decision table it owes has its numbers here -- Newton where the target is comfortably inside the envelope, LM near it, multi-start when the initial aim may be on the wrong side of the peak.

tasks.title: Multi-start strategy with deduplication of solutions
tasks.validation: finds both arcs without user hint
tasks.notes:
Done 2026-08-19 (38th run). VALIDATION MET. packages/analysis/src/multi-start.ts (multiStart, goldenRatioSamples, multiStartAngles) and multi-start.test.ts, 21 tests in ~0.7 s.

THE DESIGN DECISION IS WHICH PROBLEM TO MULTI-START ON, and it was settled by measurement before any code was written, because deduplication presupposes ISOLATED solutions and the obvious reading of this task does not have any. A multi-start over (theta, v0) is searching a problem whose solution set is a CURVE: P5.05's zero vertical Jacobian row makes F one scalar equation in two unknowns, and P5.06's minimum-norm step lands on whichever point of that curve is nearest the start. Measured on a 140 m target, 21 starts over theta in [0.15, 1.35] and v0 in {40, 55, 70}: 21 starts, 21 DISTINCT converged aims, every one a genuine hit under 3e-10 m, speeds spanning more than 20 m/s. Any dedup rule that respects those answers returns 21, and 'both arcs' is not a statement about that set -- 'low' and 'high' are not defined on a curve. It is kept as a negative control in the test file rather than described.

FIXING THE SPEED IS WHAT MAKES THE TWO ARCS EXIST, which is also how P5.08 states the problem ('fix the speed, and the curve meets that constraint twice'). So the starts vary elevation only and the local solve is P5.16's constrainedShooting under a DEGENERATE speed box [v0, v0] -- validateAimBounds permits min == max, only min > max is rejected. No peak, no bracket, no ordering assumption: solveArcs's 24-sample peak sweep, which brackets one root either side, is exactly the hint the criterion rules out.

CRITERION MET. 16 starts over theta in [0.05, 1.5] at 55 m/s against a 140 m target collapse onto exactly TWO solutions, theta = 0.303042401650 (low, dR/dtheta = +322.1, 7 starts) and 1.185648587950 (high, dR/dtheta = -282.3, 8 starts). Both agree with solveArcs -- which found them the other way, using the peak -- to 6 decimal places. Labels are the SIGN of a local derivative at each solution (P5.20's rangeSlopeAt), not the ordering of the pair, so they survive a bound clipping one arc away, which the test checks by clipping one away.

15 OF 16 STARTS ARE ACCEPTED, NOT 16, and the one lost is the finding. It lands at theta = 0.7346, 3.3 mrad from the measured peak at 0.7313, where dR/dtheta passes through zero; the projected minimum-norm step is near zero there too, so the iteration stops on its step tolerance after ONE iteration with 66 m of miss outstanding. That is P5.20's basin boundary, sampled -- the peak belongs to neither arc and rejecting it is correct. The test asserts exactly that one start is lost and no other.

THREE OF THE FIRST-DRAFT ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG and were corrected against measurement rather than loosened: the accepted count (above); cluster spread, which is 6.1e-9 rad and set by where the projected solve stops rather than by the residual tolerance, so the merge tolerance has two orders of room below it and not five; and the reason for the golden-ratio start sequence. It does NOT beat a uniform grid on largest gap at a fixed count -- 0.0902 against 0.0625 at n = 16 -- and that false claim is now pinned AS false in the test file. The real reasons are the three-distance theorem (exactly three gap lengths, measured) and prefix extension (the first n of n+k points are the first n, so raising startCount keeps every solve already paid for).

tasks.validation: checker validates against stored solutions
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-19 (39th run). VALIDATION MET: `packages/runtime/src/inverse-exercises.test.ts` grades all five stored solutions correct, in 42 tests. `packages/runtime/src/inverse-exercises.ts` holds the set; the checker is `checkAnswer` / `checkAll`. THE CRITERION WAS READ AS THREE CLAIMS, because the literal one is nearly vacuous -- `checkAnswer(ex, ex.answer.solution)` compares a number with itself and would pass against a key of five zeros. (1) It accepts the stored solutions. (2) It REJECTS: tolerance probed either side, at the boundary, on non-finite input, and against the specific wrong answer each exercise exists to catch -- the two arcs must not accept each other, the drag optimum must not accept 45 deg, the envelope must not accept the drag-free parabola of safety. (3) The stored key is RIGHT, not merely stored: every exercise carries a `recompute()` deriving it from @ballista/analysis, asserted to agree within 1e-9, which doubles as a drift guard. FOUR OF THE FIVE KEYS ARE ANCHORED OUTSIDE THIS CODEBASE: low arc 18.90031076438649 deg against the closed form 0.5*asin(gR/v0^2) to 13 significant figures, high arc 71.09968923561345 deg as its complement to 90, their midpoint at exactly 45 deg (the drag-free peak), and min launch speed 54.24016039799292 m/s = sqrt(g*300) exactly. FIVE DIFFERENT INVERSE PROBLEMS, not one five times: low root, high root, maximization (maximizeRange), nested minimization (minimumSpeedToHit), reachability (assessReachability). PROJECTILE CHOICE WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: a regulation baseball (145 g, 36.6 mm) moves the max-range elevation 4.94 deg below 45, a 1 kg 5 cm sphere in the same air only 1.86 deg, so the baseball is used and the dense sphere rejected as making the lesson look like rounding. Envelope ceiling 60 m downrange at 40 m/s is 28.277 m against the drag-free parabola's 70.5 m. ONE FINDING, filed here rather than left in a commit message: the documented inclusive boundary was not delivered. `solution + tolerance` is a rounded double whose distance back from `solution` is not `tolerance` -- 7.1e-16 too large for exercise 1 -- so a naive `error <= tolerance` graded the exact boundary WRONG. The test encoded the right belief and the checker was fixed to absorb the representation error with 4 ulps of slack; a further test pins that the slack stays at ulp scale, rejecting an answer outside by one part in a billion. Suite 248 files / 2382 tests green, up 42 from 2340; typecheck, lint, lint:deps, format:check and build all clean. NOT DONE HERE: no UI route. The blueprint's L5 table assigns exercise *content* to @ballista/app, but every prior exercise (P4.20 neglected-effects, P4.29 density-altitude) puts its computation in @ballista/runtime and only the route in app, and this followed that precedent. A route rendering INVERSE_EXERCISES with an answer box is a natural follow-on and is filed as P0.108.

tasks.title: ADR-017: tolerance coupling between inner IVP and outer optimizer
tasks.validation: rule implemented (inner tol ≤ outer tol²-style heuristic) + test
tasks.notes: DONE on the 42nd run. packages/analysis/src/tolerance-coupling.ts (coupleTolerances, checkToleranceCoupling), 16 tests in tolerance-coupling.test.ts, docs/adr/ADR-017-inner-outer-tolerance-coupling.md. THE RULE HAS TWO CLAUSES AND NEITHER DOMINATES. (1) noise floor: rtol <= 0.1*tau/L, linear in the outer tolerance and dependent on the trajectory scale L. (2) Jacobian: the achievable relative accuracy at the optimal difference step is eps^{p/(p+1)}, so rtol <= eta^{(p+1)/p} -- eta^2 for a forward difference, eta^{3/2} for a central one. THIS TASK'S TITLE QUOTES THE SQUARE, WHICH IS THE FORWARD CASE; this package differences centrally by default, where the square over-tightens by 31.6x at eta=1e-3. The scheme is an input, not a hard-coded exponent. Both clauses bind on the same 295 m shot -- crossover near tau = 0.09 m. THE MEASURED FINDING, which is not what the task title suggests: a loose inner solve does not make the outer one fail to converge. At rtol=1e-3 against a 1e-6 m outer tolerance newtonShooting converges in 3 iterations to a reported residual of 2.148e-07 m at an aim that actually misses by 4.392e-02 m -- 2.0e5x, status 'converged', no diagnostic anywhere. The residual is a smooth deterministic function of the aim at fixed rtol, so the solver finds an exact root of the wrong function. Same shape as P0.97/ADR-016. AUDIT, NOT ENFORCE: neither entry point throws and newtonShooting is unchanged, because deliberately loose solves are legitimate (basin-of-attraction, multi-start, the perf harness) and ShootingProblem does not carry L. ADR-017 records the follow-up not taken: putting the audit's verdict on the four solvers' result objects, which is a breaking change to their public types. Five fault injections run and reverted, each failing exactly its intended assertions.

tasks.title: Distribution schema: normal, lognormal, uniform, truncated variants on any scenario param
tasks.validation: sampling moments match analytics (1e5 draws, 3σ bands)
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-22 (43rd run). VALIDATION MET: sampling moments match analytics at 1e5 draws inside 3-sigma bands, asserted seven times -- untruncated normal, two-sided truncated normal, one-sided truncated normal on both sides, a far-tail window, untruncated lognormal, truncated lognormal, and uniform. FILES: packages/engine/src/distribution.ts (distributionSpecSchema, sampleDistribution, distributionMoments, distributionSupport) and normal-distribution-functions.ts (erf, erfc, normalPdf, normalCdf, normalUpperTail, normalQuantile, standardNormalIntervalMass), both re-exported from the engine index. 48 tests: 27 + 21. THE BANDS ARE THE ESTIMATORS OWN STANDARD ERRORS, not a tuned tolerance: sigma/sqrt(n) for the mean and sigma^2*sqrt(2/(n-1)) for the variance. They therefore tighten as n grows, so a biased sampler cannot be hidden by drawing more samples. The lognormal variance band alone carries a factor of 4, because excess kurtosis of about 1.6 widens the variance estimator beyond the normal-theory formula; the factor is derived in a comment, not fitted. TRUNCATION IS INVERSE-CDF, NOT REJECTION. Rejection is simpler but its cost is unbounded as the window moves into the tail, and P6.04 runs 1e4 replicates. One test draws 1e5 samples from the [3sigma, 4sigma] window where acceptance is 1.3e-3 and rejection would need about 8e7 draws. THE TAIL IS WHERE THE ARITHMETIC MATTERS. Every probability is computed in whichever of Phi or Q stays away from 1. standardNormalIntervalMass on [4, 5] keeps sixteen digits where the naive Phi(b)-Phi(a) keeps eleven, and that mass is the divisor in every truncated moment. erf/erfc come from the regularised incomplete gamma at a=1/2, iterated to convergence rather than truncated at a fixed polynomial order, so there is no fitted-coefficient error floor; normalQuantile Halley-refines against normalCdf, so its A&S 26.2.23 seed affects only iteration count. A SPEC CAN BE LEGAL AND STILL UNSAMPLEABLE: [40 sigma, 41 sigma] underflows to zero mass. The schema rejects that at parse time rather than returning NaN at sample time. VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: four faults injected in turn and reverted -- the truncated-normal mean shift sign (4 tests fail), truncation dropped from the sampler (4), the shift^2 term of the variance factor (4), the k*s shift in the lognormal raw moment (2). Note that the sampler-truncation fault is NOT caught by the support test, because clampToSupport masks it; the moment tests are what catch it. TWO TESTS OF THE FIRST DRAFT ENCODED WRONG BELIEFS AND WERE FIXED RATHER THAN LOOSENED: comparing erfc at two points 2e-9 apart and expecting agreement to 1e-14 ignored erfc own slope there (-0.2518, so 5e-10 of genuine difference), and a trapezoid reference integral for normalCdf had 8e-11 of its own truncation error, which would have set the tolerance instead of the function under test -- replaced by Simpson. The implementation matched an independent Taylor series to 3e-16 throughout. SCOPE: this task is the per-parameter distribution only. Binding distributions to named ScenarioSpec fields is P6.02 (UncertainScenarioSpec) and was deliberately not started here.

tasks.title: `UncertainScenarioSpec`: base spec + distribution overlays + N + seed
tasks.validation: serialize round-trip; validates against base schema
tasks.notes: VALIDATION MET. packages/engine/src/uncertain-scenario-spec.ts + 51 tests. Criterion is 'serialize round-trip; validates against base schema' and both halves are asserted directly: a JSON.stringify/parse/re-parse cycle is deep-equal and byte-identical as text (deep equality alone would tolerate a reordering the substream mapping does not), is idempotent on a second pass, and runs over EVERY entry in PRESET_SCENARIOS as the base -- the base is the half most likely to drop a field, carrying optional spin/lateral channels, nested wind variants and tabulated drag. The base is parsed by scenarioSpecSchema itself, unmodified, so an invalid base (negative mass, wrong schemaVersion, absent) fails the study, and the issue is reported under the 'base' path rather than the study root. SHAPE: base ScenarioSpec + ordered array of {path, distribution} + replicates (N, positive int) + seed. The array is ordered rather than a keyed record because P6.03 assigns substreams by overlay index and P6.05 needs a fixed reduction order; duplicate paths are rejected because last-one-wins would make a result depend on key order. Dotted paths are resolved against this study's own base at parse time, so a typo names itself instead of becoming a NaN 1e4 replicates later; readSpecNumberAtPath is exported for P6.03 to share, and refuses __proto__/constructor/prototype since a path can arrive from a shared URL. Two seeds: base.seed fixes the nominal realization (ADR-011 frozen wind), study seed fixes the ensemble. NOT HERE, deliberately: applying a drawn parameter vector back onto a spec -- that is P6.03's replicate generator. FOUND WHILE DOING THIS: adding the first engine export whose signature inlines a ScenarioSpec made typedoc's unresolvable {@link z0} in scenario-spec.ts fire, and typedoc fails on warnings; fixed in the preceding commit.

tasks.title: Replicate generator: seed+index substreams (P0.11) → param vectors
tasks.validation: replicate i identical regardless of batch partitioning
tasks.notes: VALIDATION MET. packages/engine/src/replicate-generator.ts + 32 tests. The criterion is 'replicate i identical regardless of batch partitioning' and it is asserted three ways: a replicate generated alone equals the same index taken from any range containing it (five target indices against four differently-shaped ranges each); every contiguous partition of 0..N-1 into chunks of 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 16 and 64 reassembles into the identical sequence; and asking for the ranges backwards gives the same result as forwards, which is the one that catches hidden state rather than a hidden index. API: generateReplicate(study, i) -> {index, values, spec}, generateReplicateRange for a worker batch, replicates() as a lazy generator (P6.04 budgets 50 MB for 1e4 replicates and a materialized array of specs would spend most of it first), plus writeSpecNumberAtPath as the write counterpart of P6.02's reader, and replicateStreamId / replicateSeed / replicateRng exported because each is a claim a value-level test cannot grade. ONE SUBSTREAM PER (REPLICATE, OVERLAY) PAIR, NOT ONE PER REPLICATE. One generator per replicate meets the criterion and is still wrong, for a reason that only appears when a study is EDITED rather than re-run: distributions consume different numbers of raw uniforms -- normal takes two via Box-Muller, uniform takes one, a truncated variant takes one via the inverse CDF -- so changing overlay 0's kind shifts every later parameter in every replicate, and comparing two studies differing in one parameter (P6.17's entire subject) would compare two unrelated ensembles. Two cases assert the independence, and both pass under a per-replicate stream, which is why they sit outside the batch block. PCG32 DISCARDS THE TOP BIT OF A STREAM ID: its increment is (streamId << 1) | 1 masked to 64 bits, so s and s + 2^63 are the SAME stream and any 64-bit hash of (i, j) is two-to-one onto the streams. The stream id is therefore NOT hashed -- it is the plain packing i * OVERLAY_STRIDE + j, injective by construction, with OVERLAY_STRIDE = 2^20 and MAX_REPLICATE_INDEX = 2^43 - 1 keeping it under 2^63; both bounds are checked at call time, not assumed. What IS hashed is the seed (splitmix64), which is what stops neighbouring pairs starting from arithmetically related states. VALIDATION IS ON AND THE COST WAS MEASURED: each drawn spec is re-parsed by scenarioSpecSchema at 24.7 us, so 1e4 replicates pay 0.25 s against 1e4 integrations and there is no case for an opt-out. A failing draw THROWS rather than being dropped -- dropping is rejection sampling on the output and biases the estimator, integrating a negative mass poisons it silently -- and the message names the drawn value and points at P6.01's truncated variants. VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: eight faults injected in turn and reverted. TWO WERE NOT CAUGHT BY THE FIRST DRAFT and are why replicateSeed is exported: removing the seed hash, and replacing the derived seed with the study seed, both passed every value-level assertion, because the streams alone already differ so the drawn values differ anyway. Two cases now grade the hash itself (every pair distinct; pairs one stream apart differ in more than 16 of 64 bits). Note what they deliberately do NOT pin -- neutering splitmix64's second multiply still passes, because a one-round mixer still meets both properties. They grade the property, not the constants. NOT HERE, deliberately: base.seed is untouched, so every replicate carries the study's single nominal wind realization; one frozen OU path per replicate is P6.16, and a test asserts the base seed is unchanged so that boundary moves deliberately or not at all.

tasks.title: `mc` worker job: batch integrate, record observables only (Sink selection)
tasks.validation: 1e4 replicates without retaining trajectories; memory < 50 MB
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-23 (47th run). VALIDATION MET: 1e4 replicates retain 0.35 MB against the 50 MB budget, measured as heapUsed across a forced GC on both sides (P1.21's methodology). FILES: packages/analysis/src/observable-sink.ts (ObservableSink, Observables) and packages/runtime/src/mc-job.ts (McJob, McColumns, createMcColumns, runMcReplicate, runMcRange, MC_T_MAX_SECONDS), both re-exported from their package index. 66 tests: 56 + 10. THE WORK IS THE SINK, NOT THE LOOP. sweep-job.ts attaches a TrajectoryRecorder whose cost is O(steps x channels); nothing downstream of a Monte Carlo batch reads those rows. ObservableSink carries the first row, the last row and the best apex candidate -- O(model.dim) for a whole solve -- and one instance is reused across the batch. IT IS THE SAME ARITHMETIC AS observables.ts, NOT AN APPROXIMATION, and the tests assert that with Object.is rather than a tolerance, because a tolerance is exactly what would let a streaming reimplementation drift and keep passing. Two facts make exactness reachable: TrajectoryRecorder records the initial state plus one row per accept, so the sink sees the same rows; and apex's scan is already local to consecutive row pairs. Only the candidate ORDER had to be reproduced -- apex considers row 0, then the final row, then interior crossings, with strict-greater comparison, so ties resolve to the earliest CONSIDERED rather than the earliest in time. Streaming sees crossings before the final row, so the crossing maximum is kept separate and folded in after the endpoints; a running maximum is associative and first-wins tie-breaking survives the two-stage computation. hermiteValue and hermiteStationaryPoint are now exported from observables.ts and shared rather than copied, which is what keeps the exactness claim true as either side changes. THE CRITERION IS MET AND IS ALSO NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the finding worth carrying forward. Restoring a per-replicate TrajectoryRecorder and retaining every trajectory -- the exact implementation the criterion exists to forbid -- costs 10.5 MB on this fixture and PASSES the 50 MB assertion, because a drag-free preset flight is a few dozen accepted steps and 1e4 kilobyte trajectories never reach 50 MB. The threshold is a property of the fixture, not of the code. The acceptance test is kept verbatim, and a second test measures the property directly: quadrupling N must not grow retained memory beyond the output columns, which fails under the retaining variant by about 8 MB. A future task that changes the MC fixture should not read the 50 MB test as protection. TWO BUGS THE TESTS FOUND AND WHICH WERE FIXED, NOT WORKED AROUND: the apex scan paired the row BEFORE last with the incoming row, so every refinement after the first used a stale row (the sink needs one row of history, not two); and the sink's memory test ran both its long and short solves on DOPRI5, where the configured h is only an initial guess, so the controller converged both to ~395 steps and the comparison was vacuous -- now fixed-step RK4 under Hermite dense output, 100x apart, measured while holding 20 finished sinks so the signal is linear in the count while GC slack is not. ONE DOCUMENTED CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED: SolveReport.status is 'ok' for a solve that merely exhausts its tspan, so it cannot distinguish that from an impact, and SolveReport carries no terminal-event flag. mc-job.ts therefore reports a per-replicate `landed` flag computed from tFinal < MC_T_MAX_SECONDS; a truncated flight's 'impact point' is wherever it was at 60 s, and averaging those in alongside real impacts would bias P6.07's and P6.11's estimators invisibly. WHAT THE TESTS DELIBERATELY DO NOT PIN: relaxing the downward-crossing guard (vy0 >= 0 && vy1 < 0) to any sign change is NOT caught by any case, including the bouncing one. An upward crossing refines to a local MINIMUM of the interpolant, and a running maximum never takes it, so the fault cannot change the reported apex. The guard mirrors observables.ts and is correct; it is simply not observable at the value level, and nobody should read the passing suite as grading it. VERIFICATION: seven faults injected into the sink and reverted, five caught -- two of them only by the bouncing arc and the still-climbing solve, and one only by a non-zero launch epoch, all three of which were added after the first draft passed everything. typecheck, eslint, depcruise (1489 modules, 0 violations) and prettier clean; full suite 2661/2661 across 257 files, up from 2595/255.

tasks.title: Deterministic reduction order (by replicate index) for all statistics
tasks.validation: shuffled worker completion ⇒ identical stats hash
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-24 (48th run). packages/analysis/src/mc-stats.ts (+ .test.ts, 15 tests, all passing). Pipeline: assembleMcColumns copies each chunk into its global slice via Float64Array.set (a coverage bitmap catches overlaps/gaps regardless of chunk arrival order); mcStats walks the assembled buffer 0..N-1 folding per-observable sum/sumSquares/min/max over landed replicates only; hashMcStats folds the full stats through an inlined splitmix64 into a 16-hex-digit 0x-prefixed string. Assembly-order invariance verified across three arrival orders (as-partitioned, reversed, interleaved) on a 64-replicate fixture and again on 256-replicate arrival-order permutations across two different partitionings. The right-to-left reduction fault is caught by the hash; assembly-order permutation of singleton chunks is (correctly) not, because the assembled buffer is identical either way and the mcStats loop always walks it left-to-right. Non-landing replicates count toward count/landedCount only; a poison-value test confirms they contribute to no observable sum/min/max. Structural typing on the columns keeps analysis import-free of runtime (would be a cycle: runtime already imports ObservableSink). splitmix64 inlined rather than imported from engine both to avoid coupling to that module property tests and because engine does not export it.

tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-24 (49th run). packages/analysis/src/streaming-moments.ts (+ .test.ts, 23 tests): WelfordAccumulator (running mean + M2 by Welford's recurrence, with a Chan/Golub/LeVeque merge so chunk-local accumulators combine without revisiting values -- deterministic for a fixed merge order, NOT bit-identical to sequential, asserted both ways) and P2QuantileEstimator (Jain & Chlamtac 1985, one quantile from five markers, no sample retained), plus welfordMoments/p2Quantiles/exactQuantile helpers. mc-stats.ts's McObservableStats gained mean and variance, computed by a per-observable WelfordAccumulator inside the existing canonical loop (48th-run handoff: extend McStats, do not add a second module) over the landed subset only; hashMcStats now folds them too so a reproducibility check keeps covering the whole struct. mean is NaN for an empty landed subset, variance NaN for <2, not 0. tasks.title: MC convergence check: SE ∝ N^{−1/2} measured on range observable
tasks.validation: log–log slope −0.50±0.05
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-24 (50th run). VALIDATION MET: log-log slope of the estimator's standard error against batch size measured at -0.51162 on the real range observable, against the criterion's -0.50 +/- 0.05. FILES: packages/analysis/src/mc-convergence.ts (mcConvergenceStudy, sampleStdDev, standardErrorOfMean) + .test.ts (20 tests), and packages/runtime/src/mc-convergence-range.test.ts (7 tests) which is where the criterion itself is measured -- analysis may not import runtime (section 2.1 layering), so the generic estimator lives in analysis and the measurement against the pipeline lives runtime-side. THE MEASUREMENT IS ACROSS BATCHES, NOT WITHIN ONE. Reporting s/sqrt(N) from a single batch cannot detect a violation of the law it is testing: it computes sigma/sqrt(N) by construction and so returns a flawless -0.5 even on perfectly correlated draws. mcConvergenceStudy instead splits the pool into disjoint batches of size N and takes the sample standard deviation ACROSS the batch means, which is an empirical measurement of estimator spread and knows nothing about sqrt(N). Each point still carries the derived value as predictedStandardError for comparison; on the range pool the two agree at ratios 0.92 to 1.00, and the analysis suite asserts they part company when independence fails. MEASURED, on a pool of 49152 replicates (drag-free preset, normal jitter stdDev 2 on vx0 and vy0, seed 20260824): mean range 91.7817 m, per-replicate sigma 12.2285 m; measured SE 3.04905 / 2.09942 / 1.48275 / 1.05380 / 0.74520 / 0.52770 / 0.35166 at batch sizes 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 / 1024. WHY SEVEN SIZES OVER A FACTOR OF 64: the SE estimate at size N comes from POOL/N batch means, so the largest size is the least certain (48 batches, ~10% relative error), and a wide lever arm in log N divides that noise down -- expected slope uncertainty near 0.02, comfortably inside 0.05. Starting at N=16 is not a small-sample cheat: Var(mean of N) = sigma^2/N is EXACT for iid finite-variance samples, so the law holds at every N with no CLT appeal. BATCH SIZES RE-PARTITION ONE POOL rather than each drawing fresh replicates: M integrations instead of sum(K_i * N_i) for the same precision. That correlates the SE estimates across sizes, which moves the fitted line up or down but not its slope; within any one size the batches stay disjoint and independent. NOT FLAKY, BY CONSTRUCTION: replicate i is a pure function of seed and index (P6.03), so the slope is a fixed number rather than a draw. One runtime assertion re-runs the pool in two halves and requires the identical slope -- P6.03's partitioning guarantee restated at the value level. The analysis suite carries the robustness argument that the passing slope is not one tuned seed: five independent fixed seeds give -0.4744 / -0.4982 / -0.5095 / -0.4810 / -0.5340, all inside +/-0.05. COUNTEREXAMPLES ARE ASSERTED, not just the passing case: a perfectly correlated pool (each draw repeated 16x) has a measured SE more than 3x the derived one at the smallest batch, and a pool whose batch means never shrink yields slope === null rather than a fabricated number. DECIDES WHAT mc-job.ts DEFERRED HERE: a replicate that never reached the ground inside MC_T_MAX_SECONDS is excluded from the pool before the estimator sees it, since its 'impact' is wherever the horizon caught it. The runtime test asserts this study loses none, so a batch of N really holds N samples; a study that did truncate would need its batch sizes recomputed against the landed count, which is why the exclusion is the caller's step and not hidden inside mcConvergenceStudy. DOCS: docs/analysis/README.md gained a section (required by packages/validation/src/analysis-docs.test.ts for every re-exported module). Gate green: typecheck, lint, lint:deps, format:check, 2741/2741 tests across 262 files, app build.

tasks.title: CI bands on estimates (t-based) + displayed honestly with N
tasks.validation: coverage test: 95% CI covers truth ~95% over 200 repeats (drag-free analytic)
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-25 (51st run). VALIDATION MET: a 95% t interval covers the analytic truth in 192 of 200 repeats = 0.96, which is 0.65 binomial sigma from the nominal 0.95 (1 sigma = sqrt(.95*.05/200) = 0.01541). FILES: packages/analysis/src/confidence-interval.ts (+ .test.ts, 35 tests) and packages/runtime/src/mc-confidence-coverage.test.ts (8 tests), where the criterion itself is measured -- analysis may not import runtime (section 2.1 layering), so the estimator lives in analysis and the measurement against the pipeline lives runtime-side, the same split P6.07 used. THE TRUTH IS EXACT, NOT ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON THE CRITERION NAMES THE DRAG-FREE CASE. A coverage test needs something to cover, and for a jittered ensemble the analytic value at the mean inputs is generally the WRONG target since E[f(X)] != f(E[X]). Drag-free ground-launch range is the exception: R = 2*vx0*vy0/g is BILINEAR, so under INDEPENDENT jitter E[R] = 2*E[vx0]*E[vy0]/g holds exactly -- no linearisation, no CLT appeal, no error term to bound. The independence is what P6.03's substream-per-pair generator supplies, so the criterion is quietly also a check on that: correlated overlays would move E[R] off the truth and coverage would collapse. y0 is forced to 0 because the raised-launch form carries a sqrt(vy0^2+2*g*y0) term that is not bilinear. MEASURED, on 200 repeats of 64 replicates = 12800 (drag-free preset, normal jitter stdDev 2 on vx0 and vy0, seed 20260825): analytic truth 91.77269893388672 m; pool mean 91.84957 m with pool SE 0.10830, i.e. 0.71 SE away, so no detectable integrator or seeding bias -- this is asserted BEFORE the truth is used, since otherwise every coverage figure would measure the wrong thing while still looking plausible. Per-replicate sigma 12.2525 m. First repeat: mean 94.5072, SE 1.50479, t(0.975,63) = 1.998341, half-width 3.00708. COUNTEREXAMPLES ARE ASSERTED, not just the passing case. (a) Width alone cannot pass: displacing the truth by 4 standard errors of a single repeat drops coverage to 0.045. An infinitely wide interval would otherwise score 100% and satisfy a one-sided reading of 'covers ~95%'. (b) The level is a dial, not a decoration: an 80% interval covers 160/200 = 0.800 exactly, so a multiplier that ignored `level` and always returned the 95% one would pass the criterion and fail here. (c) WHY THE TASK SAYS t-BASED: at n=5 (df=4) the multiplier is 2.776 against the normal's 1.960, and rebuilding the same intervals with z gives 183/200 = 0.915 against t's 194/200 = 0.970. The under-coverage is measured on the real pipeline rather than argued from theory. NOT FLAKY, BY CONSTRUCTION: replicate i is a pure function of seed and index (P6.03) and each repeat is a fixed disjoint index window, so the coverage is a fixed number rather than a draw. The assertion band is still written in binomial sigmas rather than tuned to the observed value -- a proportion compared directly to 0.95 gives a test that either never fails or fails at random. CoverageResult.standardError reports that scale so callers cannot skip it. THE t QUANTILE is solved in the UPPER TAIL by Newton under a bisection safeguard, seeded from engine's normalQuantile (the df->infinity limit, so the seed improves exactly where t gets harder to bracket); the safeguard earns its place at df=1 where the true multiplier is 12.7 against the seed's 1.96. Tail policy mirrors normal-distribution-functions.ts: Q is computed as itself, not as 1-cdf. Validated against CLOSED FORMS rather than copied digits -- df=1 is the Cauchy (tan) and df=2 has an elementary inverse, both to 1e-12 relative; df->infinity against normalQuantile; round-trip Q(quantile(p)) == 1-p to 1e-12 across df 1..5000. The accuracy floor is the incomplete beta continued fraction's ~1e-12, not the root find's 1e-15, and the tests say so rather than asserting a precision the special function lacks. DISPLAYED HONESTLY WITH N is read as a property of the value, not of the chart: MeanConfidenceInterval carries sampleSize, degreesOfFreedom and level alongside the bounds and no format option omits n, so P6.09-P6.11's plots cannot obtain a band without the n that produced it. meanConfidenceInterval returns null below 2 samples rather than a zero-width interval that would read as infinite precision. DOCS: docs/analysis/README.md gained a section (required by analysis-docs.test.ts for every re-exported module). Gate green: typecheck, lint, lint:deps, format:check, 2784/2784 tests across 264 files, app build.

tasks.title: Trajectory ensemble fan: quantile envelope bands (5/25/50/75/95%) over time via dense-output resampling on common grid
tasks.validation: bands nested and monotone; median ≈ nominal for symmetric inputs
tasks.notes: Done in the 53rd run. `packages/analysis/src/ensemble-fan.ts` puts an ensemble of adaptively-integrated replicates onto one time grid and reduces each grid point to its quantiles: `resampleOnGrid`, `buildCommonGrid`, `buildEnsembleFan`, `quantileOfSorted`, `DEFAULT_FAN_LEVELS`. 28 tests. Nothing renders here -- P6.20 and P6.24 consume the arrays, the same split P6.09 used. BOTH HALVES OF THE CRITERION ARE MET, EACH WITH THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IT NEEDS. (a) BANDS NESTED AND MONOTONE: asserted at every grid point of a 64-point fan over nine ballistic arcs, and again over TWENTY-ONE levels (0, 0.05, ..., 1) rather than only the five the task names -- nesting must not be a property of the level set that happens to be default. The counterexample that stops a clamp passing: at a full sweep the outermost pair is asserted to be exactly the sample min and max, which a repaired-after-the-fact band would not be. Nesting is STRUCTURAL rather than repaired: every level is read from the same sorted column through a level-to-index map that is non-decreasing in p, and nothing clamps the output, because a clamp would hide the only kind of bug that could produce a crossing. (b) MEDIAN ~ NOMINAL FOR SYMMETRIC INPUTS: nine arcs at 16..24 m/s in steps of 1, so the median speed is exactly the nominal 20; the median band lands on the nominal arc to 12 digits at every one of 40 grid points. This is an equality rather than a tolerance on a spread. The counterexample: replacing one arc with a 120 m/s outlier separates the median from the mean by more than 1 m at a mid-flight grid point, so an implementation that averaged instead of ordering -- which passes every symmetric case in the file -- fails here. THE RESAMPLING IS GENUINELY DENSE OUTPUT. A `Trajectory` holds accepted steps only, and interpolating them linearly is second-order: it discards three orders of the accuracy a DOPRI5 solve was paid for, invisibly, since the result still looks like a trajectory. The caller instead names a DERIVATIVE CHANNEL and gets cubic Hermite from the two endpoint values and the two endpoint slopes -- the interpolant `HermiteDenseOutputStepper` builds inside the solver. For a ballistic state that channel is already recorded (dx/dt is vx, dy/dt is vy), so third-order dense output is available from the recorded rows alone with no change to `Sink` and no second integration. That is a property of THIS model family and not a general fact, which is why the channel is an explicit argument: a wrong one produces a smooth plausible curve that is not the solution, which is worse than the documented linear fallback. Measured, not argued: on a genuine cubic the Hermite path is exact to 1e-10 at 41 points, and on the ballistic parabola it is exact to <1e-12 where linear is off by 1.226 m at a step midpoint with h = 1 (g h^2 / 8). The second is what proves the derivative channel is actually being used; the first alone would pass for an implementation that ignored it on a linear problem. A BAND PAST THE FIRST IMPACT MEANS SOMETHING DIFFERENT, and the type says so. Replicates end at different times, so the ensemble thins and a late quantile is conditional on the replicate still being airborne. `EnsembleFan` carries `sampleCount` per grid point and `commonSupportEnd` -- the same 'displayed honestly with N' commitment P6.08 made, and for the same reason. A grid time outside a replicate's own span resamples to NaN rather than to a clamped endpoint: repeating an impact point across the rest of the grid would draw a projectile resting on the ground AND drag the quantiles towards it. Asserted in both directions (the NaN is there, and it is not equal to the endpoint it would have been clamped to). ONE FINDING, asserted rather than special-cased: a NaN in a recorded row takes out BOTH adjacent intervals INCLUDING THEIR FAR ENDPOINTS, because the interpolation weights it by zero and 0 * NaN is NaN, not 0. The affected columns thin to the surviving replicates rather than voiding, which is the property that matters. A short-circuit returning y0 at exactly t0 while returning NaN an instant later would be a stranger surface than a clean hole, so the behaviour is documented in the header and in the test instead of being patched. The quantile estimator is type-7 (NumPy/R default), linear between order statistics, checked against numpy.percentile([1,2,3,4]) = 1.75/2.5/3.25; chosen over nearest-rank because a fan is read as a continuous surface and a nearest-rank band steps by a whole order statistic as the surviving count changes by one. It is written `a + frac*(b-a)` so an exact index reproduces its order statistic bit for bit, which is asserted. tasks.title: Hit-probability estimator for target + Wilson interval
tasks.validation: matches binomial simulation on constructed case
tasks.notes: Done 2026-08-25 (54th run). packages/analysis/src/hit-probability.ts exports wilsonInterval, hitProbability, formatHitProbability and DEFAULT_HIT_PROBABILITY_LEVEL; re-exported from the package index and documented in docs/analysis/README.md (analysis-docs.test.ts enforces both). Impacts are scored through targets.ts's isHit, so there is no second definition of a hit. CRITERION MET, and it is the coverage suite rather than a formula check: 4000 seeded binomial samples at each of (n=25,p=0.5), (25,0.2), (40,0.05), (100,0.9), asserting the Wilson interval covers the true p at about its nominal 95%; plus a head-to-head in which Wald under-covers at p=0.05,n=40 because k=0 makes its interval empty of the truth about 13% of the time. WHY WILSON: Wald's width is proportional to sqrt(p(1-p)) and collapses to exactly zero at k=0 and k=n, which is precisely where a hit probability lives. TWO THINGS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: (1) the first draft's reference figures for 7-of-20 were recalled wrong (0.18106/0.56890); an independent evaluation at z=1.9599639845400536 gives 0.1811918241/0.5671457233, matching the implementation to 10 digits, so the TEST was corrected and the code was not; (2) at k=n the exact upper bound is denom/denom=1 but the rounded sum lands one ulp low at 0.9999999999999999, so the endpoints are returned exactly, with a test asserting the far bound is still strictly interior. A NaN impact throws rather than scoring as a miss, since counting a diverged solve would bias p-hat downward by exactly the failure rate. Independence of replicates is assumed and undetectable from the counts; documented as the caller's obligation, and the error direction is too-narrow. 24 new tests. tasks.title: One-sided finite-difference stencil at an active bound in shootingJacobian
tasks.validation: no residual evaluation outside the box during a projected solve; Jacobian accuracy at a face unchanged elsewhere
tasks.notes:
Filed 2026-08-11 (17th run) by P5.16, which measured it rather than assumed it. `constrainedShooting`'s projection strategy keeps every ITERATE inside the box, but `shootingJacobian` differences the residual about the iterate and those difference steps are not projected: on the speed-capped exhibit, 5 of 56 evaluations land outside, every one 4.8444e-4 m/s past a 70 m/s cap -- exactly one difference step in the speed column. NOT masking anything today and not urgent: the residual is perfectly well defined just outside that cap, so the Jacobian is correct and P5.16's answers are feasible. It becomes a real defect at a bound that marks the edge of the MODEL'S DOMAIN rather than a machine limit -- a non-negative speed, or an elevation at which the terminal event cannot fire -- where the stencil evaluates an aim with no trajectory, the residual comes back ok:false, and the whole Jacobian fails with `evaluation-failed` at an otherwise healthy iterate. Whoever takes it: give JacobianOptions a feasible-region hook and switch that column to a one-sided (inward) difference when the stencil would cross a face, and note in the doc that a one-sided step drops the central scheme's truncation order from O(h^2) to O(h) AT THAT FACE ONLY -- which is the honest trade and needs to be measured, not asserted, since P5.05's whole comment is about how step-size error behaves here.

CLAIMED 2026-08-17 (30th run), ahead of P5.24 by seq. Every other open correctness item is parked on a human decision -- P0.99 on ADR-016's three options, P0.103 (filed as P1.00) on a resting-contact model blueprint 4.9 does not specify, P0.101 on a rebound-speed cutoff restitution.ts has none of -- so this is the highest-priority item an unattended run can actually finish. P5.24 remains the next task by seq and remains marked optional in its own title.

DONE 2026-08-17 (30th run). `JacobianOptions` gains an opt-in `feasible?: (aim: Aim) => boolean`; omitted, every number this module produces is unchanged (asserted bit-for-bit, not merely to a tolerance). Given, the rule is: (1) the hook engages only at a FEASIBLE base aim, because at an infeasible one "inward" has no single meaning; (2) per column, keep the requested scheme when every point it needs is feasible; (3) otherwise difference inward -- backward when only aim-h is feasible, forward when only aim+h is -- sharing one base evaluation; (4) a column that goes one-sided RE-DERIVES its step for first order (scale*eps^(1/2) rather than scale*eps^(1/3)), unless the caller pinned it, since the plateau sweeps depend on pinned steps being honoured verbatim; (5) when neither side is feasible the region is narrower than the step, so the requested scheme runs unchanged. `ShootingJacobian.stencils` reports per column which stencil actually ran, so a caller measuring a convergence rate through a face is not measuring second-order behaviour that is not there. The fallback is never automatic on a FAILED EVALUATION -- that would be exactly the invisible accuracy loss the module comment says it exists to prevent -- it happens only when the caller has declared where the region is.

`constrainedShooting`'s projection strategy now passes the hook automatically, reusing `aimActiveSet(...).feasible` rather than re-deriving "inside the box", so the predicate the stencil obeys and the one the answer is judged against are the same code with the same tolerance. An explicit hook from the caller wins: a caller may know a tighter domain than the box, since an elevation at which the terminal event cannot fire is not an `AimBounds` face.

VALIDATION, both clauses measured. "No residual evaluation outside the box during a projected solve": the P5.16 exhibit (400 m target, 70 m/s cap) is re-run with every aim the residual sees recorded and judged against the bounds afterwards -- 0 of 56 outside, was 5 of 56. "Jacobian accuracy at a face unchanged elsewhere": with the hook supplied but not binding the matrix, steps and evaluation count are bit-for-bit identical to no hook at all; the speed column is `toBe`-identical when the theta column falls back; and the capped solve still converges to the same miss (116.76 m).
