tasks.title: 76 stale claude/* branches on the remote; CLAUDE.md asks for none, and this environment cannot delete refs
tasks.validation: git ls-remote --heads origin | grep -c refs/heads/claude/ returns 0 (or a documented, deliberate few)
tasks.notes:
Filed 2026-08-11 (18th run). CLAUDE.md: "Don't leave long-lived claude/* branches around after a task finishes." The remote currently carries 76 of them, 7 of which are fully merged into main and so are pure cruft; the rest are unmerged and need a human to decide whether anything on them is wanted before they go. THE 18TH RUN COULD NOT COMPLY and this is the honest record of that: it worked on claude/upbeat-ride-uhifsa, merged it into main and pushed main (fast-forward, e84f8ab..8536d49), deleted the local branch, and then found that `git push origin --delete` fails in this sandbox with "fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly" on every attempt (4 retries with 2/4/8/16 s backoff). The GitHub MCP server exposes create_branch but no delete-branch tool, so there is no second route. The leftover ref points at the OLD main (e84f8ab) and is fully merged, so it holds nothing and costs nothing but noise. A human with normal push rights can clear all 7 merged ones in one command; the CI/agent credential apparently cannot delete refs at all, which is worth fixing at the permission level or the policy will keep being unmeetable.

RE-TESTED 2026-08-17 (30th run), and the diagnosis is now sharper than "the remote end hung up". `git push origin --delete claude/upbeat-ride-bd97il` on a branch fully merged into main fails with `error: RPC failed; HTTP 403 curl 22` FIRST, and the sideband disconnect the 18th run recorded is the consequence of that 403, not an independent network fault. So this is a PERMISSION denial on ref deletion, not flakiness and not something a retry or a backoff can reach -- which confirms the 18th run's guess and makes the fix unambiguous: the credential needs delete-ref rights, or the policy line in CLAUDE.md needs to acknowledge that agent sessions cannot meet it. Note the same session pushed to `main` and to a `claude/*` branch in this repository without trouble, so it is deletion specifically that is refused, not writes in general.

RE-TESTED 2026-08-18 (35th run), third independent confirmation, and the count has grown: `git ls-remote --heads origin | grep -c refs/heads/claude/` now returns **82**, up from the 76 this task was filed with. `git push origin --delete claude/upbeat-ride-ywti18` again failed with `send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet` / `the remote end hung up unexpectedly`, and the GitHub MCP server still exposes `create_branch` with no delete counterpart (re-checked, not assumed). Note the exit status is **0** and the last line printed is `Everything up-to-date`, so a script that only checks `$?` will conclude the deletion succeeded -- worth knowing for whoever automates the cleanup. ONE OF THE 82 IS THIS RUN'S OWN, and the honest attribution matters: the 35th run created `claude/upbeat-ride-ywti18` through the API as a write-access probe before it had any commit to put there, then could not remove it. Its commits landed on `main` directly by fast-forward, so the branch holds nothing. The lesson is the same one the telehealth repo's status file reached independently on the same date: **do not create the branch until there is a commit for it.**

tasks.title: chunked-integration.test.ts asserts a wall-clock budget (maxSliceMs < 10) and flakes on CI runners
tasks.validation: the correctness suite contains no assertion that can fail from machine load alone; the 10 ms cooperative-yield target is still measured and still reported
tasks.notes:
Filed 2026-08-11 (18th run) after it turned main red. `packages/solverkit/src/chunked-integration.test.ts` line 318, P2.40, asserts `expect(maxSliceMs).toBeLessThan(10)` on a value from `performance.now()`. On CI run 31506207711 it measured 12.668292 ms and failed; 1950 of 1951 tests passed.

IT IS FLAKY, AND THE EVIDENCE IS UNUSUALLY CLEAN rather than circumstantial. The 18th run pushed two commits two minutes apart. 8536d49 -- which contains ALL of the run's code, the whole of P5.17 -- was CI **success** (run 31505994904). 5bafdff, the commit that FAILED, changes only CHANGELOG.md and ROADMAP.json: markdown and JSON text, no code at all, nothing under packages/solverkit, and nothing that any bundler or test even reads. A text-only commit cannot slow down a chunked integrator, so the difference between the two runs is runner load. Main's CI history shows the same intermittency before this run: failures at f951754 and 79322ba on 2026-08-10 sit between successes. CONFIRMED BY RE-RUN: `rerun_failed_jobs` on run 31506207711 -- the SAME commit, the same tree, not one byte changed -- came back **success**. A test that passes and fails on identical input is flaky by definition, and main is green again without anything being edited to make it so.

DO NOT JUST RAISE THE NUMBER. Whatever the threshold is, a wall-clock assertion on a shared runner can always lose a timeslice, so a bigger constant buys a longer gap between flakes rather than fixing the class of problem. The 10 ms cooperative-yield target is a real and worthwhile property -- it is what makes the UI responsive during a 1e6-step run -- so the fix is to stop expressing it as a pass/fail assertion in the correctness suite. Options, for a human to choose between: move the timing to `pnpm bench:solverkit`, which already reports regressions as SOFT WARNINGS and would have surfaced this without turning main red; or keep the test but assert the deterministic half (slice count, step count, status, that the generator yields at all) and report the milliseconds without asserting them. The correctness assertions in that test are sound and should be kept exactly as they are. SIGHTING 2026-08-17 (33rd run), and it is the cleanest evidence yet: CI run 226 attempt 1 at e632668 failed this assertion at 13.065580 ms (2252 of 2253 passed), and attempt 2 of the SAME run at the SAME commit, with nothing changed in between, passed. Same tree, same code, red then green -- load-sensitivity observed directly rather than inferred from two different commits. The 33rd run's own change (P0.94) is ruled out as the cause: it touched no file under packages/solverkit, the suite was 2253/2253 locally minutes before, and the format:check step it added passed, since it runs before Test in the job. The job was re-run rather than the assertion weakened; this task still needs a human to choose between the two options above.

SIGHTING 2026-08-23 (44th run), and it is the cleanest cross-over evidence yet. CI run 244 at 07e7b23 failed ATTEMPT 1 here -- chunked-integration.test.ts:318, maxSliceMs 11.982128 against the 10 ms budget, 2562/2563 passing. rerun_failed_jobs on the identical tree produced ATTEMPT 2, in which THIS TEST PASSED and a different one failed instead (solver-lab-route.test.tsx:91, see P0.106). Two attempts of one commit, two different failing tests, each green in the other attempt: neither is a regression, both are load-sensitive. The 44th run's diff touched packages/engine only and the timed region here is a dim-1 decay model with a mock Euler stepper, reached from that diff solely as one extra barrel re-export evaluated at import time and never inside the measurement. The full suite was green locally at 2563/2563 before the push. STILL NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: this needs the human decision the notes above describe, and an unattended run must not pick between the two options or raise the constant. CLOSING THE LOOP: the commit recording this went green as CI run 245 at cfc2df8, all 35 steps, so main recovered without anything being edited to make it -- a third data point on essentially the same tree.

REPRODUCTION RECIPE FOUND 2026-08-23 (45th run), while validating P0.106. This flake had only ever been seen sporadically on CI; it can now be provoked locally on demand. RECIPE: run the FULL `pnpm test` suite with external CPU load -- two of four cores busy-looping was enough. It reproduced in 2 of 4 such runs (suite duration 136-140 s under load against 100-103 s unloaded). BOTH HALVES ARE NECESSARY: the same file run STANDALONE under the same load passed 3/3, and the full suite UNLOADED passed 3/3, so it needs suite parallelism AND external load together. That is consistent with the filing -- it is a wall-clock assertion measuring a machine that is busy doing something else. The measured maxSliceMs value was not captured in those runs (the output was filtered to the failure line), so no number is claimed here beyond CI run 244's 11.982128 ms against the 10 ms budget. STILL NEEDS A HUMAN: this changes nothing about the decision, which is whether the cooperative-yield target is asserted or merely measured and reported. Nothing was weakened to get the other runs green.

tasks.title: Ground-level launch: impact event fires at t=0, so solveArcs silently returns wrong low arcs for short targets
tasks.validation: a launch from exactly y=0 produces the closed-form range at every elevation in (0, pi/2), including elevations whose entire flight fits inside the integrator's first step; solveArcs' low-arc downrangeMiss is at tolerance for targets from 1 m out to the envelope
tasks.notes:
Filed 2026-08-15 (24th run), found while building P5.23's exhibit. NOT FIXED HERE: it is outside P5.23 and the fix belongs to the event detector, which is engine/solverkit surgery.

SYMPTOM. With launchPoint [0, 0] (exactly ground level), createShootingResidual returns ok:true, timeOfFlight:0 and impact === the launch point for every elevation below about 0.1229 rad at v0 = 60 m/s. The range function therefore reads 0 across that whole band. solveArcs inherits it: for a 50 m target at 60 m/s drag-free it returns a LOW ARC of theta = 0.122892 whose downrangeMiss is 39.32 m, with iterations: 39 (brentRoot ran to its limit on a function with a cliff in it) and no error of any kind. For a 25 m target the low arc misses by the full 25 m. Targets at 100 m and beyond are correct, and both high arcs are correct throughout, which is why this has stayed invisible.

MECHANISM, measured rather than guessed. The ground-impact event g(y) = y is exactly satisfied at t = 0 when the launcher sits on the deck. The detector only skips that root once the first adaptive step ends with y still positive; when the ENTIRE FLIGHT fits inside the first step, the only sign change in that step is the one at t = 0, and it localizes there. The threshold matches exactly: the residual dump shows nSteps: 1 with a first step of about 1.5 s, and the cutoff elevation 0.1229 rad is precisely the elevation whose drag-free flight time 2 v0 sin(theta)/g equals 1.5 s. Above the cutoff, tof matches 2 v0 sin(theta)/g to every printed digit; below it, tof is exactly 0.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE THAT IT IS THE t=0 ROOT AND NOTHING ELSE: raising the launcher to y = 1e-9 m fixes it completely. At theta = 0.05 rad, h = 0 gives tof 0 and x 0; h = 1e-9 gives tof 0.611575 and x 36.6486, which is the closed form to six figures. A nanometre of clearance is the entire difference.

BLAST RADIUS. Everything that shoots at a short target from ground level: solveArcs (P5.08), and through it trajectory-designer's (v0, R) -> theta lock (P5.22), basin-of-attraction (P5.20) and the target marker (P5.21). The existing arcs.test.ts suite does not catch it because its targets are far enough out that every candidate elevation flies longer than one step. Any test for this must include a target short enough that the flight fits inside the first step, which is the case the current suite has no example of.

SUGGESTED FIX. Reject a terminal event localized at (or within a step-size epsilon of) t0 when the event function is already zero at t0, and continue the search into the interior of the step -- i.e. an event active at the initial condition needs a departure before a crossing counts. A guard on timeOfFlight > 0 in the residual would mask the symptom rather than fix the detector, and would turn a wrong answer into a failed one for these aims instead of a right one.

P5.23's ill-conditioning module already refuses to difference across this region (a zero flight time is rejected as hard as a failed solve) because differencing across the cliff produced 4.5e5 m/rad against a drag-free maximum of 2 v0^2/g = 734 -- finite, positive and plausible-looking. That guard is local to that module and is not a fix for this.

25th run, claimed 2026-08-15. MECHANISM CONFIRMED AND REFINED by reproduction before any edit. The 24th run's note says the first step is 'about 1.5 s'; it is 6 s, and 1.5 s is its first interior sample. `integrate` starts at h = (tFinal - t0)/DEFAULT_STEP_COUNT = 600/100 = 6 s, and DOPRI5 integrates drag-free flight EXACTLY (constant acceleration makes y(t) a quadratic, which a 5th-order RK reproduces to round-off), so the error estimate is ~0 and that 6 s step is accepted whole. scanStepForEvents then samples theta = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 -- t = 0, 1.5, 3, 4.5, 6 s. Measured cutoff at v0=60: theta=0.12 (tof 1.4649) fails, theta=0.125 (tof 1.5256) succeeds; 1.5 s is exactly the 0.25 sample. So the condition is tof < h/4, not tof < h.

TWO faults compose, and the second is why simply refusing the t=0 root is not the fix. (1) g(t0) = y = 0 EXACTLY at ground level, so the pair (g=0 at theta=0, g<0 at theta=0.25) reads as a falling crossing and brentRoot, handed gLo = 0, returns the left endpoint without a single iteration. (2) the entire excursion lies inside [0, 0.25] and NO sample sees it -- so deleting the spurious bracket alone turns a wrong answer into a missed event (ok:false), which the 24th run's note explicitly warns against. Both have to be fixed together: the zero at the step start must stop anchoring a bracket, AND the first sub-interval must be sampled finely enough to bracket the real crossing.

FIXED 2026-08-15 (25th run). `packages/solverkit/src/event-detection.ts`, in `scanStepForEvents`. Validation criterion met: at v0 = 80 m/s from exactly y = 0, `solveArcs` now returns both arcs with |downrangeMiss| < 1e-8 for targets at 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 130, 200, 400 and 600 m, and each low arc lands on 1/2 asin(gR/v0^2) to 9 decimal places. The residual's flight time matches 2 v0 sin(theta)/g to 9 dp at every elevation tested from 1e-4 to 1.5 rad. 29 new tests; suite 2198/2198 across 237 files.

THE FIX IS TWO CHANGES, AND EITHER ALONE IS WRONG. (1) A zero at the step's start no longer anchors a bracket when the state DEPARTS the surface -- previously (g=0 at theta=0, g<0 at theta=0.25) read as a falling crossing and brentRoot, handed gLo = 0, returned the left endpoint without a single iteration. (2) The active-at-start case gains DEPARTURE_THETAS, a 12-rung geometric ladder inside the first sub-interval (theta = 0.25*2^-k, k = 12..1), because the real crossing can lie entirely inside it where nothing was sampled. Without (2), fixing (1) turns a wrong answer into a MISSED event, which the 24th run's note explicitly warned against; that was observed, not reasoned about -- the first draft did exactly that and failed 26 tests.

WHAT DECIDES WHETHER THE t0 ZERO COUNTS IS `crossesInDirection`, NOT A HARD-CODED SIGN. If the state leaves THROUGH the surface (the side the event's `direction` counts as a crossing), t0 really is the crossing and it fires exactly as before. A horizontal launch from exactly ground level has v_y = 0, goes straight down, and lands at t=0 with zero range -- that is the right answer and not a defect. It is also not a curiosity: `solveArcs` evaluates theta = 0 at its own lower angle bound on EVERY call, so the first draft's blanket suppression broke every ground-launch test in arcs.test.ts. Routing the decision through `direction` also makes the rule correct for any event rather than for the ground specifically: an event declaring "any" still fires at t0 either way, which is its declaration honoured rather than this bug leaking back in.

COSTS NOTHING ON AN ORDINARY STEP, asserted by a test that counts `g` calls: g(t0) != 0 skips the ladder entirely and leaves the original five-sample scan byte-for-byte in behaviour.

THE LADDER HAS A FLOOR AND IT IS DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The last rung is theta = 0.25*2^-12 ~ 6.1e-5 of a step; on the default 6 s initial step that resolves a flight of about 0.37 ms, which at 60 m/s is an elevation around 3e-6 rad and a range around 2 cm. Below that the excursion is not bracketed and the t0 crossing is reported instead, so the answer degrades continuously to the theta -> 0 limit rather than failing.

ALSO CORRECTED: the 24th run's note says the first step is "about 1.5 s". It is 6 s -- `integrate` starts at (tFinal - t0)/DEFAULT_STEP_COUNT = 600/100 -- and 1.5 s is its first interior sample. DOPRI5 accepts that 6 s step whole because constant acceleration makes y(t) a quadratic it integrates exactly, so the error estimate is ~0. The real condition is tof < h/4, and the measured cutoff (theta 0.12 fails, 0.125 passes at v0 = 60) is exactly the 0.25 sample.

NOT INVESTIGATED, AND WORTH A LOOK BY WHOEVER IS NEXT IN SOLVERKIT: restitution bouncing resumes integration from a state sitting exactly on the ground (the action reflects v_y, leaving y at 0), so every bounce after the first is an active-at-start step and hit fault (1) too. This fix covers it by construction and `chunked-integration`/bounce tests stayed green, but no test in the suite specifically exercises a bounce whose flight is shorter than a quarter step. Filed as P0.98.

tasks.title: No test covers a restitution bounce whose flight is shorter than a quarter step
tasks.validation: a bouncing solve whose later bounces each last less than h/4 conserves the expected number of impacts and their times, against the closed form for a drag-free bouncing ball
tasks.notes:
Filed 2026-08-15 (25th run) by P0.97, which fixed the class of bug this would catch but did not add a test at this angle. A restitution bounce resumes integration from a state sitting EXACTLY on the ground -- restitutionBounceAction reflects v_y and leaves y at 0 -- so every bounce after the first is an 'event active at the step start' step and had the same two faults P0.97 describes: the zero at t0 anchoring a bracket that brentRoot resolves to t0 without iterating, and a short flight lying entirely inside the first sub-interval. As a drag-free bouncing ball loses height geometrically, its later bounces are ALL short, so this is the regime rather than an edge of it. NOT KNOWN TO BE BROKEN: P0.97's fix covers the mechanism by construction and every existing bounce test stayed green, so this is a coverage gap and not a reported defect -- which is exactly why it is worth pinning before someone touches scanStepForEvents again. Whoever takes it: a drag-free ball dropped from h0 with restitution e has closed-form impact times t_n = sqrt(2 h0/g) (1 + 2 e (1-e^n)/(1-e)), so the whole sequence is checkable without a reference implementation. Choose h0 and tspan so the later bounces fall below h/4 = 1.5 s on the default step.

ATTEMPTED 2026-08-15 (26th run), RETURNED TO TODO -- the task's premise does not hold from the adaptive driver, which is a finding rather than a failure to deliver. Measured: the driver truncates each step to land on the localized event, so the step shrinks in lockstep with the bounces. Over both an e=0.5 and an e=0.2 drop-from-rest sequence the ratio flight/step is 5.00 at EVERY bounce -- about five steps per flight, never a fraction of one -- even where the flight is 1.3e-4 s against a nominal step of 0.12. Direct proof the sub-interval path is untouched: emptying P0.97's DEPARTURE_THETAS ladder leaves the whole new test file green. So the regime needs a FIXED step, and that is blocked by P0.99: a stepper with no dense output has event detection silently disabled. Do P0.99 first, then this becomes reachable with ClassicalRK4Stepper at a fixed h. Landed meanwhile: restitution-bounce-short-flights.test.ts, 5 cases pinning impact TIMES against the closed form t_n = t0(1 + 2e(1-e^n)/(1-e)) to 1e-12 relative and the resolved impact count -- coverage that did not exist, but NOT this task's criterion.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-16 (27th run), without P0.99 being fixed. The fixed step this task needs is reachable today via `new HermiteDenseOutputStepper(new ClassicalRK4Stepper())`, which arms events on a fixed step and localizes a ground impact to the closed-form time -- now tested in event-detection-requires-dense-output.test.ts. P0.99 does not have to land first; only the wrapper does. || DONE 2026-08-16 (29th run). The regime is real, it is reachable, and reaching it needed a FIXED step -- which is the one thing the 26th run's groundwork block could not do. An adaptive driver truncates every step to land on the localized event, so the live step shrinks in lockstep with the bounces and flight/step sits at ~5 forever; with `h` pinned by the caller the flights decay geometrically past it. A fixed-step stepper reaches event detection at all only through HermiteDenseOutputStepper (integrate's hasEvents guard needs stepper.interpolant, and no bare fixed-step stepper has one -- that is P0.99, still open), so the test wraps ClassicalRK4Stepper. Added 8 cases to restitution-bounce-short-flights.test.ts, describe.each over h=0.12 and h=0.25: at h=0.12 the last two impacts arrive from flights of 0.135h and 0.027h, at h=0.25 the last three from 0.065h, 0.013h and 0.003h, and EVERY impact time matches the closed form t_n = t0 (1 + 2e(1-e^n)/(1-e)) to within 5e-16 relative -- RK4 is exact on a quadratic and the Hermite cubic reproduces it exactly, so the only error is the root find's. TWO PERTURBATIONS, applied and reverted, both caught by the same 2 cases: emptying DEPARTURE_THETAS, and forcing activeAtStart=false (removing P0.97's suppression). Worth knowing which case is load-bearing -- only the h=0.12 pair goes red under both; h=0.25 pins the regime but is insensitive to the ladder, and the counts stay green under both perturbations because the solve still reports the same NUMBER of impacts, just at wrong times. The closed-form assertion is what notices. COUNTS ARE ASSERTED AS LOWER BOUNDS, NOT PINNED, and report.status is deliberately not asserted at all: see P0.101, filed this run -- both are 'ok'/5 today only because the bounce sequence dies early, and the honest fix changes both.

tasks.title: Event detection is silently disabled for any stepper without dense output, and the solve still reports ok
tasks.validation: a terminal ground impact is detected, or the solve fails loudly, when integrating with a stepper that has no interpolant; no configuration returns ok with the projectile below ground
tasks.notes:
Filed 2026-08-15 (26th run) by P0.98, measured not inferred. integrate.ts line ~287: `const hasEvents = events !== undefined && events.length > 0 && stepper.interpolant !== undefined`. ClassicalRK4Stepper (and every other fixed-step stepper in the package -- explicit/semi-implicit Euler, Heun, midpoint, SDIRK2, the symplectic ones) exposes no `interpolant`, so hasEvents is false and the ENTIRE event block is skipped. Nothing warns. REPRO, both at h=0.12 over tspan [0,12], same model, no restitution so ground-impact is terminal, y0 = [0, 5, 3, 0]: with createDormandPrince54Stepper the solve stops correctly at t=1.009810 with y=1.0e-15; with ClassicalRK4Stepper it runs the full span to tFinal=12 and ends at y=-7.011e+2 -- the projectile falls 701 m through the ground -- and reports status 'ok'. This is the same SHAPE of defect as P0.97: a silently wrong answer with ok:true, no error, at a configuration a caller can reach without doing anything unusual. It is arguably worse, because P0.97 needed a near-zero elevation to trigger and this needs only a stepper choice. Whoever takes it: the guard is presumably deliberate -- root localization needs dense output -- but silently dropping the events is not the right response to that. Options are to fail loudly at init when a model declares events and the stepper cannot localize them, or to fall back to a Hermite interpolant built from the step endpoints and their derivatives (which every explicit stepper can supply) rather than requiring the stepper's own. Decide in an ADR; do not just widen the guard. Note HermiteDenseOutputStepper already exists and is referenced in integrate.ts's own comment, so the fallback may be closer than it looks.

CLAIMED 2026-08-16 (27th run), ahead of P5.24 by seq. Same justification the 26th run recorded for taking P0.98 ahead of it: this is a correctness bug that returns ok:true with a physically impossible answer, and the repo's priority order puts correctness above the next task by seq -- P5.24 is additionally marked optional in its own title. The 26th run's changelog names P0.99 as the next task for exactly this reason.

ATTEMPTED 2026-08-16 (27th run), RETURNED TO TODO -- both remedies this task's own notes proposed were implemented far enough to measure, and BOTH ARE WRONG. See ADR-016 (Proposed), which now records the measurements rather than a decision.
  (1) THROW when the stepper has no interpolant: 88 tests fail across 31 files. Not odd callers -- convergence-harness, euler-global-error, work-precision-harness, golden-trajectories, reference-solution, energy-drift-study, stability-boundary-sweep, phase-portrait, every fixed-step stepper's own test, and the app routes over them. Structural reason: a convergence-order or energy-drift study MUST hold h fixed, and createPlanarProjectileModel ALWAYS attaches a ground-impact event, so 'event-bearing model + fixed-step stepper' is the normal case in this repo, not a caller error. Throwing outlaws the platform's own pedagogy.
  (2) AUTO-WRAP in HermiteDenseOutputStepper: worse. Those same studies would keep running but with the terminal event ARMED, truncating them at ground impact and silently changing every convergence rate, energy-drift figure and golden trajectory they are pinned against. Also contradicts the wrapper's opt-in design (SS5.1(c), ~1 extra rhs call/step) and drops localized event times to 3rd-order Hermite error the caller never opted into.
  ROOT CAUSE OF BOTH FAILURES: the API cannot express whether THIS caller wants events; the stepper choice decides it invisibly. The fix is an API change, not a guard change. ADR-016 sketches three options (tri-state cfg.events; an eventsArmed diagnostic on SolveReport; post-hoc terminal-guard evaluation) and chooses none. NOTE: this task's validation criterion is NOT achievable by a local edit to integrate.ts -- expect to update call sites.
  LANDED ANYWAY: event-detection-requires-dense-output.test.ts (7 tests) characterizing the bug -- the measured wrong numbers, the same failure on explicit Euler/Heun/midpoint, the working HermiteDenseOutputStepper workaround, and the legitimate fixed-step-plus-event-model pattern pinned in the same file so the cost of the throw sits next to the bug that seems to justify it. Its assertions are the DEFECT, not the spec: rewrite the file when fixing, do not delete it. integrate.ts's comment now carries the trap and points at ADR-016; no behaviour changed.

tasks.title: After the last resolvable restitution bounce the ball tunnels through the ground and free-falls, still reporting ok
tasks.validation: a bouncing solve run past its Zeno accumulation point ends with the projectile at rest on the ground, or fails loudly; it never reports ok with y far below zero
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-15 (26th run) by P0.98, measured on the adaptive driver. A drag-free bouncing ball is Zeno: impacts accumulate at t_inf = t0(1 + 2e/(1-e)) with infinitely many in finite time, so no integrator resolves them all -- that part is expected and is not the bug. The bug is what happens after the last resolvable bounce: the ball passes THROUGH the ground and free-falls for the rest of the span. Measured at H0=5, e=0.2, tspan [0,12], default step: 7 impacts resolved, the last at t=1.514683 against t_inf=1.514715, then yFinal = -5.391e+2 with status 'ok'. At e=0.5 the same shape, yFinal = -3.967e+2. Every resolved impact time is correct to 2.1e-15 relative, so localization is not at fault -- the sequence simply runs out of resolution and nothing catches the ball. Related to but distinct from P0.99: this one reproduces on the ADAPTIVE path with dense output present and events firing normally. Whoever takes it: the physical answer is a resting contact once the bounce energy falls below a threshold, which is a modelling decision (blueprint 4.9 does not currently specify one) and wants an ADR rather than an ad-hoc epsilon. Until then a caller integrating a bouncing trajectory past t_inf gets nonsense with no indication.

tasks.title: Root `pnpm build` script is broken under pnpm 11: `pnpm -r ... run build` parses `run` as the script name

tasks.notes:

tasks.title: A restitution bounce is silently missed when the localized impact leaves y a hair below the terrain; the projectile then falls through the ground and the solve still reports ok
tasks.validation: no bouncing configuration returns status ok with the projectile below the terrain; a drag-free bouncing ball either resolves impacts until a documented Zeno cutoff and then rests on the ground, or fails loudly
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-16 (29th run) by P0.98, MEASURED NOT INFERRED, and it is the same shape as P0.97 and P0.99: a silently wrong answer with ok:true at a configuration a caller reaches without doing anything unusual. MECHANISM: scanStepForEvents decides an event is active at the step start with `g0 === 0` EXACTLY. But the state a restitution bounce resumes from is Brent's localized root, whose g_gnd is zero only to within the root find's own error -- measured at up to ~1e-15 m and of EITHER SIGN. restitutionBounceAction reflects v_y and passes position through, so that residual becomes the next step's starting height. When it is NEGATIVE the step starts nominally below ground: activeAtStart is false, the DEPARTURE_THETAS ladder is not armed, the scan falls back to INTERIOR_THETAS = [0.25, 0.5, 0.75], and a flight shorter than a quarter step ends before the first of them. g<0 at theta=0 and g<0 at every sample after it is no sign change, so the impact is missed, the ball keeps accelerating downward, and nothing ever fires again. REPRO, drag-free ball dropped from y=5 with e=0.2 over tspan [0,12], HermiteDenseOutputStepper(ClassicalRK4Stepper): at h=0.4 and h=0.5 the sequence stops after 2 impacts and the solve returns status 'ok' with yFinal = -5.45e+2 -- the ball 545 m underground. The same run at h=0.12 gives 5 impacts and h=0.8 gives 6, so the failure is NOT monotone in h; it depends on the sign of a rounding residual, which is why it has hidden this long. THE ADAPTIVE PATH IS NOT EXEMPT: createDormandPrince54Stepper on the same problem resolves 7 impacts and also ends at yFinal = -5.39e+2 with 'ok'. The committed test above it pinned that 7 and never looked at yFinal. CANDIDATE FIX, IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED THIS RUN, THEN REVERTED ON PURPOSE: snap the post-bounce height back onto the terrain in createGroundImpactEvent (out[Y] = terrain.height(out[X])). It is exact rather than a tolerance -- the impact is ON the surface by the event's definition, so this removes the root find's error instead of accommodating it, and it restores the invariant event-detection.ts's own comment already assumes. It works: the fall-through is gone and y stays exactly 0. BUT it then exposes the Zeno tail underneath -- the ball bounces ~20000 times, burns the whole step budget, tFinal converges to the accumulation point t_inf = 1.5147 and the solve returns status 'failed'. So the snap alone trades a silent wrong answer for a loud failure on EVERY bouncing solve. That is the trade DEPARTURE_THETAS' own comment endorses in general, but making the ordinary bouncing case fail is a product decision, not a bug fix, so this run did not take it unattended -- same reasoning the 27th run applied to P0.99. WHOEVER TAKES IT: the snap is the right first half and is cheap; the decision to make is the second half -- a Zeno cutoff (stop bouncing and transition to resting contact below some rebound speed, which needs a threshold with a physical justification, not a magic number) versus letting it fail loudly. Note restitution.ts has no cutoff of any kind today. Decide the cutoff, then land both together, then tighten P0.98's lower-bound assertions and the 7-impact pin above into exact counts.

tasks.title: `pnpm check:cross-engine-drift` silently overwrites the committed results file with a degraded record when run outside CI
tasks.validation: running the drift check in an environment without Playwright browsers leaves scripts/cross-engine-drift-results.json unmodified, or writes only where it is explicitly asked to
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-17 (30th run), fixed 2026-08-17 (31st run). DEFECT: `scripts/measure-cross-engine-drift.mjs` ended by unconditionally writing the COMMITTED `scripts/cross-engine-drift-results.json`. Run from the documented pre-push gate in any environment lacking Playwright's exact browser revisions, it replaced a real chromium measurement (status: measured, 141.0.7390.37, maxRelativeDrift 0, bit-identical over 101 rows x 5 series) with two `status: unavailable` records carrying launcher stack traces, rewrote the provenance paragraph, printed 'All measured engines are within the drift threshold' and exited 0 -- vacuously true of zero measured engines. A soft-warn check downgraded committed evidence and reported success. FIX: writing is now opt-in behind `--record`; CI passes it (.github/workflows/ci.yml), a local gate run does not, so the gate can no longer write at all. A `--record` run additionally refuses to write when zero engines measured, so a CI run whose `playwright install` failed cannot erase a good record either -- the flag buys the right to write a measurement, not to erase one. The zero-measured case now warns 'No engine could be measured ... This is not a pass' instead of the vacuous all-clear. VALIDATION: 5 tests in packages/validation/src/cross-engine-drift-record.test.ts run the real script as a subprocess and assert the committed file is byte-identical afterwards, in both flag modes. They force PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH at a nonexistent path where 'nothing measurable' must hold deterministically, so the --record case behaves the same on the CI runner and cannot itself perform the write it forbids; one test asserts CI still passes --record, so making writing opt-in cannot silently freeze the committed measurement. Mutation-tested: restoring the unconditional write fails 3 of them, restoring the vacuous all-clear fails 2, dropping --record from CI fails 1. Confirmed first-hand this run -- the full suite runs the script 4 times and left the results file unmodified.

tasks.title: A raised PlatformTarget can never be hit, because the shooting residual is read at the ground impact; the solve stalls instead of saying so
tasks.validation: either a shooting solve against a target above the launch datum can converge, or it fails with a status naming the reason rather than "stalled"
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-18 (35th run) by P5.25, MEASURED NOT INFERRED. createShootingResidual reads the miss at impactPoint(trajectory), and createFlight requires the model to declare a TERMINAL event -- for createPlanarProjectileModel that is ground impact at y = 0. So for any target whose centre sits above the launch datum, the residual's vertical component is pinned at -(target height) for EVERY aim and no aim can reduce it. REPRO, now pinned as the golden case 'newton-raised-platform-unreachable': PlatformTarget at [120, 15], halfExtents [2], quadratic drag, initial aim (0.9 rad, 60 m/s) -> status 'stalled', converged false, merit 14.999999999999991 after 4 iterations and 26 evaluations. THIS IS NOT THE SILENT-WRONG-ANSWER SHAPE of P0.97/P0.99/P0.101: converged is false and the merit is honest, so a caller who checks is not misled. What is wrong is narrower -- targets.ts documents PlatformTarget as modelling 'landing on top of a platform', and that is unreachable through this entry point, while the failure a caller gets ('stalled') describes the line search rather than the cause. WHOEVER TAKES IT: the fix is not in the solver. Either the model needs a terminal event at the target surface rather than at the ground (which makes the target part of the dynamics, an ADR-sized change), or createShootingResidual should reject a target above the launch datum up front with a message naming the terminal event, or the residual should be read from a non-terminal crossing of the target's height. Decide which before writing code. Note the store's entry pins the CURRENT behaviour: when this is fixed, rewrite that entry rather than deleting it, the same instruction P0.99's characterization test carries.

tasks.title: Build-heavy tests flake against their hook/test timeouts under the parallel suite; raising the timeouts weakens nothing
tasks.validation: the full `pnpm test` suite passes repeatedly on a loaded container without any build-heavy test crossing a timeout, and no assertion was changed to achieve it
tasks.notes:
Filed 2026-08-18 (35th run) by P5.25. This is the task the P4.38 changelog entry explicitly 'left for a task that claims it' and which was never actually filed; it is filed now so it stops being rediscovered. THE CLASS: tests that vite-build the app and/or launch Chromium run close to their limits and cross them when the 244-file suite runs in parallel. P4.38 measured canvas-viewport.test.ts at 48.6 s against a 60 s HOOK timeout and lazy-plotly-pane.bundle.test.ts at 22.1 s against a 30 s TEST timeout, and recorded 1 green run in 4. SIGHTING 2026-08-18 (35th run): packages/app/src/app-shell.responsive.test.ts failed with 'Hook timed out in 60000ms' followed by 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading httpServer)' in one full-suite run, and PASSED STANDALONE IN 34.4 s in the same container minutes later -- the same margin story, on a third file. ATTRIBUTION, since the 35th run initially got this wrong and corrected it: that run's own addition is about 1.75 s of test CPU against a suite total that varied between 224.9 s and 296.3 s ACROSS RUNS OF THE SAME TREE, so it is under 1% and well inside the container's own run-to-run variance -- one of its runs finished FASTER than the pre-change baseline and still saw a timeout. These are timeouts, not assertions, so unlike P0.96 raising them weakens nothing and needs no human decision about what is being asserted. Suggested: raise the hook and test timeouts for the build-heavy files specifically (per-file, not globally, so an ordinary unit test that hangs still fails fast) and record the headroom measured. Do NOT conflate this with P0.96, which is a wall-clock ASSERTION and does need a human. SIGHTING 2026-08-22 (40th run): the first full-suite run after adding packages/validation/src/analysis-docs.test.ts reported '1 failed | 248 passed' with the failing file NOT CAPTURED -- the run's tail was read before the failure block, which was the 40th run's own mistake and is recorded so the sighting is not overstated. It did NOT reproduce: three subsequent full runs were 2429/2429 across 249 files, and canvas-viewport.test.ts passed standalone twice. In the run that was captured, canvas-viewport.test.ts took 37.6 s -- the same margin story as P4.38's 48.6 s against the 60 s hook timeout. Attribution: the 40th run's addition is a docs test that only reads files off disk, ~40 ms of test CPU, so it is not a plausible cause beyond adding load. Consistent with this class; not proof, because the file was never identified.

SIGHTING 2026-08-23 (44th run), on a FOURTH file, and this one has a diagnosed mechanism rather than just a margin. CI run 244 attempt 2 at 07e7b23 failed packages/app/src/solver-lab-route.test.tsx:91 with "expected '' to contain 'Explicit (Forward) Euler'" -- an empty derivation panel. The test awaits a REAL dynamic import of KaTeX by spinning a FIXED five macrotask turns (`for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))`) and then asserting. That is a fixed-turn race, not a condition wait: under the parallel suite the import plus module transform needs more turns than five, the panel is still empty, and textContent is ''. It passed 3/3 standalone in the same container minutes later, the same passes-alone-fails-in-suite signature as the app-shell.responsive sighting. Note it is a RACE rather than a timeout, so the 'raise the timeout' remedy does not apply to this file; the equivalent no-decision-needed fix is to poll for the rendered content up to a bounded deadline and then assert exactly the same two things (the heading text and a .katex node), which changes no assertion and removes the dependence on how many event-loop turns a dynamic import happens to take. NOT DONE by the 44th run: it had already claimed P6.02, and this task's own validation criterion demands repeated full-suite runs on a loaded container to verify, which is the task itself rather than a drive-by. CLOSING THE LOOP: CI run 245 at cfc2df8 was green, all 35 steps, so this file passed there too; three runs of near-identical trees gave red/red/green on two different tests, which is the flake signature rather than a regression.

CLAIMED 2026-08-23 (45th run). Taken out of `seq` order deliberately, and the reason is the taskSelection policy's own construction rather than an exception to it: `P0.*` bug filings take minors from 90 upward and are APPENDED, so this task's seq of 304 records when it was filed, not where it belongs in the work order -- the policy's own taskIds note says "Ids are labels, not an ordering". Read literally, first-todo-by-seq would be P6.03, which starts a new Phase 6 feature while a known flake can redden `main` at any commit. The 44th run also ended by naming this task as the one that "needs no decision, only a session that claims it". REMAINING WORK when this note was written: (1) replace solver-lab-route.test.tsx's fixed five-macrotask-turn spin with a bounded-deadline poll, asserting exactly the same two things; (2) raise the per-file hook/test timeouts on the build-heavy files and record the measured headroom; (3) satisfy the validation criterion, which needs repeated full-suite runs on a loaded container.

DONE 2026-08-23 (45th run). Two changes, one per half of the class, and no assertion in any touched file was altered. (1) THE RACE: solver-lab-route.test.tsx's fixed five-macrotask-turn spin is replaced by waitForRenderedDerivation, which polls until the derivation panel is non-empty up to a 20 s deadline. The wait condition is deliberately WEAKER than what the test asserts -- it waits for "non-empty" and the assertions still check the heading text and a real .katex node -- because waiting on the assertion's own condition would make the assertion vacuous. On deadline it now reports "the lazy KaTeX import never resolved (this is a hang, not a slow machine)" instead of an assertion diff against '', which is what sent four sessions looking at the wrong thing; verified by temporarily setting the deadline to 0. (2) THE TIMEOUTS: seven call sites across six build-heavy files, hooks 60 s -> 180 s and bundle tests 30 s -> 90 s, per-file so an ordinary unit test that hangs still fails against vitest's 5 s default. Standalone measurements taken first rather than picking a round multiple: canvas-viewport 24.8 s, app-shell.responsive 25.8 s, app.e2e 22.9 s, worker-pool.e2e 2.3 s, lazy-plotly-pane 13.0 s, lazy-katex-pane 0.8 s. 180 s is ~3.7x the slowest hook measurement on record (P4.38's 48.6 s) and 90 s is ~4x the slowest bundle-test one (22.1 s), against an observed suite-parallel inflation of ~2.4x. worker-pool.e2e and lazy-katex-pane were raised despite having no sighting and huge margin, because leaving two files of a six-file class on the old limits invites one more rediscovery.

VALIDATION, met as written -- "the full pnpm test suite passes repeatedly on a loaded container without any build-heavy test crossing a timeout, and no assertion was changed to achieve it". Four full-suite runs on a DELIBERATELY loaded container (two of four cores busy-looping, suite duration 136-140 s against 100-103 s unloaded, so the load was real and measurable) plus three unloaded runs. ZERO build-heavy timeout failures in any of the seven: no 'Hook timed out', no canvas-viewport, app-shell.responsive, app.e2e, worker-pool.e2e or bundle-test failure. Unloaded runs were 2563/2563 across 254 files every time.

WHAT THE LOADED RUNS DID FAIL, and it is not this task: two of the four reddened on P0.96's wall-clock ASSERTION in packages/solverkit/src/chunked-integration.test.ts, and the other two passed. That is P0.96 doing exactly what it is filed for, it is a different failure mode (assertion, not timeout), and it needs a human decision -- see the reproduction recipe now recorded against P0.96. It was not weakened, silenced or worked around here.

tasks.title: 84 stale `claude/*` branches sit on the remote against CLAUDE.md's own rule not to leave them; 79 of them are not ancestors of `main`, so nobody can tell at a glance whether any hold unlanded work
tasks.validation: either the remote holds no `claude/*` branch older than the current run, or each surviving one is listed with the reason it survives -- and no branch is deleted without first showing its work is on `main`
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-18 (37th run), MEASURED NOT INFERRED, while confirming this run left no branch behind. `git ls-remote --heads origin 'claude/*'` returns 84 refs. Only 5 are ancestors of `origin/main`; the other 79 are not, and `git rev-list --count origin/main..<branch>` runs from 9 to 392. CLAUDE.md says: 'Don't leave long-lived claude/* branches around after a task finishes ... merge it into main and delete it yourself once done rather than leaving it for someone else to close out.' THE COUNT IS ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT LOST WORK, and this filing does not claim it is. Spot-checked four of the largest: `nice-keller-vp78r0` (ahead 392, tip 2026-08-15) ends at 'P0.97: mark done; file P0.98', `keen-bohr-fkdyhu` and `upbeat-ride-uhifsa` (ahead 352, tip 2026-08-11) both at 'P5.16: file P0.93', `clever-pasteur-gox9dy` (ahead 146, tip 2026-07-27) at 'P4.13 PchipTerrain'. tasks.title: Three library scenarios cost 10-100x the inverse-solve median and set the whole pooled tail
tasks.validation: the cost of frozen-ou-gust, dust-grain and density-altitude-2000m is attributed to a named cause (step count, rhs cost, or stiffness) with a measurement per target, and either reduced or documented as irreducible
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-22 (41st run) by P5.30, which measured it rather than guessed it. P5.30's budget is MET and this is not a regression -- it is a shape worth naming before someone reads the p99 as a latency tail. THE NUMBERS, warm p50 per target at rtol 1e-12: frozen-ou-gust 143.25 ms, dust-grain 105.09 ms, density-altitude-2000m 89.14 ms, against a pooled p50 of 9.66 ms and a cheapest target of 0.04 ms. That is a 3600x spread across the library. THE CONSEQUENCE: those three are 3 of 20 targets, so 15% of pooled samples are theirs and EVERYTHING ABOVE POOLED p95 IS ONE OF THEM. The recorded p99 of 147.48 ms is therefore frozen-ou-gust's own median, not a rare slow event -- p99 over this pool is a target-mix statistic and moves if the library gains or loses a slow scenario, which is worth knowing before anyone treats it as a latency SLO. Iteration counts do NOT explain it: all three converge in 3-5 Newton iterations, the same as the fast targets, so the cost is per-iteration integration work rather than a harder solve. Suspects, in the order worth measuring: step count (a stochastic OU gust field and a drag-crisis-adjacent dust grain both plausibly force tiny steps), rhs evaluation cost, and genuine stiffness. Start by recording nSteps per solve -- the harness already builds every problem, so this is an instrumentation change, not a new harness. If irreducible, say so in the artifact's provenance so the next reader does not re-derive it.

tasks.title: `pnpm test` is red on a fresh clone: cross-engine-drift-record.test.ts needs packages/engine/dist, which only `pnpm typecheck` emits
tasks.validation: `pnpm test` passes from a clean checkout with no prior build step, or the dependency is declared somewhere a reader will find it before hitting the failure
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-23 (45th run), hit while establishing that run's baseline. NOT A NEW OBSERVATION, and that is the argument for filing it: the 38th run already recorded it, in a commit message -- "pnpm test on a fresh clone fails 4 tests with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on packages/engine/dist/index.js ... Run typecheck first, or pnpm verify. Not a bug -- CI's ordering is already correct." A note in one commit message among 247 is not somewhere a future session will look, which is why the 45th run rediscovered it seven runs later at the cost of a 103 s suite run. The counts differ (4 tests then, 3 now) but the mechanism is identical. `pnpm install && pnpm test` on a fresh clone fails 3 assertions in packages/validation/src/cross-engine-drift-record.test.ts. The chain: the test shells out to scripts/cross-engine-drift-fixture.mjs, which imports packages/engine/dist/index.js, which does not exist until something emits it. `pnpm typecheck` is what emits it -- `tsc -b` over composite projects writes dist as a side effect -- and ci.yml happens to run Typecheck before Test, so CI never sees this and neither does anyone who ran the full gate in order. The failure is also actively misleading: it surfaces as "expected 'No engine could be measured' ... received ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND", which reads like the drift measurement is broken rather than like a missing build. Options, none of them chosen here: have the test build what it needs; have it skip with an explicit message when dist is absent; or declare the ordering in the test file and README so the next person reads it before losing time to it. NOT a regression and not urgent -- the gate run in CI order is green -- but it is an undeclared edge in the task graph and it cost this run one full 103 s suite run to diagnose.
